# Data and network

> What Skribly Agent stores and where, every connection it makes, the folders it reads and writes, the local ports it opens, the No network calls switch and what an uninstall leaves.

Skribly Agent works on your computer and needs no account. It sends no telemetry, no crash reports and no identifiers, and it has no server of its own. **Settings → Privacy and network** lists every place where the app itself talks to the network, every folder outside its own data folder that it reads or writes, and every local port it opens, each with what, when and why. The list is data, and a test fails when the code has a call, a folder or a port that it does not name.

![Settings, Privacy and network: the switch No network calls by the app, off, and the list of what the switch does not cover](/_astro/agent-privacy.CR3YT9sx_Z1YaMiB.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Open **Settings** and choose **Privacy and network**, or
* switch **No network calls by the app** from the tray or menu bar menu, which stays in step with Settings.

## How to turn the network off

[Section titled “How to turn the network off”](#how-to-turn-the-network-off)

1. Open **Settings → Privacy and network**.

2. Switch on **No network calls by the app**.

3. Every call listed below now ends with a calm “switched off” message before anything is sent. Addresses on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` stay open, because they never leave the computer.

| Option                          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **No network calls by the app** | Stops all calls of the app itself before anything is sent. Also covers redirects: a request to a local address follows only local redirects, at most five. The hidden audit window cancels every request that is not local. | Off     |

## What the switch does not cover

[Section titled “What the switch does not cover”](#what-the-switch-does-not-cover)

* **Agents in panes.** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and the others are programs you run. They have their own connections, tokens and settings.
* **Agents started in the background.** The commit suggestion, pipelines and tasks started from MCP tools start the same agents without a pane. Their traffic is the agent’s.
* **MCP servers and `npx`.** The `claude mcp` and `npx` commands started from the MCP configuration make their own traffic.
* **Terminals and SSH.** The shell, commands and SSH connections in panes work as in an ordinary terminal.
* **The Browser view.** Pages you open are loaded by the browser itself. Text that is not an address goes to the DuckDuckGo search engine.
* **Links.** A link opens in the system browser only after you click it.

## Connections of the app

[Section titled “Connections of the app”](#connections-of-the-app)

Every call goes through one small module of the app, and the test checks that no other call exists.

| Connection                 | To                                                                                                      | When                                                                                                                              | Sends a token             |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| App updates                | The public release home of Skribly Agent on GitHub and the file server it redirects to                  | 8 seconds after start and every 4 hours while **Update automatically** is on, and when you press **Check for updates**            | No                        |
| Interface translation      | `translate.googleapis.com` and `api.mymemory.translated.net`                                            | Only for an interface language that is neither Polish nor English and is not in the cache yet; see [Languages](/agent/languages/) | No                        |
| Themes from Open VSX       | `open-vsx.org`                                                                                          | When you search the theme catalogue or install a theme                                                                            | No                        |
| Editor extension           | Your editor’s marketplace, through the editor’s own command                                             | Only when you install an extension in the editor                                                                                  | No                        |
| Task trackers              | The address of each tracker you added                                                                   | When you open tasks, pick a task, comment, change a status, log time or test the connection                                       | Yes, only to that tracker |
| Git accounts and activity  | `api.github.com`, `gitlab.com`, `codeberg.org`, `bitbucket.org`, `dev.azure.com` or your own Git server | When you connect an account, open the repository list or the activity card                                                        | Yes, only to that server  |
| Cloning a repository       | The server of the repository                                                                            | Only when you clone; a token of a connected account is used only for that clone                                                   | Yes, only to that server  |
| Push and pull              | The server the project’s origin points to                                                               | Only when you press push or pull; git uses its own keys or credential manager                                                     | No                        |
| Skills repository          | `github.com/skribly/agent-skills` or the address from Settings                                          | When you download or sync the skills repository                                                                                   | No                        |
| Pull requests through `gh` | `github.com`, through the GitHub CLI                                                                    | When you open the changes of a project whose origin is on GitHub and when you create a pull request                               | No                        |
| `gh` and `glab` login      | GitHub or the GitLab server you choose                                                                  | When you open the window that connects a Git account                                                                              | No                        |
| Claude Code plugins        | The Claude Code plugin marketplace, through `claude`                                                    | When you open the plugins list and when you install one                                                                           | No                        |
| MCP server test            | The address of the MCP server you test                                                                  | Only when you press the test on a server with an address; a local address also works with the network off                         | Yes, only to that server  |
| Docker images              | The registries named in the compose file, through Docker                                                | Only when you start a compose project or pull its images                                                                          | No                        |
| Page audit (WCAG and SEO)  | The address you give                                                                                    | Only when you run a page audit                                                                                                    | No                        |
| Dependency audit           | `api.osv.dev`: package names and versions from lock files, never code                                   | Only when you run the security audit of a project with lock files                                                                 | No                        |
| Tool installation          | Whatever the shown command contains (`brew`, `winget`, `npm`, `curl`)                                   | Only when you press install or log in for an agent or tool                                                                        | No                        |

## Folders outside the data directory

[Section titled “Folders outside the data directory”](#folders-outside-the-data-directory)

| What                              | Where                                                                                                                                                                                         | Access                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent sessions                    | `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.codex/sessions`, `~/.copilot/session-state`, or the folders named by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `COPILOT_HOME`                                              | Read only: token counts, session history and resume. For the history only the start of each file is read                         |
| Agent configuration               | `~/.claude.json`, `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.claude/plugins`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `~/.gemini/settings.json`, and `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.gemini` in the project | Read; written only after you confirm an MCP change, and a copy of the file is made first when you copy an entry to another agent |
| Agent commands and skills         | `.claude/commands`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/prompts`, `~/.cursor/commands`, `~/.gemini/commands`, `~/.config/opencode/command`                      | Read only                                                                                                                        |
| Project folders                   | The projects you added and the folder you chose for cloning                                                                                                                                   | Read; written only by what you do: edits, stage, commit, branch changes, clones, `.skribly`, `.cursor/rules` and skills          |
| Worktree folders                  | `~/.skribly/worktrees` or the folder from Settings                                                                                                                                            | Read and write                                                                                                                   |
| Local API file                    | `~/.skribly/control.json`                                                                                                                                                                     | Written at every start while the local API is on; readable by you only                                                           |
| `skribly` command                 | `~/.local/bin/skribly` or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Skribly\bin`                                                                                                                                        | Written only when you install the command                                                                                        |
| Editor extensions                 | `~/.vscode/extensions`, `~/.cursor/extensions`, `~/.windsurf/extensions`, `~/.vscode-oss/extensions`                                                                                          | Read only: theme JSON files, no extension code is run                                                                            |
| Code folders for activity         | `~/Developer`, `~/Projects`, `~/code` and folders you add                                                                                                                                     | Read only: commit history                                                                                                        |
| Downloads from Claude Design      | `~/Downloads/Skribly Design`                                                                                                                                                                  | Written when you download a file in that tab                                                                                     |
| Update package                    | The system’s temporary folder (`skribly-update-…`)                                                                                                                                            | Written while updating on macOS                                                                                                  |
| Tool locations                    | `PATH`, `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.claude/local`, Docker paths                                                                                                | Read only: checks that programs exist and asks for their version                                                                 |
| Other tools’ files                | Herdr and the agents’ folders                                                                                                                                                                 | Read only, only when you open **Import and export** and press preview                                                            |
| Export archive and import backups | The archive you choose and the backups folder in the data directory                                                                                                                           | Read and write, only after you export or import                                                                                  |
| Pane start folder                 | The project folder, or your home folder                                                                                                                                                       | Only where a pane starts; what the program does there is up to it                                                                |
| Processes of the panes            | The system process list and memory counters                                                                                                                                                   | Read only, every 3 seconds, only while the **Resources** view is open and the window is visible                                  |

## Ports

[Section titled “Ports”](#ports)

| Port                     | Default                                | Bound to    | Who can reach it                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chrome DevTools Protocol | Off; `9333` when browser sharing is on | `127.0.0.1` | Any program on this computer, without authentication. It sees all tabs, including signed-in profiles. It opens at the next start of the app |
| Local control API        | On, random free port                   | `127.0.0.1` | Processes that read the token from `~/.skribly/control.json`                                                                                |

Caution

Turn on browser sharing only while you work with agents, and turn off the local control API in **Settings → Sessions & control** if you do not use the `skribly` command or the MCP server. See [Browser](/agent/browser/).

## What the app stores

[Section titled “What the app stores”](#what-the-app-stores)

The data directory holds settings, projects, layout, sessions, encrypted tokens, the skills repository, downloaded themes, backups, the Browser’s profiles and the `skribly` shims of the panes. **Settings → Updates → Data directory** shows where it is; see [Settings](/agent/settings/#data-directory).

| Data                                     | Where                                           | Protection                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tracker and Git tokens                   | `secrets.json` in the data directory            | Encrypted with the system password store; see below              |
| Tracker accounts                         | `trackers.json`                                 | Plain JSON, no keys                                              |
| Settings, projects, layout and pipelines | JSON files in the data directory                | Plain JSON                                                       |
| Disabled MCP servers                     | `mcp-stash.json`                                | Plain JSON, and it can hold keys from the server’s configuration |
| Sign-ins in browser tabs                 | Separate browser profiles in the data directory | Browser cookies                                                  |
| Task content                             | `.skribly/tasks/` in the project                | Excluded from git                                                |
| Control API token                        | `~/.skribly/control.json`                       | Readable only by you; random, new on every start                 |

## Tokens and the keychain

[Section titled “Tokens and the keychain”](#tokens-and-the-keychain)

Tokens are encrypted through the system password store: the Keychain on macOS, the Windows data protection API, and the keyring on Linux (GNOME Keyring or KWallet). Tokens saved by earlier versions still open, and a token is encrypted again when the system rotates its key.

* When the store is unavailable or refuses a call, for example a locked keyring, a new token is kept in memory until the app closes and is offered to the store again on its next use. It is never written to disk as plain text.
* On Linux without GNOME Keyring or KWallet, tokens are only obfuscated. The first save shows one warning that says so and how to install a keyring.
* Agent sessions the app starts receive tracker tokens as environment variables, so skills can fetch tasks. An agent can read them, like any program in your terminal.
* Export and import archives never contain tokens, passwords, API keys or MCP environment values.

## What an uninstall leaves

[Section titled “What an uninstall leaves”](#what-an-uninstall-leaves)

Your data stays on purpose, and so do the files that belong to your projects and agents.

| System                            | Removed with the app                                                                                                                      | Stays                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| macOS (drag the app to the Trash) | The app and its link handlers                                                                                                             | `~/Library/Application Support/Skribly Agent`, the preferences file, caches, the Keychain item `Skribly Agent Safe Storage`, `~/.local/bin/skribly` (it fails until removed), `~/.skribly` |
| Windows (Settings → Apps)         | Program files, shortcuts, the update cache in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\skribly-agent-updater`, the `skribly` command and the `skribly://` handlers | `%APPDATA%\Skribly Agent` and `~/.skribly`                                                                                                                                                 |
| Linux `.deb` and `.rpm`           | `/opt/Skribly Agent`, the `/usr/bin/skribly-agent` link, the desktop file and icons, the AppArmor profile on Ubuntu 24.04 and later       | `~/.config/Skribly Agent`, `~/.cache/skribly-agent-updater`, the keyring item, `~/.local/bin/skribly`, `~/.skribly`                                                                        |
| Linux AppImage, Windows portable  | Delete the file                                                                                                                           | The same data and `~/.skribly`                                                                                                                                                             |

Check `~/.skribly/worktrees` for uncommitted work before you delete `~/.skribly`. To remove everything, delete the data directory, `~/.skribly`, the `skribly` command and the keychain or keyring item.

## How the app protects you

[Section titled “How the app protects you”](#how-the-app-protects-you)

* The window runs in Electron’s sandbox with no access to Node.js, calls only a fixed list of methods, shows only its own page and denies every permission request except clipboard writes and full screen.
* Preview and agent tabs run sandboxed, without access to the app, and cannot start on a `file:` address.
* Commands run without a shell, with a time limit and an output limit. The exception is `.cmd` and `.bat` files on Windows.
* Reading, writing, discarding and searching reject paths outside the project directory. Extracting packages rejects paths that escape the target directory.
* Themes are read as JSON, and extension code never runs.

Note

Agent terminals run with your permissions. An agent in a terminal can do whatever you can do in a terminal.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

* To report a security problem, see [Security](/security/).
* Switch the network off when you work offline: updates, translation and trackers then report that they are switched off instead of failing.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Every section of Settings and its defaults.

[Updates](/agent/updates/)How the app updates itself.

[Languages](/agent/languages/)The interface language and online translation.

[The skribly MCP server](/agent/skribly-mcp/)What agents can read and change through skribly mcp.

# Docker

> The Docker view of Skribly Agent lists containers by compose project, runs compose commands, shows logs, images and volumes, and alerts you to failures.

The **Docker** view shows the containers of the Docker engine on this computer, grouped by compose project, with the compose files of the open project on top. You start, restart and stop containers, read their logs, open a shell, and see images and volumes. A watcher in the background raises an alert when a container crashes, runs out of memory, fails its health check or restarts in a loop.

![The Docker view: the compose file of the project with Up, Restart, Pull and Down, and the containers of three compose projects with their state, ports and actions](/_astro/agent-docker.DVJXCDsu_ZRrOlh.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Docker** in the activity bar on the left, or press `⌘9`, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Docker**.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` in place of `⌘`.

If Docker is not found, the view says **Docker not found** and lists where it looked (the `docker` command in `PATH`, and the folders of Docker Desktop, OrbStack, colima and Rancher). If the engine is not running, it says **Docker is not running**, shows the command that starts it and checks again every few seconds.

## The tabs

[Section titled “The tabs”](#the-tabs)

| Tab            | What it shows                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Containers** | Every container, grouped by compose project, with the compose files of the open project above                                                  |
| **Images**     | Images with size and age. **Remove dangling** removes untagged images, **Remove unused** removes every image no container uses. Both ask first |
| **Volumes**    | Volumes with their driver and mount point                                                                                                      |
| **Alerts**     | The recent alerts, with the number in the tab. **Clear** empties the list. A click on an alert opens its container                             |

## How to run a compose project

[Section titled “How to run a compose project”](#how-to-run-a-compose-project)

When the open project has a compose file, a bar **Compose in project** lists each file and its compose project name.

1. Press **Up** to start the project (`docker compose up -d`).

2. Use **Restart** and **Pull** when you need them, and `ps` to list the project’s containers.

3. Press **Down** to stop and remove the project’s containers. It asks first. Volumes stay.

A group header in the container list has its own **Up**, **Restart**, **Stop** and **Down** for that compose project.

## How to work with a container

[Section titled “How to work with a container”](#how-to-work-with-a-container)

Each row shows the state, the health, the image, the ports and, after **Show CPU/RAM**, the processor and memory use. A port with a link opens in the [Browser](/agent/browser/). A container that crashed shows its exit code.

| Button                         | What it does                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Open shell (docker exec)**   | Opens a terminal with a shell inside a running container                                                                |
| **Logs**                       | Shows the last 100, 200, 500 or 2000 lines. **Follow in terminal** keeps following them                                 |
| **Pause** and **Resume**       | Pause and resume the container                                                                                          |
| **Restart**, **Stop**, **Run** | Control the container                                                                                                   |
| **Remove container**           | Removes it. Data outside volumes is lost. It asks first                                                                 |
| **Fix with agent**             | Shown for a container with a problem. It sends the logs and a summary of `inspect` to an agent and asks for a diagnosis |

Above the list a search field matches containers, images and projects, and the filter has **All**, **Running** and **Problems**, each with a count. **Show CPU/RAM** reads the use once, and the button then reads **Refresh CPU/RAM**.

The list reloads when the engine reports a change, and every 30 seconds while the view is open.

## Alerts and the status bar

[Section titled “Alerts and the status bar”](#alerts-and-the-status-bar)

The watcher listens to the events of Docker. It raises an alert in the app, and a system notification, for these four things:

| Alert                   | When                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Container crash**     | A container ended with a code other than 0, and not because you stopped it |
| **Out of memory (OOM)** | The kernel killed a process in a container that went over its memory limit |
| **Failed health check** | A container became unhealthy                                               |
| **Restart loop**        | At least 3 restarts within 2 minutes                                       |

The status bar at the bottom shows `Docker OK` when all containers are fine, or the number of containers with a problem, in red. A click opens this view. A click on a system notification opens the view on that container.

Since the watcher uses the `docker events` stream, it no longer runs `docker ps` every 15 seconds while the stream is alive, also while the window is hidden. The list reloads when the stream reports a change, and while the window is hidden only once you come back. The 15 second check is only a fallback while monitoring is on and the stream is down.

## Settings → Docker

[Section titled “Settings → Docker”](#settings--docker)

| Option                   | What it does                                                                                                                                                             | Default                    |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| **Container monitoring** | Runs the watcher. Off: Skribly does not run `docker events` or poll the engine in the background, and the Docker view still works                                        | On                         |
| Container crash          | Alert on this event                                                                                                                                                      | On                         |
| Out of memory (OOM)      | Alert on this event                                                                                                                                                      | On                         |
| Failed health check      | Alert on this event                                                                                                                                                      | On                         |
| Restart loop             | Alert on this event                                                                                                                                                      | On                         |
| **Context**              | The Docker context from `docker context ls` that Skribly talks to (Docker Desktop, OrbStack, colima or a remote server). It does not change the context of your terminal | The current Docker context |
| **DOCKER_HOST**          | The address of the engine: `unix://`, `tcp://`, `ssh://` or `npipe://`. It wins over the context                                                                         | Empty, the context is used |

The four alert switches are greyed out while monitoring is off. If system notifications are off in **Editor & notifications**, alerts appear only in the app. When more than one context exists, a picker for the context also sits in the view’s header.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Caution

**Remove unused** deletes every image that no container uses, and you will have to pull them again. **Down** removes containers but keeps volumes.

* Use **Fix with agent** first when a container crashes: the agent gets the logs and the `inspect` summary without you copying them.
* Point **DOCKER_HOST** at a remote engine only over `ssh://` or a network you trust.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Browser](/agent/browser/)Open a published port in the app's browser.

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)Where the agent from Fix with agent works.

[Resources](/agent/resources/)Memory, processor and ports of every pane.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)All the settings of Skribly Agent.

# Documents

> The Documents view of Skribly Agent shows a project's README, changelog, decision records and .docs folder as safe, read-only Markdown with search.

The **Documents** view shows the documentation a project keeps beside its code: the README, the changelog with its unreleased part first, the `.docs/` and `docs/` folders as a tree, and the decision records of an `adr` folder as a table. A file is shown as rendered Markdown, read only. You can search the titles and the text, open a file in the Code view, copy its path, or hand it to an agent to check against the code.

![The Documents view in the day theme: the tree of README, Changelog, decisions and .docs on the left and the rendered README with Open in the Code view, Copy path and Hand to an agent](/_astro/agent-documents.DoQ4O6Fv_ZlJ2cg.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Documents** in the activity bar on the left (the open book icon), or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Documents**.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` in place of `⌘`. The view has no number shortcut: `⌘1` to `⌘9` stay with the first nine views. Select a project first.

## What it lists

[Section titled “What it lists”](#what-it-lists)

| Entry               | Where it comes from                                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| README              | `README.md` (or `README`, `readme.md`) at the top of the project                                                            |
| Changelog           | `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGES.md` or `HISTORY.md` at the top. The `Unreleased` section is moved to the start, and a note says so |
| **Decisions (ADR)** | The Markdown files of a folder named `adr` under `.docs/` or `docs/`, or `adr/` and `doc/adr/` at the top                   |
| `.docs/`            | Every Markdown file of the folder, as a tree                                                                                |
| `docs/`             | The same for a `docs` folder                                                                                                |

Folders such as `node_modules`, `.git` and `build` are skipped, and a symbolic link is not followed. A very large set is cut at 800 files, and the view says so.

### Decision records

[Section titled “Decision records”](#decision-records)

**Decisions (ADR)** is a table with one row per record: number, title, status and date. They are read from the front matter at the top of the file:

```md
---
status: Accepted
date: 2026-03-14
---


# Keep the cart in zustand
```

Without front matter the number comes from the file name (`0007-…`, `ADR-12…`) or the title (`# 3. Use X`), the status from a `Status:` line or a `## Status` section, and the date from a `Date:` line. Choose a title to open the record.

## How to read a file

[Section titled “How to read a file”](#how-to-read-a-file)

1. Choose a file in the tree. In the tree `↑` and `↓` move, `→` opens a folder, `←` closes it and `Enter` or `Space` opens a file or a folder.

2. Read it. Headings, lists, task lists, tables, code blocks, quotes and links are rendered. Nothing can change: the boxes of a task list are shown, not ticked.

3. Follow a link. A link to another Markdown file of the project opens it in this view, also with a `#heading`. A link to another file of the project opens it in the Code view. A link inside the page scrolls to that heading.

The view renders Markdown without running anything:

* Raw HTML is shown as text. A `<script>`, an `onerror` attribute, an `<iframe>` or a `<style>` in a file never runs. HTML comments are left out.
* Only an `https:` address opens, and it opens in your system browser. Every other link (`http:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, `mailto:` or a path that leaves the project folder) is shown as dotted text that does nothing.
* Images load only from the project folder (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG, up to 5 MB). An image from the web is never requested, and its description is shown in brackets instead.
* A file that is not saved as UTF-8, or is larger than 2 MB, is not shown, and the view says why. Open it in the Code view instead.

## How to search

[Section titled “How to search”](#how-to-search)

1. Type in **Search the documents**. The view looks in the titles and paths first, then in the text of every listed file.

2. Read the results: up to three matching lines per file, with the line number.

3. Choose a result to open the file, or the button beside it to open the file at that line in the Code view. `↓` from the search goes to the first result. `Esc` clears the search.

## What the bar above a page does

[Section titled “What the bar above a page does”](#what-the-bar-above-a-page-does)

| Action                    | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Open in the Code view** | The file opens in the editor of the Code view                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Copy path**             | The path relative to the project goes to the clipboard                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Hand to an agent**      | A dialog shows a prompt that names the file and asks the agent to check it against the code. Edit it, choose a running session of the project or a new session of an installed agent, then press **Send** (`⌘↩`). Nothing is sent before you press it |

## When the view updates

[Section titled “When the view updates”](#when-the-view-updates)

The view reloads the list and the open file by itself when a listed file changes. It asks for the files’ sizes and modification times every few seconds, and only while the window is visible and focused. The refresh button next to the title reloads at once.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

Use **Hand to an agent** on a README or a how-to after a change of code. The agent compares the page with the code and lists what is out of date.

* Put decision records in `.docs/adr/` with a short front matter, and they show up in the table.
* A page that is too large is not shown here. Open it in the Code view.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Editor and files](/agent/code/)The Code view, where a document opens at a line.

[Plan](/agent/plan/)The Markdown checkboxes of the plan files.

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)The sessions a document can be handed to.

[Skills](/agent/skills/)Generate a .docs skeleton for a project.

# Extensions

> The Extensions tab of Skribly Agent keeps your own prompts, rules, skills, MCP servers and commands per agent or technology, all off until you switch them on.

The **Extensions** tab holds your own additions for an agent or for a technology: prompts, rules, skills, MCP servers and shell commands. Each one is a plain file. You choose who it is for, add it, and switch it on for a project. Nothing runs by itself, everything is off until you switch it on, and no secret is ever stored.

![The Extensions tab: buttons to add a prompt, rule, skill, MCP server or command, and one prompt, one rule and one team skill switched on with their token estimates](/_astro/agent-extensions.B-KsqHlv_SjoEE.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Plugins & MCP** in the activity bar on the left and choose the **Extensions** tab, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Plugins & MCP**.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` in place of `⌘`. The view has no number shortcut: `⌘1` to `⌘9` stay with the first nine views. Select a project in the top bar first: the switches, the detected technologies and the team’s additions belong to a project.

## Kinds of addition

[Section titled “Kinds of addition”](#kinds-of-addition)

| Kind       | What it is                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Prompt     | Reusable text                                            | **Send** types it into an agent pane. Choose the pane next to **Send to** at the top of the list                                                                                           |
| Rule       | Text for the agent’s instructions                        | Added to `TASK.md` when you start a task from the app, for the agent that starts it                                                                                                        |
| Skill      | A folder with a `SKILL.md`, chosen from disk             | Switching it on copies it into the project’s skills folder: `.claude/skills/<name>` for Claude Code, `.agents/skills/<name>` for the other agents. Switching it off removes only that copy |
| MCP server | A stdio command and arguments, or an http or sse address | **Write to the agent…** adds it to the configuration of the agents you tick, with the same code as [MCP servers](/agent/mcp/)                                                              |
| Command    | A shell command kept as text                             | **Run…** shows the whole command and, after your click, types it into a new terminal in the project                                                                                        |

Hooks are not part of this version.

Nothing an addition brings runs by itself. A prompt is sent only by your click. A command runs only after you confirm the exact text shown, and the app refuses to run it if the stored text changed since it was shown. An MCP entry is written only after a confirmation. Rules are text, not code. The one thing a switch does is copy a skill into a project.

## For whom an addition is

[Section titled “For whom an addition is”](#for-whom-an-addition-is)

The list **Show for** picks what you look at, and a new addition is made for it.

| Scope                               | Meaning                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **All agents** and **All projects** | Applies to every agent and every project. It shows under every other scope too, marked **from a broader scope** |
| An agent                            | One agent the app knows, such as Claude Code or Codex                                                           |
| A technology                        | A technology found in the open project, or one an addition already names                                        |

The app finds technologies by reading files at the root of the open project, such as `package.json`, `composer.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `Gemfile`, `pom.xml` and `Dockerfile`. It never runs anything. The tab lists each technology with the file and entry that proved it, for example `package.json: react`.

## How to add an addition

[Section titled “How to add an addition”](#how-to-add-an-addition)

1. Choose the scope in **Show for**.

2. Press the button of the kind under **Add**: **Prompt**, **Rule**, **Skill**, **MCP server** or **Command**.

3. Fill in **Name**, an optional description and the content. For a skill press **Choose the skill folder**. For an MCP server choose stdio or a remote address, then the command and arguments or the address.

4. Under **Where to store it** choose **Mine** (the app’s data folder) or **Team** (`.skribly/extensions` in the repository). **Team** is greyed out when the folder is read-only or no project is selected.

5. Tick the box that switches it on for the open project if you want that, and save.

A text is at most 20,000 characters and a command at most 2,000. A skill folder holds at most 200 files, 512 KB each and 2 MB in all. Links are skipped, and `.git` and `node_modules` are not copied.

## Your folder and the team’s

[Section titled “Your folder and the team’s”](#your-folder-and-the-teams)

| Where | Path                                                                         | Notes                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Yours | `extensions/` in the app’s data folder, with `index.json` and `skills/<id>/` | The data folder is shown in **Settings**                                                                                           |
| Team  | `.skribly/extensions/` in the project, with `index.json` and `skills/<id>/`  | Shown with a team badge. When the folder cannot be written, the addition is read-only: you can switch it on, not edit or remove it |

To share an addition with the team, save it with **Team**, then commit `.skribly/extensions/`. If the repository ignores `.skribly/`, use `git add -f .skribly/extensions`.

The switches are kept on your side, in your own `index.json`, never in the repository. So a repository you clone cannot hand instructions to an agent by itself.

## Switched off until switched on

[Section titled “Switched off until switched on”](#switched-off-until-switched-on)

Press the switch of an addition to turn it on for the project. The switch is bound to the content you turned on: a SHA-256 of the kind, scope, name, description, text and MCP entry, and for a skill the path and hash of every file.

If that content changes in any way other than an edit in the app, for example a `git pull` or a hand edit of `index.json`, the addition counts as off everywhere. Its rules are not added to `TASK.md`, its command does not run and its MCP entry is not written. The tab marks it **changed since you switched it on**. Read it and switch it on again.

* An edit you save in the app keeps the switch.
* A skill already copied into a project keeps the copy you approved. The tab says the stored skill is newer, and switching it on again replaces the copy.

## Token estimate

[Section titled “Token estimate”](#token-estimate)

Each rule, prompt and skill shows roughly how many tokens it adds: the characters of the text (for a skill, of `SKILL.md`) divided by four, rounded up. MCP servers and commands show none. With a project selected, a line above the list sums the switched-on rules and skills, because those go into every task. Prompts are not counted, as you send them only when you want.

## Check an addition

[Section titled “Check an addition”](#check-an-addition)

The shield button on an addition runs a check and changes nothing. It repeats the checks of saving: name, description, scope, limits, the refusal of secrets and a well formed command or http(s) address for an MCP server. For a skill it also checks that `SKILL.md` exists with a name and a description, and the file limits and the secret check on the stored files. It never starts an MCP server and never runs a command.

## Never a secret

[Section titled “Never a secret”](#never-a-secret)

An MCP entry never holds a token. It names the environment variable the server reads:

* for a stdio server, **Environment variables the server reads (names only)** is a list of names. Each is written as `${NAME}` and the agent expands it when it starts the server (Cursor gets `${env:NAME}`, Codex gets `env_vars`);
* for a remote server, **Environment variable that holds the Bearer token (name only)** is one name, written as `Authorization: Bearer ${NAME}` (Codex gets `bearer_token_env_var`).

Text, an MCP entry or a skill file that looks like it holds a key, a token or a password is refused, and the error does not repeat the value. A flag and its secret value as two arguments (`--api-key abc…`) is refused too. A reference such as `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is fine.

When you write an MCP server to an agent, a confirmation shows the agents and the scope. The entry has no auto-approve setting, so the agent asks before using a tool as always. The default scope is the open project, and **Everywhere (user configuration)** is a separate choice. Codex reads only the user configuration, so for it the entry always goes there.

## Import and export

[Section titled “Import and export”](#import-and-export)

* **Export** (top right, or the download button on one addition) writes one JSON file. It holds the text, the MCP entries and the files of each skill. It never holds your per-project switches.
* **Import** reads such a file and first shows what it will add: name, kind, scope, and which ones exist already (they are skipped). Nothing is added until you confirm. Imported additions go to your own additions, all switched off.

A file with a secret anywhere, with a skill path that leaves its folder, or in another format is refused whole. A file can be up to 10 MB.

## What the store refuses

[Section titled “What the store refuses”](#what-the-store-refuses)

The team folder comes from the repository, so other people write it. The store treats every byte of it as untrusted, and checks your own folder the same way.

* An index entry whose id is not one the store makes (`u-` for yours or `t-` for the team’s, then up to 32 letters and digits), or that would not pass the checks of a new addition, is ignored. Ignored entries stay in the file, unused, and the tab says how many there are.
* A symbolic link on the way to the store or inside a skill is refused, in the project’s `.claude` and `.agents` folders too. A team folder with a link in it is treated as absent.
* A team skill whose files break the limits or look like they hold a secret is refused when it is switched on and when it is exported.
* An `index.json` that cannot be read, for example with a git conflict left in it, is never overwritten. The team folder with such an index is skipped and read-only, and saving into your own index is refused until you fix the file.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Caution

Read a team addition before you switch it on. A rule goes into the instructions of every task, and a command runs in your terminal.

* Keep a rule short: it is added to every task for that agent.
* Put what only one technology needs under that technology, so other projects do not carry it.

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

# Frequently asked questions

> Short answers about Skribly Agent - systems, accounts, data, agents, worktrees, trackers, cost, languages, updates and accessibility - each with a link to the page that explains it.

Short answers, each with the page that explains the topic. If you do not find your question, try [Troubleshooting](/agent/troubleshooting/) or [All features at a glance](/agent/features/).

## The app

[Section titled “The app”](#the-app)

### What is Skribly Agent?

[Section titled “What is Skribly Agent?”](#what-is-skribly-agent)

A desktop app that runs coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent and Gemini side by side in terminal panes, with your tracker tasks, git, pipelines, skills and audits in the same window. See [Overview](/agent/) and [All features at a glance](/agent/features/).

### Which systems does it run on?

[Section titled “Which systems does it run on?”](#which-systems-does-it-run-on)

macOS, Windows and Linux. The download page offers installers for each. See [Install](/agent/install/).

### Why does my system warn me when I open it?

[Section titled “Why does my system warn me when I open it?”](#why-does-my-system-warn-me-when-i-open-it)

The builds are not signed or notarised yet, so macOS and Windows show a warning the first time. [Install](/agent/install/) shows how to open the app on each system.

### Does it need an account?

[Section titled “Does it need an account?”](#does-it-need-an-account)

No. The app works on your computer, has no server of its own and sends no telemetry. See [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/).

## Agents

[Section titled “Agents”](#agents)

### Which agents does it run?

[Section titled “Which agents does it run?”](#which-agents-does-it-run)

Thirteen: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Aider, Amp, Droid, Qwen Code, Goose, Crush and Kimi CLI, and any command-line tool you add as a custom agent. See [Supported agents](/agent/agents/).

### Does it include the agents?

[Section titled “Does it include the agents?”](#does-it-include-the-agents)

No. Skribly starts the agents installed on your computer, finds them in your `PATH` and can offer their install commands. Signing in and the terms of use stay with each agent’s provider.

### Can several agents work on one repository at once?

[Section titled “Can several agents work on one repository at once?”](#can-several-agents-work-on-one-repository-at-once)

Yes. Give each its own worktree, a separate folder with its own branch, so they do not overwrite each other’s files. See [Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/) and [The skribly command](/agent/cli/#parallel-worktrees).

### Can an agent start another agent?

[Section titled “Can an agent start another agent?”](#can-an-agent-start-another-agent)

Yes, through [the `skribly` command](/agent/cli/) or [the Skribly MCP server](/agent/skribly-mcp/). The MCP server is read-only by default, and every change it can make asks you in the app first.

### Will an agent run dangerous commands without asking?

[Section titled “Will an agent run dangerous commands without asking?”](#will-an-agent-run-dangerous-commands-without-asking)

That depends on the agent’s own permission settings. The optional [command guard](/agent/settings/#command-guard) makes Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode ask before the dangerous ones. It is off by default and is a safety net, not a sandbox.

## Your data

[Section titled “Your data”](#your-data)

### Does my code leave my computer?

[Section titled “Does my code leave my computer?”](#does-my-code-leave-my-computer)

Skribly itself does not upload it. The agents you run talk to their providers as they always do. The list of every connection the app makes is in **Settings → Privacy and network**. See [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/).

### Can I turn the network off?

[Section titled “Can I turn the network off?”](#can-i-turn-the-network-off)

Yes. **Settings → Privacy and network → No network calls by the app** stops every connection the app itself makes, including update checks. See [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/#how-to-turn-the-network-off).

### Where are my settings and tokens?

[Section titled “Where are my settings and tokens?”](#where-are-my-settings-and-tokens)

Settings are in the data directory, which **Settings → Updates → Data directory → Show** opens. Tracker tokens are encrypted with the system keychain. See [Settings](/agent/settings/#data-directory).

### How do I move to another computer?

[Section titled “How do I move to another computer?”](#how-do-i-move-to-another-computer)

Export your data and import it there. See [Import and export](/agent/import-export/).

## Tasks, cost and quality

[Section titled “Tasks, cost and quality”](#tasks-cost-and-quality)

### Which trackers can I connect?

[Section titled “Which trackers can I connect?”](#which-trackers-can-i-connect)

Skribly Tracker, Jira Cloud and Server, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab and Linear. See [Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/).

### Is the cost the same as my bill?

[Section titled “Is the cost the same as my bill?”](#is-the-cost-the-same-as-my-bill)

No, it is an estimate worked out on your computer from the session files of the agents and a dated price table. A subscription is shown as an API equivalent. Some things that change a bill are not visible in the files. See [Settings → Cost](/agent/settings/#cost).

### Does a budget stop an agent?

[Section titled “Does a budget stop an agent?”](#does-a-budget-stop-an-agent)

No. A budget draws a bar and can send a notification at 80% and at 100%. Nothing is blocked.

### Which audits are there?

[Section titled “Which audits are there?”](#which-audits-are-there)

Three: **Security**, **Accessibility (WCAG)** and **SEO**, run from the Audits view. See [Audits](/agent/audits/).

## Interface

[Section titled “Interface”](#interface)

### Can I use it in Polish?

[Section titled “Can I use it in Polish?”](#can-i-use-it-in-polish)

Yes. Polish and English are built in, and **Follow the system** picks one of them. Other languages are translated from the internet and saved for offline use. See [Languages](/agent/languages/).

### Is it accessible?

[Section titled “Is it accessible?”](#is-it-accessible)

Skribly Agent is built to WCAG 2.2 AA as a target. It has a high-contrast theme, text size, reduced motion, underlined links and a strong focus indicator. See [Accessibility](/agent/accessibility/).

### How do I update it?

[Section titled “How do I update it?”](#how-do-i-update-it)

Updates download in the background and install when you quit the app. **Settings → Updates** checks on demand. See [Updates](/agent/updates/).

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Troubleshooting](/agent/troubleshooting/)Fixes for the common problems.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Every option and its default.

[Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/)Pane, app and editor keys.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What is stored and which connections are made.

# All features at a glance

> One short paragraph for every view and area of Skribly Agent, each with a link to the page that explains it.

Skribly Agent has one view per job, reachable from the activity bar, with `⌘1` to `⌘9` (`Ctrl` on Windows and Linux) or from the command palette `⌘K`. This page names each area in a few lines; the linked page has the details.

## Dashboard

[Section titled “Dashboard”](#dashboard)

Agents at work, tasks assigned to you, your recent commits and token use in one page, with a Getting started list. See [Dashboard](/agent/dashboard/) and [First run](/agent/first-run/).

## Agents and sessions

[Section titled “Agents and sessions”](#agents-and-sessions)

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI and nine more run side by side in workspaces, tabs, splits and panes, each in a terminal or a chat. The app reads each agent’s state, tells you when one waits and resumes sessions after a restart. See [Workspaces](/agent/workspaces/), [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/), [Supported agents](/agent/agents/), [Terminals](/agent/terminals/), [Session history](/agent/session-history/) and the [attention inbox](/agent/inbox/).

## Code and changes

[Section titled “Code and changes”](#code-and-changes)

A Monaco editor, search, side-by-side diffs and a terminal; changes, commit messages that follow your history with no AI trailers, branches, push and pull requests, a history graph and review notes you send back to the agent. Worktrees keep agents apart. See [Editor and files](/agent/code/), [Changes and commits](/agent/changes/), [Review notes](/agent/review/), [History](/agent/history/) and [Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/).

## Tasks and trackers

[Section titled “Tasks and trackers”](#tasks-and-trackers)

Jira, Redmine, GitHub Issues, GitLab, Linear and Skribly Tracker in one list, plus local tasks. **Start with an agent** writes the task to `.skribly/tasks/<KEY>/TASK.md` and `STATE.md`, creates a branch or worktree and launches the agent with a ready prompt. Status, comments, assignment and time logging work without leaving the app where the tracker supports them. See [Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/).

## Plan

[Section titled “Plan”](#plan)

The Plan view counts the Markdown checkboxes of your plan files and hands an open item to the Code view or to an agent. See [Plan](/agent/plan/).

## Pipelines

[Section titled “Pipelines”](#pipelines)

A pipeline is several agents, from different vendors if you like, working toward one goal. Stages run in order and the steps of a stage run in parallel; each step is a headless agent that reads the latest part of a shared `handoff.md`, not the previous agent’s whole conversation. See [Pipelines](/agent/pipelines/).

![The Pipelines view: built-in pipelines and recent runs on the left, a running Plan, execution and review pipeline on a graph, and its steps on the right](/_astro/agent-pipelines.CvDBO-NR_Z1DjvJY.webp)

## Skills

[Section titled “Skills”](#skills)

Skills from [agent-skills](/skills/) installed with one click in each agent’s own format, adapted to the project, with a `.docs/` skeleton generated from the repository. See [Skills](/agent/skills/) and [Token saving](/agent/token-saving/).

## Audits

[Section titled “Audits”](#audits)

The **Audits** view checks a project and a running site for security, accessibility (WCAG) and SEO, gives each report a score from 0 to 100 and sends selected findings to an agent as a short task list. See [Audits](/agent/audits/) and [Audit rules](/agent/audit-rules/).

![A security audit with a score of 40 out of 100: eleven findings sorted by severity, the first a leaked GitHub token shown masked, with its fix on the right](/_astro/agent-audits.BDn5_xFa_btVBA.webp)

## Token use and resources

[Section titled “Token use and resources”](#token-use-and-resources)

A board of token use per agent, project and day, computed locally from the agents’ session files, and a view of the memory, processor and ports of every pane. See [Token use](/agent/usage/) and [Resources](/agent/resources/).

## Extensions, plugins and MCP

[Section titled “Extensions, plugins and MCP”](#extensions-plugins-and-mcp)

Prompts, rules, skills, MCP servers and commands you add per project or team; Claude Code plugins; the MCP servers of Claude, Codex, Cursor and Gemini switched on and off with one toggle; and a Claude Design to code bridge. See [Extensions](/agent/extensions/), [Plugins](/agent/plugins/) and [MCP servers](/agent/mcp/).

## Browser, Docker and documents

[Section titled “Browser, Docker and documents”](#browser-docker-and-documents)

A preview browser at phone, tablet and laptop sizes with DevTools and a screenshot for the agent, which you can share with agents over the Chrome DevTools Protocol; Docker containers, compose projects and alerts; and the README, changelog and `.docs` folder read safely. See [Browser](/agent/browser/), [Docker](/agent/docker/) and [Documents](/agent/documents/).

## Settings, themes and languages

[Section titled “Settings, themes and languages”](#settings-themes-and-languages)

Themes from your VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf extensions or from Open VSX, separate day and night themes, text size, accessibility settings, interface languages, and import and export of your setup. See [Settings](/agent/settings/), [Themes](/agent/themes/), [Accessibility](/agent/accessibility/), [Languages](/agent/languages/) and [Import and export](/agent/import-export/).

## CLI and MCP

[Section titled “CLI and MCP”](#cli-and-mcp)

Agents can drive other agents through the `skribly` command and the `skribly mcp` server, over a local control API on `127.0.0.1` with a random token. See [The skribly command](/agent/cli/) and [Skribly MCP](/agent/skribly-mcp/).

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Overview](/agent/)What Skribly Agent is and what it needs.

[Install](/agent/install/)Files for each system.

[Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/)The Ctrl+B prefix and every global shortcut.

# First run

> What Skribly Agent does on its first launch: the animated tour, the Getting started list on the Dashboard, the menu bar or tray icon and the single window.

On the first launch, about a second after the window opens, an animated tour starts. A cursor moves through the app, opens the views and says what each one is for. After the tour, the Dashboard keeps a **Getting started** list that follows your real setup. The app also puts an icon in the menu bar (macOS) or the system tray (Windows and Linux).

![The first-run tour pointing at the project switcher, with Pause and Next](/_astro/agent-tour.DIZ0kQaJ_Z1Lg6YP.webp)

## The tour

[Section titled “The tour”](#the-tour)

The tour has 18 steps. It goes on by itself about every 6 seconds, and it waits on its step while the window is hidden. Each step shows a card with the step number, a title, a short text and a progress bar. The card is a dialog: focus moves into it, `Tab` stays inside it and focus returns to where it was when you close it.

With reduced motion, set in the system or with the accessibility switch, the cursor is not drawn and the tour does not advance by itself: it waits for you to press **Next**.

| Key or button                   | What it does                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `→` or **Next**                 | Next step                                                                  |
| `←` or the previous-step button | Previous step                                                              |
| **Pause**                       | Stops the automatic advance; the button then reads **Auto** and resumes it |
| `Esc` or the close button       | Closes the tour                                                            |
| **Let’s get started**           | Closes the tour on the last step                                           |

Closing the tour in any way marks it as shown, so it does not start by itself again.

### How to replay the tour

[Section titled “How to replay the tour”](#how-to-replay-the-tour)

* Choose the **?** button at the top of the window, then **Start tour**, or
* open **Help** in the activity bar and press **Start tour**, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Start tour**, or
* choose **Settings → Appearance and tour** and press **Run now**, or
* press **Tour** on the **Getting started** card of the Dashboard.

### How to show the tour at the next launch

[Section titled “How to show the tour at the next launch”](#how-to-show-the-tour-at-the-next-launch)

1. Open **Settings → Appearance and tour**.

2. Press **Reset tour** next to **Show the tour on next launch**. The button works once the tour has been shown.

3. Restart the app. The tour starts again about a second after the window opens.

## The Getting started list

[Section titled “The Getting started list”](#the-getting-started-list)

The Dashboard shows a **Getting started** card with a progress bar and a count such as `5 of 8`. Each item is marked done from your real data, not by ticking, and has a button that takes you to the place.

| Item                                     | Done when                                                                                    | Button                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| **Add project**                          | The app has at least one project                                                             | **Add project**                                   |
| **Connect a task tracker**               | At least one tracker account is saved                                                        | **Connect** (opens **Settings → Task trackers**)  |
| **Detect agents**                        | At least one agent is installed                                                              | **Detect**, or **Detect again** when one is found |
| **Install skills**                       | The current project has a skill installed for an agent                                       | **Open Skills**                                   |
| **Run your first agent**                 | An agent session has been started                                                            | **Run**                                           |
| **Connect an agent through skribly mcp** | You pressed its button; it opens the section of **Settings** that holds the command to paste | **Show**                                          |
| **Check privacy and the network switch** | You pressed its button; it opens the privacy sheet                                           | **Show**                                          |
| **Try Ctrl+B**                           | You pressed the prefix in the Agents view                                                    | **Show**                                          |

The last three items are remembered, because the app cannot read it from data. The prefix is `Ctrl+B` on every system; press it, release it, then press `?` for the cheat sheet of pane shortcuts.

Press the cross to hide the card. When every item is done, the card says **All set — you can hide this card.** and offers **Hide**. To bring it back, choose **Settings → Appearance and tour** and press **Show again** next to **Getting started on the Dashboard**.

## The menu bar and tray icon

[Section titled “The menu bar and tray icon”](#the-menu-bar-and-tray-icon)

Clicking the icon brings up the window. Its menu lists, from the top:

| Part                                      | What it shows                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Agent counts                              | `Working`, `Waiting` and `Done` counts                                                                             |
| **Attention inbox**                       | Up to five of the newest items, each as `Waiting`, `Failed` or `Done` with the session name; choosing one opens it |
| **Open projects** and **Recent projects** | Up to five each; choosing one opens the project                                                                    |
| **Quiet notifications (no sound)**        | A switch that is the opposite of **Notification sound** in **Settings → Editor & notifications**                   |
| **No network calls by the app**           | A switch that mirrors the offline switch                                                                           |
| **Tokens used today**                     | Today’s token count, only when there is a number                                                                   |
| **Show Skribly**, **Settings**            | Bring up the window, open **Settings**                                                                             |
| **Check for updates**                     | Only on a system where the app can check                                                                           |
| **Quit**                                  | Quits the app                                                                                                      |

A part with nothing to show is left out. Long names are cut with an ellipsis. On macOS the number of items waiting for you is written next to the icon, and the icon’s tip names it on every system.

## One window

[Section titled “One window”](#one-window)

Only one instance of Skribly Agent runs. Starting it a second time brings the existing window forward; if you closed the window, a new one opens.

Tip

Shortcuts on this site use `⌘`. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` instead.
