# Your first session

> Start your first agent session in Skribly Agent step by step, learn the agent states, send a prompt, answer from the inbox and commit the result.

This page takes you from an installed agent to a first commit. You need a [project](/agent/first-workspace/) and an installed agent; if none is found, see [Install](/agent/install/#install-an-agent).

![The Agents view: the workspace sidebar with three projects and their worktrees, and a Claude Code pane that reviews a diff and lists accessibility issues](/_astro/agent-agents.C2sSCdmD_ZOVEKt.webp)

## How to start the session

[Section titled “How to start the session”](#how-to-start-the-session)

1. Open **Agents** (`⌘2`) and press **New session**. On the Dashboard, **Run agent** does the same with the first installed agent.

2. Pick the agent. A dimmed card is an agent that is not installed; **Terminal** is a plain shell.

3. Check the **Project**. In **Working copy**, choose **Main** (it carries the folder’s name) to work in the project folder, or **+ New worktree…** and give a branch to work in a separate copy, so the agent does not touch your files.

4. Leave **Mode** on **Terminal**. Write the **First message (optional)**, for example “Review the payment module and suggest tests”.

5. Press **Run**, or `Enter` in the message field.

The agent starts in a pane with its own login and keys. Skribly never asks for them.

## What the states mean

[Section titled “What the states mean”](#what-the-states-mean)

The pane header and the sidebar show a state, read from the agent’s screen.

| State                      | What to do                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **starting**               | Wait a moment                                               |
| **working**                | Nothing; the agent is busy                                  |
| **waiting for a decision** | The agent asks for approval or a choice. Answer in the pane |
| **done**                   | The agent finished its turn. Read the result                |
| **ready**                  | You saw the result; give it the next prompt                 |
| **finished**               | The process has exited                                      |

Press the state badge to see **Why this state?** when one looks wrong. More is on [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/#agent-states).

## How to send a prompt

[Section titled “How to send a prompt”](#how-to-send-a-prompt)

Click in the pane and type, as in the agent’s own terminal. The agent works and the state changes to **working**. To send the same text to several agents, tick the checkboxes in their headers and use the field on the tab bar, as described under [Broadcast](/agent/sessions/#broadcast).

## What happens when the agent waits

[Section titled “What happens when the agent waits”](#what-happens-when-the-agent-waits)

When an agent asks you something and you look at another pane or another view, the count on the **Agents** icon and the **Inbox** button goes up, and, if the window is in the background, a system notification appears. Open the [attention inbox](/agent/inbox/) with `⌘⇧U` or `Ctrl+B i`, press the row or its digit, and answer in the pane. A finished turn shows up there too, as **done**.

## How to commit the result

[Section titled “How to commit the result”](#how-to-commit-the-result)

1. Open **Code & git** (`⌘4`) and the changes of the project.

2. Review the diff and stage the files you want. [Review notes](/agent/review/) let you send comments back to the agent.

3. Press **Suggest**. The message follows the pattern of your repository’s history, and no AI trailers are added.

4. Press **Commit**.

The steps in detail are on [Changes and commits](/agent/changes/).

Tip

Shortcuts on this site use `⌘`. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` instead. The `Ctrl+B` prefix is the same on every system.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)States, the agent panel, chat mode and hand-off.

[Attention inbox](/agent/inbox/)The sessions that wait for you.

[Changes and commits](/agent/changes/)Stage, suggest a message and commit.

[Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/)Start a session from a tracker task.

# Your first workspace

> Add a project to Skribly Agent from a folder or a link, see what the app detects, connect a task tracker and switch between projects.

A project is a folder, usually a git repository. Agents, git, audits and skills work in the folder of the project you select at the top of the window. Add one before you start an agent.

![The Code & git view before a project is chosen: Select a project, with Add project and Clone from a link](/_astro/agent-no-project.Ds8vqHex_Z28Ogbe.webp)

## How to add a project

[Section titled “How to add a project”](#how-to-add-a-project)

1. Click the project switcher in the top bar and choose **Add project…**. The same action is in **Settings → Projects**, on the Dashboard and in the command palette (`⌘K`).

2. Pick the folder. The app adds it, selects it and detects the conventions of the repository.

3. Open **Settings → Projects**, press **Configure** on the project, check the values and press **Save**.

Adding a folder that is already a project selects the existing one. Removing a project from the list with **Remove from list** does not touch any file on disk; you can add it again at any time.

## How to clone a repository

[Section titled “How to clone a repository”](#how-to-clone-a-repository)

1. Choose **Clone from a link…** in the project switcher, in the palette (**Clone a repository from a link…**) or with **Clone from a link** in **Settings → Projects**.

2. Paste the **Repository link**: a browser link, an `https://` or `ssh://` address, `git@host:owner/name.git` or `owner/name` for GitHub. A link that points at a branch, such as `…/tree/develop`, fills the branch.

3. Press **Choose** next to **Destination folder**. The line below says which folder will be created, `<folder>/<name>`.

4. Fill **Branch (optional)** if you want a branch other than the default one.

5. Press **Clone and add project**. The dialog shows the progress and **Stop** ends it.

Private repositories use an account from **Settings → Git accounts**, your `gh` login or an SSH key. A link with a user name or password is refused: never put one in the link.

## What is detected

[Section titled “What is detected”](#what-is-detected)

Detection only suggests values. Press **Detect** in the project’s settings to run it again; your edits are never applied without **Save**.

| Setting                      | How it is detected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Base branch**              | The first existing of `develop`, `main`, `master`; otherwise the first local branch                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Checks (comma separated)** | `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` for the scripts the `package.json` has; `composer test` when there is a `composer.json`; `python manage.py test` when there is a `manage.py`; `pytest` when there is only a `pyproject.toml` |
| **Dev-mode app URL**         | The port after `--port` in the `dev` or `start` script; otherwise `5173` when the script uses Vite and `3000` for everything else; set only when a `package.json` exists                                                                            |
| **Branch pattern**           | `feature/{key}-{slug}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Commit template**          | Empty: the commit message follows the repository’s history                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Commit language**          | Automatic                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The same section lets you set the project’s name and colour, a **Project tracker** and the **Project / repository / team in the tracker**, so the task list of that project shows only its own tasks.

## How to connect a tracker

[Section titled “How to connect a tracker”](#how-to-connect-a-tracker)

1. Open **Settings → Task trackers** and press **Add tracker**.

2. Choose the tracker and enter the URL and the token.

3. Press **Save and check**. The app saves the account, encrypts the token and tests the connection.

URLs, token permissions and starting a task with an agent are on [Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/).

## How to switch projects

[Section titled “How to switch projects”](#how-to-switch-projects)

Click the project switcher in the top bar and choose a project from the list. The current one has a coloured dot and its name on the button. Agents, git, audits and skills now work in the new folder. Panes that already run stay where they are; the Agents view groups them by project, as described on [Workspaces](/agent/workspaces/).

Tip

Shortcuts on this site use `⌘`. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` instead.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Your first session](/agent/first-session/)Start an agent in the new project.

[Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/)Tasks from your tracker, started with an agent.

[Workspaces](/agent/workspaces/)Tabs, splits and the workspace sidebar.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Every section of Settings.

# History

> The History tab of Skribly Agent draws a graph of the last 300 commits of all branches, with branch and tag labels, and shows the details of a commit you click.

The **History** tab of the **Code & git** view draws the commits of the project as a graph. It covers all branches, local and remote, so you see where each branch started, where it was merged and which commit each branch and tag points at. It only reads: nothing in this tab changes the repository.

![The History tab: a graph of all branches with commit messages, branch and tag labels, authors, dates and short hashes](/_astro/agent-code-history.BDJGGWd-_Z1olyuV.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Open **Code & git** (`⌘4`) and choose the **History** tab, the last of the four icons in the left panel.
* The graph opens in the main area, as a tab named **History**, next to your files. The left panel keeps the details of the commit you selected.

If the project is not a git repository, the tab says so. If the repository has no commits yet, the graph shows **No history** and points you to the commit box of the **Changes** tab.

## How to read the graph

[Section titled “How to read the graph”](#how-to-read-the-graph)

Each row is one commit. From left to right it shows:

| Part            | What it means                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dots and lines  | One column (lane) per line of work. A branch runs down its lane until it ends or is merged. Lanes do not move, so lines stay straight. A filled dot is a commit; a hollow one is a merge (a commit with more than one parent) |
| Labels          | Branch names, remote branches such as `origin/main`, and tags. Remote branches and tags have their own colours; the current branch is shown by its name alone                                                                 |
| Message         | The subject of the commit                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Author and time | Who made it and how long ago                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Hash            | The first 7 characters of the commit hash                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Commits are in date order, newest first. The graph holds the last 300 commits of all branches, and it draws at most 12 lanes.

## How to see the details of a commit

[Section titled “How to see the details of a commit”](#how-to-see-the-details-of-a-commit)

1. Click a commit in the graph, or move to it with `Tab` and press `Enter` or `Space`.

2. Read the left panel: the subject, the first 12 characters of the hash, the author and the time, the branch and tag labels, and the parents of the commit (8 characters each).

Before you select a commit, the panel says to click one in the graph.

## How to find a branch or a tag

[Section titled “How to find a branch or a tag”](#how-to-find-a-branch-or-a-tag)

Look for its label in the graph: it sits on the row of the commit it points at. To switch to a branch, use the branch button of the **Changes** tab, described in [Changes and commits](/agent/changes/#how-to-switch-or-create-a-branch).

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

The view refreshes every 8 seconds while the window has focus, and the refresh button in the panel head reloads at once. A branch that an agent just made shows up without any action.

* Long histories are cut at 300 commits. For older commits use `git log` in the terminal at the bottom of the view.
* The branches of worktrees live in the same repository, so they appear in the graph as well.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Changes and commits](/agent/changes/)Stage, commit, switch branches and push.

[Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/)Every worktree and branch of your projects at a glance.

[Editor and files](/agent/code/)The same view as an editor.

# Import and export

> Settings, Import and export in Skribly Agent writes your data to one zip without secrets, previews an import before it changes anything and reads other tools read only.

**Settings**, section **Import and export**, does two things. It writes your own data into one archive you can take to another computer. And it reads what you already built in other tools, Herdr and the rules, commands, skills and MCP entries of your agents, and offers to bring it in. Every import shows a preview first. Nothing is changed until you tick it, and nothing leaves your computer.

![Settings, Import and export: an archive preview with projects, pipelines, extensions and app settings to tick, and Import from other tools with Herdr and agent files](/_astro/agent-import-export.Mm5NxbuQ_1FFDGW.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Settings** in the activity bar on the left and choose **Import and export**, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Settings**.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` in place of `⌘`. Everything on the page is a native checkbox, list or button: `Tab` moves, `Space` ticks and `Enter` presses.

## How to export your data

[Section titled “How to export your data”](#how-to-export-your-data)

1. Under **Export your data**, tick what goes into the archive. Each line shows how many items it holds.

2. Press **Export…** and choose where the `.zip` is saved.

3. Press **Show in folder** to find the file.

| Section                                                         | What is in it                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Projects and their settings**                                 | Name, folder, colour, pin and the settings of each project                                                          |
| **Pipelines with their layout**                                 | The pipelines you saved, with the layout of their steps. Nothing if you use only the built-in ones                  |
| **Extensions: rules, prompts, skills, MCP with their switches** | Your rules, prompts, skills, MCP entries and commands, with their scope and the project switches                    |
| **App settings**                                                | The settings of the app                                                                                             |
| **Task list**                                                   | The local tasks of your projects: `meta.json` and `STATE.md` of each folder in `.skribly/tasks`                     |
| **Usage numbers**                                               | The numbers of the activity heat map, a count per day. No commit messages, no e-mail addresses, no repository names |

What is never in an archive: tokens, passwords and API keys (tracker keys stay in the system keychain and are not read), the values of the environment variables of MCP entries (an entry keeps only the names), and anything from the agents’ own session logs. On top of that every string of every file is checked, and one that looks like a secret, or sits under a key named like one (`token`, `password`, `apiKey` and so on), is replaced by `••••••`.

### What is inside the archive

[Section titled “What is inside the archive”](#what-is-inside-the-archive)

An archive is a plain zip, deflate and no encryption, so you can open it and read it. It holds `manifest.json` and one JSON file for each section you ticked: `projects.json`, `pipelines.json`, `extensions.json`, `settings.json`, `tasks.json` and `usage.json`. The manifest names the format (`skribly-export`), its version, the app version, the date and the platform. An archive made by a newer version of the app is refused.

## How to import an archive

[Section titled “How to import an archive”](#how-to-import-an-archive)

1. Under **Import from an archive**, press **Choose an archive…** and pick the file.

2. Read the preview. It shows the app version and date of the archive, then each section line by line, with its status.

3. Tick what to take. New lines are ticked for you. For a line that is **different from yours**, tick it and choose what to do: **Keep mine** or **Take theirs (a backup of mine is kept)**.

4. Press **Import selected**. The result says how many items were imported and skipped, and names the backup.

| Status               | Meaning                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| new                  | Not on this computer. Ticked by default                                      |
| different from yours | Exists here and differs. Tick it and choose **Keep mine** or **Take theirs** |
| same                 | Already identical. Nothing to do                                             |
| skipped, information | Shown with the reason. It cannot be ticked                                   |

The import keeps these rules:

* Nothing is written until you press **Import selected**. A line that differs is replaced only when it is ticked and set to **Take theirs**.
* Everything that is replaced is first copied to `backups/import-<time>/` in the app’s data folder, one JSON file for each replaced item.
* Extensions come in switched off. The project switches in the archive are listed but never applied: an extension changes what an agent does, so you switch it on yourself. See [Extensions](/agent/extensions/).
* Some settings are never taken from an archive, because they start programs, open a port or point at another machine: `controlApi`, `customAgents`, `machines`, `shareBrowserWithAgents` and `cdpPort`.
* A task is written only into a project that is on this computer. Take the project first, then import again.
* The usage numbers stay in the archive as a record. The app counts them again from your repositories.
* A broken file skips only its own section. A file that is not an archive, or is damaged, too large or has a name that would leave the folder, is refused with a message.

## How to import from other tools

[Section titled “How to import from other tools”](#how-to-import-from-other-tools)

Under **Import from other tools** each source shows what was found. The app only reads the other tool’s files, only inside your home folder (a link that leads out of it is refused), and changes nothing in them. It sends nothing.

1. Press **Preview** next to a source. The button is greyed out when nothing was found.

2. Read the list. Each item names its **Source** file. Warnings are shown above it.

3. Tick the items to take and press **Import selected**. Only something the preview showed can be taken.

| Source                               | Read from                                                                                                               | Becomes                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Herdr (app)                          | `~/.local/state/herdr-core/*/docs.json` and `terminals.json`, `~/.config/herdr-core`, `~/.config/herdr-app/shared.json` | A project per space, a session layout per space and per template, a layout per agent in its launcher menu |
| Herdr (terminal)                     | `~/.config/herdr/session.json`                                                                                          | A project per workspace and a session layout from its tabs and pane labels                                |
| Agents: rules, commands, skills, MCP | See below                                                                                                               | [Extensions](/agent/extensions/) scoped to the agent, with the source file named                          |

The Herdr formats were learned from the files Herdr writes on a computer. No public format description was used, so a newer version is read as far as it is understood, and the preview says so.

A session layout keeps for each pane its tab, a title, the folder and the program (`claude`, `codex` and so on, or `shell`). Arguments are dropped, because they can hold a task text or a token. The layouts appear under **Imported session layouts**, where you can remove them. A folder outside your home folder is shown as skipped. Add it by hand in the project list.

### What is read from the agents

[Section titled “What is read from the agents”](#what-is-read-from-the-agents)

| Agent       | Rules                                | Commands (as prompts)             | Skills                        | MCP entries                                  |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`                | `~/.claude/commands/*.md`         | `~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` | `mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`             |
| Codex       | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`                 | `~/.codex/prompts/*.md`           | `~/.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md`  | `[mcp_servers.*]` in `~/.codex/config.toml`  |
| Cursor      | `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc` and `*.md`   | `~/.cursor/commands/*.md`         |                               | `mcpServers` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`         |
| Gemini CLI  | `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`                | `~/.gemini/commands/*.toml`       |                               | `mcpServers` in `~/.gemini/settings.json`    |
| OpenCode    | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`       | `~/.config/opencode/command/*.md` | `~/.config/opencode/skill/*`  | `mcp` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`  |
| Copilot     | `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` |                                   |                               | `mcpServers` in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` |

A file that is not there is skipped, so the list follows what is installed. Only your home folder is read.

Secrets are not imported:

* A rule, prompt or skill whose text looks like a secret is shown as `••••••` and marked skipped. It is never stored.
* An MCP entry keeps the names of its environment variables. The values are not read into the preview. A header is kept only as a `Bearer ${NAME}` reference, and any other header is dropped, which the preview says. A command or an address that carries a credential is skipped.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

Export before you reinstall or change computers. Then on the new one import the archive first, take the projects, and import again to take the tasks.

* If you take theirs for a line, a copy of yours stays in `backups/`, so you can go back.
* The privacy sheet lists reading other tools’ files, writing an archive and keeping a backup. See [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/).

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Extensions](/agent/extensions/)What imported rules, prompts, skills and MCP entries become.

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)Sessions and their panes.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What the app reads, writes and contacts.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)All the settings of Skribly Agent.

# Attention inbox

> The attention inbox of Skribly Agent lists the sessions that wait for you, with its keys, system notifications, quiet notifications and the tray menu items.

The attention inbox lists every agent session that needs you, newest first, so you do not have to look through your panes. Three things put a session in it: it is waiting for an answer, it ended with an error, or it is done and you have not looked at the result yet.

![The attention inbox, Waiting for you (3): a Codex session waiting for an answer, a Claude session that is done and a Cursor session that ended with an error](/_astro/agent-inbox.DzDTGiBS_Z1gK6TG.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Press **Inbox** in the tab bar of the Agents view, or
* press `Ctrl+B`, then `i`, or
* press `⌘⇧U` from any view, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Inbox: sessions waiting for you**.

Shortcuts on this site use `⌘`. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` instead; `⌘⇧U` is then `Ctrl+Shift+U`. The `Ctrl+B` prefix is the same on every system.

## What a row shows

[Section titled “What a row shows”](#what-a-row-shows)

Each row has the agent, the session name, its state (**waiting for an answer**, **ended with an error** or **done**), the project, the task key if the session has one, the last meaningful line from the screen and how long it has waited. For a question, that line is the question. The heading counts the unseen rows: **Waiting for you (3)**.

## How to go through the inbox

[Section titled “How to go through the inbox”](#how-to-go-through-the-inbox)

1. Open the inbox. Each of the first nine rows has a digit.

2. Press a row, `Enter` or its digit. The Agents view jumps to that pane with the cursor in it.

3. For a result or an error you do not need to open, press **Seen** on the row, or `S`. **Mark everything as seen** does it for all of them.

4. Press `Esc` or **Back to the panes** to return. Focus goes back to the **Inbox** button.

| Key                    | What it does                                                   |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `↑` `↓`, `Home`, `End` | Move between rows                                              |
| `Enter` or `1` to `9`  | Open the pane of the row                                       |
| `S`                    | Mark a result or an error as seen; a question cannot be marked |
| `Esc`                  | Back to the panes                                              |

A result or an error leaves the list once you have seen it: opening the pane counts, and so does marking it. A question stays listed until the agent works again, because it still waits for you. Once you have seen it, with its pane on screen in the focused window, it moves below the unseen rows, is marked **seen, still waiting** and is no longer counted in the badges, the Dock and the announcement. The seen state is kept across restarts. The list uses the same state detection as the pane headers and updates from its events; it does not poll.

The same number appears as a badge on the **Agents** icon, in the Dock icon (macOS, Linux), in the tray, in the status bar and as a polite announcement for screen readers. `Ctrl+B j` jumps to the next agent that waits for you.

## System notifications

[Section titled “System notifications”](#system-notifications)

A system notification is raised when an agent asks for a decision, or finishes a turn after at least 15 seconds of work, and you cannot see it: the window is in the background, or the session’s pane is not on screen. Clicking the notification of one session shows the window and the pane. On macOS the Dock icon also bounces. Plain shells do not notify.

An agent in a pane you cannot see also raises an in-app message when it asks for a decision or finishes a turn.

## Quiet notifications

[Section titled “Quiet notifications”](#quiet-notifications)

Notifications are quiet by default. These settings are in **Settings → Editor & notifications**.

| Setting                | What it does                                                                        | Default |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Notifications**      | Turns system notifications on and off                                               | On      |
| **Notification sound** | A notification plays a sound only when this is on                                   | Off     |
| **Muted agents**       | Sessions of the ticked agents, custom agents included, raise no system notification | None    |
| **Muted projects**     | Sessions of the ticked projects raise no system notification                        | None    |

* A muted agent or project still appears in the inbox and in the counts.
* A session you are looking at, with its pane on screen in the focused window, never notifies.
* Several notifications within four seconds fold into one, “N sessions are waiting for you”, that opens the inbox.

## The tray menu

[Section titled “The tray menu”](#the-tray-menu)

The inbox is also in the menu of the menu bar or tray icon: the **Attention inbox** section lists its five newest items, each as `Waiting`, `Failed` or `Done` with the session name, and the first line of the menu counts the agents that work, wait and are done. Choosing an item shows the window on that agent. The menu has two switches: **Quiet notifications (no sound)**, which is the opposite of **Notification sound**, and **No network calls by the app**. The whole menu is described on [First run](/agent/first-run/#the-menu-bar-and-tray-icon).

Note

Sessions in Herdr are not in the inbox. Their states are read only while the Herdr tab is open.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)The states that put a session in the inbox.

[Workspaces](/agent/workspaces/)The sidebar badge and the Herdr tab.

[First run](/agent/first-run/)The tray menu in full.

[Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/)Every global and prefix shortcut.

# Install Skribly Agent

> Install Skribly Agent on macOS, Windows or Linux, open the unsigned builds, check a download and make your agents visible to the app.

Download Skribly Agent from [agent.skribly.pl/download](https://agent.skribly.pl/download/). The page always offers the newest version. Every release has installers for macOS, Windows and Linux, the same files with fixed names, the `.zip` packages that auto-update uses and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Releases come from a public release home, so you need no account.

## Pick your file

[Section titled “Pick your file”](#pick-your-file)

| System                           | File                            | How to install                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS, Apple Silicon             | `Skribly-mac-arm64.dmg`         | Open the `.dmg` and drag the app to **Applications**                                                     |
| macOS, Intel                     | `Skribly-mac-x64.dmg`           | The same                                                                                                 |
| Windows 10 and 11, x64 and ARM64 | `Skribly-Setup.exe`             | One installer for both architectures; you choose the folder and an install for yourself or for all users |
| Windows 10 and 11, x64 only      | `Skribly-Setup-x64.exe`         | The same installer with x64 only, about half the size                                                    |
| Windows 11, ARM64 only           | `Skribly-Setup-arm64.exe`       | The same installer with ARM64 only                                                                       |
| Windows, portable                | `Skribly-Portable-x64.exe`      | Runs without installing; it does not update itself                                                       |
| Linux, any distribution          | `Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage` | Make it executable and run it                                                                            |
| Debian, Ubuntu                   | `Skribly-linux-amd64.deb`       | Install with `apt`                                                                                       |
| Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE           | `Skribly-linux-x86_64.rpm`      | Install with `dnf`                                                                                       |

Copies with the version in the name, such as `Skribly-<version>-arm64.dmg`, sit next to them.

## Install

[Section titled “Install”](#install)

* macOS

  1. Open the `.dmg` and drag **Skribly Agent** to **Applications**.

  2. Launch it once. The app has no Apple Developer certificate and is not notarised, so Gatekeeper blocks the first launch. Dismiss the message.

  3. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll to the message about Skribly Agent and click **Open Anyway**. On older macOS versions, right-click the app and choose **Open**.

     Or remove the quarantine flag in Terminal:

     ```bash
     xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Skribly Agent.app"
     ```

  You do this once. Updates that the app installs keep working. The message “is damaged and can’t be opened” has the same cause and the same fix.

* Windows

  1. Run `Skribly-Setup.exe`, or the x64 or ARM64 installer. The universal one picks the right architecture.

  2. The installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click **More info → Run anyway**.

  3. Choose the folder and whether to install for yourself or for all users.

  The portable `Skribly-Portable-x64.exe` needs no installation and does not update itself.

* Linux

  AppImage, for any distribution:

  ```bash
  chmod +x Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage
  ./Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage
  ```

  A distribution without FUSE 2 needs `libfuse2` (Ubuntu 22.04 and later: `sudo apt install libfuse2`; Ubuntu 24.04: `libfuse2t64`). Or run the AppImage with `--appimage-extract-and-run`.

  Debian and Ubuntu:

  ```bash
  sudo apt install ./Skribly-linux-amd64.deb
  ```

  Fedora, RHEL and openSUSE:

  ```bash
  sudo dnf install ./Skribly-linux-x86_64.rpm
  ```

  The `.deb` and `.rpm` packages add Skribly to the application menu.

## Check a download

[Section titled “Check a download”](#check-a-download)

Every release has a `SHA256SUMS.txt` with the SHA-256 of every file, the fixed names included. Download it next to the installer and run, in that folder:

| System             | Command                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS              | `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`                                                              |
| Linux              | `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`                                                                  |
| Windows PowerShell | `Get-FileHash .\Skribly-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256`, then compare it with that file’s line in `SHA256SUMS.txt` |

`OK`, or the same hash, means the file is the one the release was built as.

## Install an agent

[Section titled “Install an agent”](#install-an-agent)

Skribly runs the agents you already have. You need `git` and at least one agent, for example:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

You can also install an agent from the app: press **Install** on its card in **Settings → Agents**. The full list with install commands is on [Supported agents](/agent/agents/). After installing a new agent, choose **Settings → Agents → Detect again**. The app needs no separate Node.js.

An app started from Finder, the Dock or the applications menu gets a short `PATH`. On macOS and Linux, Skribly reads the environment from your login shell once at start, with a limit of 5 seconds, and adds `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`. Agents installed with nvm, Homebrew or `npm -g` are then visible as in your terminal. The window opens at once; agents, panes and anything else that starts a program wait for that shell, so nothing runs with the short `PATH`.

Note

Uninstalling removes the app and keeps your data folder, which holds your settings and sessions. What the app stores is on [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/).

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[First run](/agent/first-run/)The tour, the Getting started list and the menu bar icon.

[Supported agents](/agent/agents/)The 13 agents and how to install them.

[Updates](/agent/updates/)How the app updates itself and what the release files are.

[Troubleshooting](/agent/troubleshooting/)When an agent is not found or the app does not open.

# Languages

> Choose the interface language of Skribly Agent: Polish and English are built in, Follow the system picks one of them, and any other language is machine translated online and cached.

The interface of Skribly Agent is written in Polish and ships with an English translation, so those two work with no network. A fresh install starts in Polish. Any other language is translated from the Polish text by free online machine translators the first time you choose it, and the translation is kept on your computer, so it works offline afterwards. The change applies at once to the page, the tray menu, the application menu, notifications and dialog titles, without a restart.

![Settings, Editor & notifications: code editor, notifications on, notification sound off, muted agents and projects, and the interface language list](/_astro/agent-settings-general.DMt4OeHN_Z1fih36.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

Pick the language in any of these places:

* **Settings → Appearance and tour**, the **Interface language** list (Polish, English or **Follow the system**);
* **Settings → Editor & notifications**, the **Interface language** picker with the whole list of languages;
* the command palette (`⌘K`): **Interface language: Polish**, **Interface language: English** or **Interface language: follow the system**;
* the **Interface language** menu in the application menu, with **Polski**, **English** and **Follow the system**.

Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` where this page says `⌘`.

## How to change the language

[Section titled “How to change the language”](#how-to-change-the-language)

1. Open **Settings → Editor & notifications**.

2. Find **Interface language**. Type in **Search languages** to filter the list by name or code, or move through the list with the arrow keys, `Home` and `End` and press `Enter`.

3. For a language that is not in the list, write its code in **Language code** (for example `ga`, `sw` or `fa`) and press **Set**. A code is two or three letters, optionally followed by a region such as `pt-BR`.

4. The interface changes. For a language other than Polish and English, a progress bar shows the download while the texts are fetched.

## How the languages work

[Section titled “How the languages work”](#how-the-languages-work)

| Choice                | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Polish                | The source language of the interface. Nothing is downloaded                                                                                                                                         |
| English               | Read from a file inside the app. A text that is missing from it is translated online like other languages, unless it is already English                                                             |
| **Follow the system** | Picks Polish when the system language is Polish and English for every other system language, so it never starts a download by itself. It follows a change of the system language while the app runs |
| Any other language    | Translated online from Polish, in batches, and saved in the data directory, one file per language                                                                                                   |

The list offers 39 languages (Polish and English included) plus **Follow the system**. A language outside the list works through its code.

## Options

[Section titled “Options”](#options)

| Option                   | What it does                                                                                                                                  | Default        |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| **Interface language**   | The language of the whole app, tray, menus, notifications and dialog titles                                                                   | Polish         |
| **Language code**        | Sets a language that is not in the list                                                                                                       | Empty          |
| **Refresh translations** | Deletes the saved translations of the current language and downloads them again. Shown for every language except Polish and Follow the system | Not applicable |

## What is sent for translation

[Section titled “What is sent for translation”](#what-is-sent-for-translation)

Only sentences of the app’s own interface go to the translators (`translate.googleapis.com`, and `api.mymemory.translated.net` when the first fails). Your projects, tasks, code and file contents never do.

* Text that has no letters, or that looks like code, a path or an address, is not sent.
* Placeholders, code in backticks, addresses, paths, shortcuts and command flags inside a sentence are replaced with markers before sending and put back after.
* Texts that come from you or from your data are marked as not for translation: names, descriptions and texts of **Extensions** additions and the lines of the attention inbox.
* In the English interface, text that is already English stays on the computer.

## Offline and the network switch

[Section titled “Offline and the network switch”](#offline-and-the-network-switch)

* A saved translation is used with no network at all.
* When you choose a language that is not saved yet and the computer is offline, a notice says that the translation will download once you are online and the interface shows Polish meanwhile. It finishes by itself when the connection returns.
* A text the translator could not return is tried again after a minute.
* With **No network calls by the app** on in [Privacy and network](/agent/data-and-network/), nothing is sent for translation, and only saved translations show.

Note

The translators are third-party services, so a machine translation can be wrong or odd. Choose Polish or English when you need the exact words of the app.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

* Use **Refresh translations** when a translation looks wrong or has stayed partly Polish.
* The language of commit messages is a separate setting per project, in [Settings](/agent/settings/).
