| **Import and export**      | Data archive, import from Herdr, agent files                                                    | [Import and export](/agent/import-export/)            |

## How to change a setting

[Section titled “How to change a setting”](#how-to-change-a-setting)

1. Open **Settings** and choose the section in the list on the left.

2. Change the option. Switches, lists and buttons take effect at once; a toast confirms it.

3. For text fields (the worktree folder, the repository address, project fields) leave the field or press **Save**. A project form has its own **Save**.

## Appearance and tour

[Section titled “Appearance and tour”](#appearance-and-tour)

| Option                               | What it does                                                                                                        | Default                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **Theme mode**                       | **Day**, **Night**, **High contrast** or **Follow the system**. The sun and moon icon on the top bar changes it too | Follow the system             |
| **Text size**                        | The text of the interface, the editor and the terminals, in pixels                                                  | 13 px                         |
| **Interface language**               | Polish, English or a language translated from the internet; see [Languages](/agent/languages/)                      | Polish                        |
| **Day and night themes**             | Opens the Appearance view to choose themes from VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or Open VSX; see [Themes](/agent/themes/) | Skribly day and Skribly night |
| **App tour**                         | **Run now** starts the animated tour                                                                                | Shown once on first launch    |
| **Show the tour on next launch**     | **Reset tour** shows it again at the next start                                                                     |                               |
| **Getting started on the Dashboard** | **Show again** brings back the starter checklist on the Dashboard                                                   |                               |
| **Shortcuts and documentation**      | Opens the shortcut list and the Help view                                                                           |                               |

## Task trackers

[Section titled “Task trackers”](#task-trackers)

The accounts themselves are described in [Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/#how-to-connect-a-tracker). The section also has one switch:

| Option                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Default |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Watch trackers for changes** | While the window is open, asks the tracker only for tasks changed since the last check, less often when the window has no focus and not at all when it is hidden. A changed task gets a marker and a notification, and an agent gets only the new comments at start | On      |

## Git accounts

[Section titled “Git accounts”](#git-accounts)

Accounts for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea and Azure DevOps are used for the commit activity card of the Dashboard and for cloning private repositories. The section also keeps the **Repository folders** that are scanned for activity and **Your commit identities**, the e-mail addresses your commits are counted under. See [Dashboard](/agent/dashboard/) and [First workspace](/agent/first-workspace/).

## Agents

[Section titled “Agents”](#agents)

Skribly looks for agents in the `PATH` of your login shell and in the usual install folders.

| Option            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Default     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| **Detect again**  | Runs the detection again; the result is cached for five minutes                                                                                                                                                     |             |
| **Default agent** | The agent suggested for tasks, audits, skills and commit fixes                                                                                                                                                      | Claude Code |
| Agent cards       | The version and path of an installed agent, an install button for the others, and a link to its documentation. A badge says whether the agent has a headless mode, which chat and pipelines use, or only a terminal |             |
| **Custom agents** | Any command-line tool as an agent: a name, a command, optional arguments, an optional resume command in which `{id}` stands for the session id, and a colour. The first message is passed as the last argument      | None        |

Custom agents appear in **New session** and can be controlled with the [`skribly` command](/agent/cli/) as `custom:<id>`. See also [Supported agents](/agent/agents/).

## Cost

[Section titled “Cost”](#cost)

Cost shows what the tokens of your agents would cost next to the token counts. It is an estimate made on this computer from the session files the agents leave and a dated price table. Skribly never blocks anything because of a budget. See [Token use](/agent/usage/).

| Option                                 | What it does                                                                                                                      | Default           |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| **Show cost**                          | One switch for the whole app                                                                                                      | On                |
| Places                                 | One switch each for the usage board, the token chart, the Dashboard, the session toolbar and the tray menu                        | On                |
| **Currency**                           | USD, EUR, PLN and other common codes, or any ISO 4217 code                                                                        | USD               |
| **Rate typed by hand**                 | How much of your currency one USD costs                                                                                           | 1                 |
| **Daily ECB rate**                     | Downloads the reference rates of the European Central Bank, at most every 12 hours; the only network call of Cost                 | Off               |
| **Decimal places**                     | 0 to 4 digits after the decimal point                                                                                             | 2                 |
| **Tiny amounts as “< 0.01”**           | Shows that a cost exists instead of a zero                                                                                        | On                |
| Subscription per agent                 | Labels the cost as an API equivalent and shows the plan and its monthly price next to it. Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI | Off               |
| **Copilot CLI: premium request price** | Empty means in the plan; a price makes the cost premium requests times that price                                                 | Empty             |
| Budgets                                | Daily and monthly limits in total and per agent, shown as a quiet bar on the usage board                                          | None              |
| **Notify at 80%**, **Notify at 100%**  | One system notification per budget and period                                                                                     | On                |
| **Model prices**                       | The table in force. You can change a price, add a model with the names it has in your session files, and reset one model or all   | The shipped table |

## Projects

[Section titled “Projects”](#projects)

Open a project in the list and press **Configure**. **Detect** reads the conventions of the repository again.

| Option               | What it does                                                                        | Default                       |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **Name and colour**  | How the project appears in the app                                                  | The folder name               |
| **Base branch**      | The branch worktrees and task branches start from                                   | Detected                      |
| **Branch pattern**   | `{key}` is the task key, `{slug}` the lower-case title with hyphens                 | `feature/{key}-{slug}`        |
| **Commit pattern**   | `{type}`, `{scope}`, `{subject}`, `{key}`, for example `{type}({scope}): {subject}` | Empty: taken from the history |
| **Commit language**  | **Automatic**, **Polish** or **English**                                            | Automatic                     |
| **Dev-mode app URL** | Opened by the browser preview and the WCAG and SEO audits                           | Detected                      |
| **Project tracker**  | The account tasks come from, and the project, repository or team in it              | None: all trackers            |
| **Checks**           | Commands separated by commas that agents run before handing work back               | Detected                      |

Detection works like this:

| Setting     | How it is detected                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base branch | The first existing one of `develop`, `main`, `master`, falling back to the first local branch                                                                       |
| Checks      | `npm run lint`, `typecheck` and `test` when present in `package.json`, `composer test`, `python manage.py test`, and `pytest` when there is only a `pyproject.toml` |
| Dev URL     | The port from `--port` in the `dev` or `start` script, otherwise `5173` for Vite and `3000` for everything else                                                     |

Skribly never adds a `Co-Authored-By` trailer to a commit. **Remove from the list** takes the project out of Skribly and leaves its files alone.

## Sessions and control

[Section titled “Sessions and control”](#sessions-and-control)

| Option                             | What it does                                                                                                                       | Default                                       |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| **Restore sessions after restart** | Tabs, splits and panes return. Claude Code and Codex resume their conversation; other panes start a fresh shell in the same folder | On                                            |
| **Worktree directory**             | Where worktrees for agents are created. Removing a worktree never deletes its branch                                               | Empty: `~/.skribly/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>` |
| **SSH machines**                   | A name and `user@host` or an alias from `~/.ssh/config`. Skribly opens `ssh -t` and runs the agent there; it stores no passwords   | None                                          |
| **Local control API**              | Lets agents and scripts control panes. Listens on `127.0.0.1` only; the badge shows the port                                       | On                                            |
| **skribly command**                | **Install** adds the command to your `PATH`                                                                                        | Not installed                                 |
| **“skribly” skill for agents**     | **Install** in a chosen project teaches Claude Code and Codex to delegate work                                                     | Not installed                                 |

Under the options the section shows copyable configurations for the MCP server of Skribly, in **Read only (default)** or **With writes (–allow-writes)** form. See [The skribly command](/agent/cli/) and [The Skribly MCP server](/agent/skribly-mcp/).

## Editor and notifications

[Section titled “Editor and notifications”](#editor-and-notifications)

![Settings, Editor and notifications: the code editor list, switches for notifications and their sound, lists of muted agents and projects, and the interface language list](/_astro/agent-settings-general.DMt4OeHN_Z1fih36.webp)

| Option                 | What it does                                                                                            | Default |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Code editor**        | Opens files from the Code, Audits and Skills views: VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or **System default app** | VS Code |
| **Notifications**      | A system notification when an agent finishes or waits for you                                           | On      |
| **Notification sound** | Plays a sound with a notification                                                                       | Off     |
| **Muted agents**       | No system notifications from the checked agents; they still reach the attention inbox                   | None    |
| **Muted projects**     | The same for projects. Several notifications within a few seconds fold into one                         | None    |
| **Interface language** | Polish, English, **Follow the system**, or a translated language                                        | Polish  |

A notification appears only when you are not looking at the session: the window is in the background or its pane is not on screen. See [Attention inbox](/agent/inbox/).

## Skills repository

[Section titled “Skills repository”](#skills-repository)

| Option                     | What it does                                                                                                               | Default                                       |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| **Git repository address** | Where skills are downloaded from. Any address `git clone` accepts, HTTPS or SSH; an SSH address needs a key in `ssh-agent` | `https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills.git` |
| **Restore default**        | Goes back to the default address                                                                                           |                                               |

After a change, synchronise the repository in the Skills view. See [Skills](/agent/skills/).

## Browser for agents

[Section titled “Browser for agents”](#browser-for-agents)

| Option                        | What it does                                                                            | Default |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Share browser with agents** | Opens the Chrome DevTools Protocol on `127.0.0.1` so agents can use the Skribly browser | Off     |
| **Port**                      | 1024 to 65535. Change it if the port is taken                                           | 9333    |
| **State**                     | Says whether a restart is needed: the port opens at startup                             |         |
| **MCP configuration**         | Copyable setup for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Playwright MCP            |         |

Caution

While sharing is on, every program on this computer can connect to the port, and tabs with signed-in accounts are visible. Turn it on when you work with agents. See [Browser](/agent/browser/) and [Troubleshooting](/agent/troubleshooting/#the-browser-port-is-in-use).

## Command guard

[Section titled “Command guard”](#command-guard)

The guard makes agents ask before a dangerous command and lets you choose groups of commands each agent may run without asking. It is **off by default**, and until you turn it on and confirm the list of files, Skribly writes nothing into the configuration of any agent. It is a safety net, not a sandbox.

| Option                | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Default |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Turn on the guard** | Previews the files that change, then writes after you confirm. Turning it off removes exactly the entries Skribly added                                                                                                                      | Off     |
| Agents                | Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode                                                                                                                                                                                                              | None    |
| Groups per agent      | **Read and search**, **Edit files**, **Git**, **Push**, **Build and tests**, **Everything**                                                                                                                                                  | None    |
| **Always ask**        | A read-only list of what always asks, whatever you tick: deleting files, discarding git changes, rewriting history, wiping databases, removing containers, killing processes, publishing packages, `sudo` and piping a download into a shell |         |

To change the groups, change the ticks and press **Preview and apply changes**. The dialog lists every file, whether it is created or extended, and each entry; **Write to the files** saves a copy of each existing file first.

## Updates

[Section titled “Updates”](#updates)

| Option                   | What it does                                                                                | Default |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Check for updates**    | Checks now and shows the state                                                              |         |
| **Update automatically** | Checks at startup and every 4 hours, downloads in the background and installs when you quit | On      |
| **Data directory**       | **Show** opens the folder; the copy button copies its path                                  |         |

See [Updates](/agent/updates/).

## Data directory

[Section titled “Data directory”](#data-directory)

**Settings → Updates → Data directory → Show** opens the folder that holds settings, projects, tracker accounts with their encrypted keys, the layout, sessions, the skills repository, downloaded themes and the history of pipelines.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

* A setting you cannot find is often in the view it belongs to: pipelines, audits and the browser keep their options on their own page.
* **Privacy and network** lists what the app does on the network. **No network calls by the app** there also stops update checks and the ECB rate.

# Keyboard shortcuts

> Every keyboard shortcut of Skribly Agent: the command palette, switching views, the Ctrl+B pane prefix, the editor and git, chat and the tour.

Skribly Agent can be driven from the keyboard: the command palette finds any view, project, agent or action, number shortcuts switch views, and a tmux-style prefix controls panes. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` wherever this page says `⌘`.

![The command palette over the Dashboard: a search field and the list of views with their descriptions and shortcuts](/_astro/agent-palette.Ch8s-qBM_1Lw2IF.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

The **Help** view, at the bottom of the activity bar, lists the shortcuts under **Keyboard shortcuts**. **Settings → Appearance and tour** has a **Shortcuts** button that opens the same list, and `Ctrl+B` `?` shows the pane shortcuts as a cheat sheet in the Agents view.

![The Help view: Start tour and Command palette, the five Getting started steps and the keyboard shortcuts](/_astro/agent-help.BbO1U87B_1HSWoQ.webp)

## Global

[Section titled “Global”](#global)

| Shortcut      | Action                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `⌘K` or `⌘⇧P` | Command palette: views, projects, **New session: \<agent>**, **New terminal** and actions. Press it again to close it |
| `⌘⇧A`         | Agent panel on the right                                                                                              |
| `⌘⇧U`         | Attention inbox in the Agents view                                                                                    |
| `⌘1` … `⌘9`   | Views: Dashboard, Agents, Tasks, Code & git, Pipelines, Skills, Audits, Browser, Docker                               |
| `Esc`         | Closes the palette and dialogs                                                                                        |

In the palette, `↑` and `↓` move through the results, `Enter` runs the selected one and `Esc` closes it. The palette shows up to 40 results and finds a word by its letters in order.

## Panes: the `Ctrl+B` prefix

[Section titled “Panes: the Ctrl+B prefix”](#panes-the-ctrlb-prefix)

Press `Ctrl+B`, release it, then press the key, as in tmux. The prefix stays active for two seconds, and a **Ctrl+B…** badge pulses on the tab bar. The shortcuts are caught before they reach the terminal, so they work with the focus in a pane. They do not work while a dialog or the palette is open. On macOS the prefix is the `Control` key, not `⌘`.

| Shortcut                   | Action                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Ctrl+B` `v` or `%`        | Split right (new shell in the active pane’s directory) |
| `Ctrl+B` `-` or `"`        | Split down (new shell)                                 |
| `Ctrl+B` `a`               | New agent session next to the active pane              |
| `Ctrl+B` `c`               | New tab in the current workspace                       |
| `Ctrl+B` `n` / `p`         | Next / previous tab                                    |
| `Ctrl+B` `1` … `9`         | Tab by number                                          |
| `Ctrl+B` `→` `↓` / `←` `↑` | Focus the next / previous pane in the tab              |
| `Ctrl+B` `z`               | Maximise or restore the active pane                    |
| `Ctrl+B` `o`               | Overview of all agents with live screens               |
| `Ctrl+B` `i`               | Attention inbox: sessions waiting for you              |
| `Ctrl+B` `j`               | Jump to the next agent waiting for you                 |
| `Ctrl+B` `h`               | Session history and resume                             |
| `Ctrl+B` `x`               | Close the active pane                                  |
| `Ctrl+B` `w`               | Next workspace                                         |
| `Ctrl+B` `b`               | Show or hide the workspace sidebar                     |
| `Ctrl+B` `?`               | Shortcut cheat sheet                                   |
| `Ctrl+B` `Ctrl+B`          | Cancel the prefix                                      |

On macOS there are also `⌘D` (split right), `⌘⇧D` (split down) and `⌘T` (new tab).

Note

`Ctrl+B` never reaches the program running in the terminal. If you use tmux inside a pane, or a `Ctrl+B` shortcut in your shell, change the prefix in that program. The Skribly prefix is fixed.

## Editor and git

[Section titled “Editor and git”](#editor-and-git)

| Shortcut     | Where                 | Action                                                                             |
| ------------ | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `⌘P`         | Code                  | Quick open (`↑` `↓` or `Ctrl+N` `Ctrl+P` to move, `Enter` to open, `Esc` to close) |
| `⌘⇧F`        | Code                  | Search in files                                                                    |
| `⌘S`         | Editor                | Save the file                                                                      |
| `⌘W`         | Editor                | Close the tab                                                                      |
| `Ctrl+G`     | Editor                | Go to line (the `Control` key on macOS too)                                        |
| `` Ctrl+` `` | Code                  | Bottom terminal (the `Control` key on macOS too)                                   |
| `⌘⇧I`        | Editor                | Ask an agent about the selected code                                               |
| `⌘⌥M`        | Diff                  | Add a review note on the selected lines                                            |
| `⌘Enter`     | Commit box            | Commit                                                                             |
| `⌘Enter`     | Note and send dialogs | Save a note, or send the notes or code to the agent                                |

## Chat and the agent panel

[Section titled “Chat and the agent panel”](#chat-and-the-agent-panel)

| Shortcut                       | Action                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`                        | Send the message                                                      |
| `Shift+Enter`                  | New line                                                              |
| `/`                            | Slash commands; `↑` `↓` choose, `Tab` or `Enter` insert, `Esc` clears |
| `Enter` in the broadcast field | Send the text to the selected panes                                   |

## Tour

[Section titled “Tour”](#tour)

| Key              | Action                      |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| `→`              | Next step                   |
| `←`              | Previous step               |
| `Tab` or `Enter` | Pause the automatic advance |
| `Esc`            | Close the tour              |

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

* The palette lists the shortcut next to each view, so you can learn them while you search.
* `⌘1` to `⌘9` stay with the first nine views; the other views have no number and open from the palette or the activity bar.

# Skills

> The Skills view of Skribly Agent fetches the agent-skills repository and installs skills into a project in each agent's own format and folder.

The **Skills** view lists the skills of the agent-skills repository: short procedures for an agent, such as working on a task, committing or reviewing. Skribly keeps a copy of the repository, installs the skills you tick into a project in the format and folder each agent reads, and can match the installed skills to the project’s conventions. What the skills themselves do is described in the [agent-skills section](/skills/).

![The Skills view: the agent-skills repository with Sync, Generate .docs and Install selected, category filters and skill cards with the agents each one is installed for](/_astro/agent-skills.C1sFLo-p_Z2idnn7.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Skills** in the activity bar on the left, or press `⌘6`, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Skills**.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` in place of `⌘`.

## How to fetch the repository

[Section titled “How to fetch the repository”](#how-to-fetch-the-repository)

1. Open **Skills**. The first time the view is empty and asks you to download the skills.

2. Press **Fetch the repository**. Skribly clones the repository into its data folder with `git clone --depth 50`.

3. Press **Sync** later to update it. It runs `git pull --ff-only`, so a fork with local commits is never rewritten.

Below the title a line shows the repository address, the short hash of the version and when it was last synchronised. An error from git is shown on the same line. Fetching and syncing are the only network calls of the view, and only when you press the button. The **No network calls by the app** switch blocks them; see [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/).

## How to install skills in a project

[Section titled “How to install skills in a project”](#how-to-install-skills-in-a-project)

You need a project selected in the app.

1. Find the skills you want. Type in **Search skills** (it looks at the name, title, description and tags) or pick a category under **Category**.

2. Tick the box on each card, or open a card to read the skill and press **Install** there.

3. Press **Install selected**. The button shows how many skills are ticked.

4. Choose the agents. Agents found on this computer have a badge, and agents the skill does not support are greyed out.

5. Press **Install in project**. A log lists what was written and where. Press **Done** to close it.

The files go into the project’s repository, so the whole team has the same skills. A skill counts as installed for an agent when any of its paths exists, and the badges on the cards and in the open card show it.

| Agent       | Where the skill goes                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                     |
| Codex       | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                     |
| Cursor      | `.agents/skills/` (the older `.cursor/rules/<name>.mdc` also counts as installed)                    |
| Gemini CLI  | `.agents/skills/` and `.gemini/commands/<name>.toml`                                                 |
| OpenCode    | `.agents/skills/` and `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`                                                 |
| Windsurf    | `.agents/skills/` and `.windsurf/workflows/<name>.md`                                                |
| Copilot     | `.agents/skills/` (the older `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md` also counts as installed) |

Claude Code reads `.claude/skills`. The other agents read the shared `.agents/skills` folder, so a skill is written once for them. The extra command files are made by the repository’s own installer.

Skribly runs the repository’s installer, `cli/agent-skills.mjs`, in a worker inside the app, so you need no separate Node.js. It runs only when you press **Install in project**. If the installer fails to write a skill, or is missing, Skribly copies the skill folder itself to `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code and to `.agents/skills/` for the others.

## How to match installed skills to the project

[Section titled “How to match installed skills to the project”](#how-to-match-installed-skills-to-the-project)

1. Install the skills first. The button is greyed out while none is installed.

2. Press **Match installed to the project (Claude)** under the title. The name in brackets is your default agent.

3. An agent opens in the Agents view with a prompt. It reads only the dependency file, the README, the last 30 commits and the linter and test configuration, fills in the project-dependent parts of the skills (check commands, base branch, branch and commit patterns, dev URL), saves them in `.tasks/workflow.md` and lists what it changed. It does not commit and does not change the general procedures.

## How to generate .docs

[Section titled “How to generate .docs”](#how-to-generate-docs)

1. Press **Generate .docs**. It needs a project.

2. Skribly scans the repository without a model and writes the skeleton of the project’s `.docs/` folder. A file you edited by hand, without the `skribly:auto` marker, is not overwritten.

3. An agent opens in the Agents view and fills in the architecture, the commands and the dependencies. It proposes a short `AGENTS.md` that points to `.docs/`, and does not save it without your approval.

## What is on the screen

[Section titled “What is on the screen”](#what-is-on-the-screen)

| Part                               | What it shows or does                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Repository line                    | Address, version, time of the last sync and any error                                                                                                         |
| **Sync**                           | Updates the repository. It reads **Fetch the repository** until the first download                                                                            |
| **Generate .docs**                 | The two steps above                                                                                                                                           |
| **Install selected**               | Opens the agent choice for the ticked skills                                                                                                                  |
| **Match installed to the project** | The prompt described above                                                                                                                                    |
| **Search skills** and **Category** | Filter the cards. The categories come from the repository                                                                                                     |
| Skill card                         | Title, `/name`, three lines of description, category and the agents it supports. A green badge with a number shows for how many agents it is installed        |
| Open card                          | The skill’s text, the agents it is installed for, **Show files** (the folder in your file manager), **GitHub** (only for an HTTPS repository) and **Install** |

## Settings → Skills repository

[Section titled “Settings → Skills repository”](#settings--skills-repository)

The address is set in **Settings**, section **Skills repository**.

| Option                 | What it does                                                                     | Default                                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| **Git repository URL** | Where Skribly fetches skills from. Any address `git clone` accepts: HTTPS or SSH | `https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills.git` |
| **Save**               | Keeps the address. Then press **Sync** in the Skills view                        |                                               |
| **Restore defaults**   | Puts the default address back                                                    |                                               |
| **Open repository**    | Opens an HTTPS address in the browser                                            |                                               |

Use your own fork or a company repository to give the team a different set of skills. If the repository has a `skills.json`, the catalogue is read from it. Without one, Skribly reads the `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` folders.

## The skribly skill

[Section titled “The skribly skill”](#the-skribly-skill)

A separate skill, `skribly`, teaches Claude Code and Codex to hand work to other agents: a reviewer beside them, an implementer in its own worktree, waiting for the result and reading it. It is built into the app and does not come from the repository. Install it in **Settings**, section **Sessions & control**, under **“skribly” skill for agents**: choose the project and press **Install**. It writes `.claude/skills/skribly/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/skribly/SKILL.md`. The commands it uses are described in [The skribly command](/agent/cli/).

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

Install only the skills a project uses. An agent keeps just each skill’s name and description in context, but a short list is easier to read. See [Token saving](/agent/token-saving/).

* Commit the installed skill folders, so a new teammate gets them with the clone.
* When a project has the `task` skill, **Start with an agent** in the Tasks view sends `/task <KEY>` to Claude Code and `$task <KEY>` to Codex instead of a long prompt.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[agent-skills](/skills/)The skills themselves: what each one does and how to install the set.

[Token saving](/agent/token-saving/)How the skills keep the text sent to the model small.

[Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/)Start a task with an agent and the task skill.

[Extensions](/agent/extensions/)Your own prompts, rules and skills, kept apart from the repository.

# The Skribly MCP server

> skribly mcp gives coding agents the control of Skribly Agent as MCP tools - read-only by default, with writes only after you allow each call in the app, and one-project mode.

`skribly mcp` is an MCP server that Skribly Agent offers to your coding agents. It exposes the operations of [the `skribly` command](/agent/cli/) as tools: list panes and agents, read a screen, wait for an agent, and, only when you allow it, start, prompt and stop agents. It also gives an agent read-only context about one project: its settings, tasks, sessions, staged diff and commit rules.

This page is about Skribly’s own server. The MCP servers your agents use to reach other tools are on [MCP servers](/agent/mcp/).

## How it works

[Section titled “How it works”](#how-it-works)

The server speaks MCP over standard input and output, and talks to the running app through the same local control API as the command. It works only while Skribly Agent is running and **Local control API** is on in **Settings → Sessions & control**. See [The skribly command](/agent/cli/#how-it-works) for the port and the token.

## How to connect an agent

[Section titled “How to connect an agent”](#how-to-connect-an-agent)

1. Make sure the `skribly` command is installed: **Settings → Sessions & control → skribly command → Install**.

2. In the same section, choose **Read only (default)** or **With writes (–allow-writes)** above the configurations. The three snippets change with the choice.

3. Copy the snippet for your agent and run it, or paste it into its configuration file.

| Agent       | Where the configuration goes                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code | In a terminal: `claude mcp add skribly -- skribly mcp`                                                  |
| Codex       | `~/.codex/config.toml`, a `[mcp_servers.skribly]` table with `command = "skribly"` and `args = ["mcp"]` |
| Cursor      | `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, under `mcpServers`                             |
| Gemini CLI  | `~/.gemini/settings.json`, under `mcpServers`                                                           |

If the command is not in your `PATH`, use the full path shown in Settings. You can also add the server from **Plugins & MCP → Add MCP server**, which offers **Skribly** (read only) and **Skribly with writes**. See [MCP servers](/agent/mcp/).

## Read by default, writes only on request

[Section titled “Read by default, writes only on request”](#read-by-default-writes-only-on-request)

`skribly mcp` offers only the tools that change nothing. An agent connected with the plain configuration cannot start, prompt or stop an agent, type into a pane, create or remove a worktree, or show a notification.

`skribly mcp --allow-writes` also offers the eight tools that change something, and every call of one asks you first. Skribly Agent comes to the front and shows a dialog with the tool name and its arguments in full, with **Deny** as the default. The app runs exactly the arguments it showed, and only after **Allow**.

The call fails, and nothing changes, when you deny or close the dialog, when the agent stops waiting before you answer, and when the app is not running or its control API is off.

Note

So that what runs is what you read, arguments longer than 4,000 characters are refused without asking, and invisible or look-alike characters, such as bidirectional marks, zero-width characters and unusual spaces, are shown as escapes like `\u{202E}`. One question is shown at a time.

The `skribly` command itself does not ask: it is what you or a script type in a terminal. The question is part of the MCP server, because an agent is the caller.

## The tools

[Section titled “The tools”](#the-tools)

| Tool                                                                                                                                                | What it does                                                    | Asks you |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `skribly_status`                                                                                                                                    | Number of panes and agents and their states                     | No       |
| `skribly_list_workspaces`                                                                                                                           | Projects, worktrees and the panes in each                       | No       |
| `skribly_list_panes`                                                                                                                                | All panes                                                       | No       |
| `skribly_list_agents`                                                                                                                               | Agents and their states                                         | No       |
| `skribly_read_agent`                                                                                                                                | The agent’s screen, 60 lines by default                         | No       |
| `skribly_wait_agent`                                                                                                                                | Waits for chosen states, 600 seconds by default                 | No       |
| `skribly_explain_agent`                                                                                                                             | Why the agent is in its state                                   | No       |
| `skribly_read_pane`                                                                                                                                 | A pane’s screen                                                 | No       |
| `skribly_wait_output`                                                                                                                               | Waits until output matches an expression, 60 seconds by default | No       |
| `skribly_list_worktrees`                                                                                                                            | A project’s worktrees                                           | No       |
| `skribly_project_profile`, `skribly_list_tasks`, `skribly_get_task`, `skribly_list_sessions`, `skribly_staged_diff_summary`, `skribly_commit_rules` | The read-only project tools below                               | No       |
| `skribly_start_agent`                                                                                                                               | Starts an agent in a new pane, optionally in a worktree         | Yes      |
| `skribly_prompt_agent`                                                                                                                              | Sends a message, optionally waiting for the end of the turn     | Yes      |
| `skribly_stop_agent`                                                                                                                                | Closes the agent’s pane                                         | Yes      |
| `skribly_create_pane`                                                                                                                               | Opens a pane                                                    | Yes      |
| `skribly_run_in_pane`                                                                                                                               | Types a shell command in a pane                                 | Yes      |
| `skribly_create_worktree`                                                                                                                           | Creates a worktree                                              | Yes      |
| `skribly_remove_worktree`                                                                                                                           | Removes a worktree and keeps the branch                         | Yes      |
| `skribly_notify`                                                                                                                                    | Shows a system notification                                     | Yes      |

The tools that change something start their description with “CHANGES THINGS.” and carry the MCP `readOnlyHint` annotation, true or false. Every result starts with a line that says it is data from Skribly Agent and the repository, not instructions, because a task text, a rules file or a screen can contain text written to steer an agent.

## Read-only project tools

[Section titled “Read-only project tools”](#read-only-project-tools)

Six tools give an agent the context of one project without any way to change it.

| Tool                          | Returns                                                                                                        | Arguments                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `skribly_project_profile`     | Name, path, settings (base branch, patterns, checks, tracker), git state and the files that state commit rules | `project`                                                     |
| `skribly_list_tasks`          | The project’s local tasks: key, title, stage, branch, next step, last update                                   | `project`                                                     |
| `skribly_get_task`            | One task: metadata, `STATE.md` and `TASK.md`, each cut at 20,000 characters                                    | `key` (required), `project`                                   |
| `skribly_list_sessions`       | The project’s agent and shell sessions with their status, without terminal output                              | `project`                                                     |
| `skribly_staged_diff_summary` | The staged changes within a character budget: every file named, then the most relevant hunks                   | `project`, `file`, `budget` (1,000 to 40,000, default 12,000) |
| `skribly_commit_rules`        | The commit rules the repository states and its last 20 commit subjects                                         | `project`                                                     |

`project` is a name, an id or an absolute path inside a project. Without it, the project of the calling pane is used. A path outside any project, an unknown name, a `file` outside the project and a task key that is a path are refused before anything is read.

`skribly_staged_diff_summary` and `skribly_commit_rules` return the same context the **Agent** button in the commit box gives its agent. See [Changes and commits](/agent/changes/).

## How to limit an agent to one project

[Section titled “How to limit an agent to one project”](#how-to-limit-an-agent-to-one-project)

Start the server with `--project <name>`, for example `claude mcp add skribly -- skribly mcp --project my-project`. Every project tool, `skribly_list_worktrees` included, is then fixed to that project, and a call that names another project is refused. `skribly_list_workspaces` lists every project, so it is not offered at all in this mode.

Caution

The tools that read terminals (`skribly_read_pane`, `skribly_read_agent`, `skribly_wait_output`) show whatever is on a screen and are not limited to one project; `skribly_list_panes` and `skribly_list_agents` list every pane. Connect them only to agents you trust, or give the agent only the six project tools through its own tool allow list.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

* Start with the read-only configuration. Add `--allow-writes` when you want an agent to orchestrate others, and answer each request in the app.
* The `--read-only` flag of earlier versions is still accepted and does nothing, because reading only is now the default.
* Install the `skribly` skill in the project so the agent knows when to delegate. See [The skribly command](/agent/cli/#how-to-turn-it-on).

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[The skribly command](/agent/cli/)The same operations from a terminal, with recipes.

[MCP servers](/agent/mcp/)The MCP servers your agents use, and how to test them.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What listens on this computer and who can reach it.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Where the control API and the configurations are.

# Tasks and trackers

> The Tasks view of Skribly Agent lists your tasks from Skribly Tracker, Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab and Linear, and starts an agent on one with its file and branch ready.

The **Tasks** view brings the tasks assigned to you from your trackers into one list, next to the tasks you started and tasks you write yourself. From a task you can change its status, assign it, comment, log time and open it in the tracker. **Start with an agent** saves the task to a file in the project, creates a branch or a worktree and starts an agent with a ready prompt, so the agent spends no tokens fetching the ticket.

![The Tasks view: tasks in progress and assigned to me from Jira and Redmine on the left, and a Jira task with Start with an agent, status, Assign to me, Comment, Log time and Open in tracker](/_astro/agent-tasks.Cduw6-XK_Z1bOamU.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Tasks** in the activity bar, or press `⌘3` (on Windows and Linux `Ctrl+3`), or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Tasks**.

Without a tracker account the list is empty and offers **Tracker settings** and **Custom task**. Connect a tracker first: see [How to connect a tracker](#how-to-connect-a-tracker).

## How to connect a tracker

[Section titled “How to connect a tracker”](#how-to-connect-a-tracker)

1. Open **Settings**, then **Task trackers**, and press **Add tracker**.

2. Choose the tracker, type a **Name** (for example “Company Jira”) and the **Address**. For Jira choose the **Installation type**, and for Jira Cloud type the **Atlassian account email**.

3. Paste the token. **Open tokens page** opens the page where you create it. The table below says which token each tracker needs.

4. Press **Save and test**. The account is saved and the connection is checked. **Test** repeats the check at any time.

You can have several accounts, also several of one tracker. Edit an account with the pencil: leave the token empty to keep the old one. Deleting an account deletes its encrypted token too; task files in projects stay.

For GitHub and GitLab you can limit an account to some repositories or projects (or a whole organisation or group). The limit narrows your tasks, the search and the places offered for new tasks. Empty means everything the token can see.

| Tracker                       | Address                                                               | Token                                                                        | Permissions                                                                | Task key           |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| **Skribly Tracker**           | Your instance; locally `http://localhost:8100`                        | **Profile → API tokens → create a token** (read and write; it is shown once) | Read and write                                                             | `AGENT-12`         |
| **Jira Cloud**                | `https://your-team.atlassian.net`, plus your account email            | id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens → Create API token                  | Read the issues of the projects you can see                                | `PROJ-123`         |
| **Jira Server / Data Center** | Your server; leave the email empty                                    | Profile → Personal Access Tokens                                             | The same                                                                   | `PROJ-123`         |
| **Redmine**                   | The home page address, without `/issues`                              | My account → API access key → Show                                           | An administrator must enable the REST API: Administration → Settings → API | `2047`             |
| **GitHub**                    | Empty for github.com; Enterprise: `https://github.example.com/api/v3` | Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens                       | Fine-grained, **Issues: Read-only** for the repositories with your tasks   | `owner/repo#12`    |
| **GitLab**                    | Empty for gitlab.com, or your own instance                            | Preferences → Access tokens → Add new token                                  | The `read_api` scope                                                       | `group/project#34` |
| **Linear**                    | Can stay empty: Linear has one API address                            | Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys → New API key               | An account that can see the teams with your tasks                          | `ENG-56`           |

The token is encrypted with the system password store (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows, libsecret on Linux) through Electron `safeStorage`. It is not shown in the interface and it does not end up in project files. When encryption is not available, for example on Linux without a keyring, the token is kept in memory only until the app closes.

A token with read-only rights is enough to list and open tasks. Changing a status, assigning, commenting, logging time and creating a task need a token that may write.

### What each tracker lists

[Section titled “What each tracker lists”](#what-each-tracker-lists)

| Tracker         | “Assigned to me”                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Tracker | Your assigned tasks                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Jira            | Issues with `assignee = currentUser()` that are not done, newest update first, up to 100. Jira Cloud signs in with email and token, Server and Data Center with the token as a bearer header |
| Redmine         | Open issues assigned to you, newest update first, up to 100                                                                                                                                  |
| GitHub          | Open issues assigned to you (pull requests left out), up to 100                                                                                                                              |
| GitLab          | Open issues assigned to you, up to 100                                                                                                                                                       |
| Linear          | Issues assigned to you that are not completed or canceled, up to 100                                                                                                                         |

### What each tracker can do in the app

[Section titled “What each tracker can do in the app”](#what-each-tracker-can-do-in-the-app)

| Tracker         | Comment | Status | Assign | Create | Search | Log time |
| --------------- | ------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | -------- |
| Skribly Tracker | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| Jira            | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| Redmine         | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| GitHub          | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | No       |
| GitLab          | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| Linear          | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | No       |

A button the tracker does not support is switched off, and its hint says why. When you create a task, the form also shows the fields the tracker has:

| Tracker         | Type | Priority | Labels | Activity (when logging time) |
| --------------- | ---- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------- |
| Skribly Tracker | Yes  | Yes      | Yes    | Yes                          |
| Jira            | Yes  | Yes      | Yes    | No                           |
| Redmine         | Yes  | Yes      | No     | Yes                          |
| GitHub          | No   | No       | Yes    | No                           |
| GitLab          | Yes  | No       | Yes    | No                           |
| Linear          | No   | Yes      | Yes    | No                           |

### Environment variables for agent-skills

[Section titled “Environment variables for agent-skills”](#environment-variables-for-agent-skills)

Agents that the app starts get the credentials of your accounts as environment variables of their own session, under the names that the [agent-skills](/skills/) skills read. This way `/task 123` works without a `credentials.env` file. No file is written to disk, and only the process the app started sees them.

| Tracker                   | Variables                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Tracker           | `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL`, `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN`                                                                   |
| Jira Cloud                | `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN`                                                                       |
| Jira Server / Data Center | `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_PAT`                                                                                           |
| Redmine                   | `REDMINE_URL`, `REDMINE_API_KEY`                                                                                 |
| GitHub                    | `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GITHUB_API_URL` when the address is not `api.github.com`                                    |
| GitLab                    | `GITLAB_URL`, `GITLAB_TOKEN`                                                                                     |
| Linear                    | `LINEAR_API_KEY`                                                                                                 |
| All                       | `AGENT_SKILLS_TRACKER`: the tracker for bare numbers, that of the project’s tracker or else of the first account |

With several accounts of one tracker, the account assigned to the project wins, then the first in the list.

To assign a tracker to a project, open **Settings → Projects** and set **Project tracker** and **Project / repository / team in the tracker**. The Tasks view then opens filtered to that tracker, and **Start with an agent** and new tasks use it by default.

## How to find a task

[Section titled “How to find a task”](#how-to-find-a-task)

1. Look at **In progress** (tasks you already started in your projects, with their stage) and **Assigned to me** (open tasks of all accounts, most recently updated first).

2. Press an account name to see only that account, or **All**.

3. Type in the search field. It filters the list by key, title and label at once. After a short pause, and at once with `Enter`, it also asks the tracker, and lists the results under **In the tracker**.

4. To open a task that is not on the list, type its number in **Task number** and press `Enter`: for example `2047`, `PROJ-12` or `org/repo#5`. It is looked up in the account selected in the filter, or in the first one.

Click a task to see its details on the right: the tracker, key, status, labels, assignee, the description and the comments.

## How to work on a task

[Section titled “How to work on a task”](#how-to-work-on-a-task)

The details have these buttons:

| Button                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Start with an agent** | Opens the start dialog, described below                                                                                                                                          |
| Status list             | Changes the status; in Jira it runs a workflow transition                                                                                                                        |
| **Assign to me**        | Assigns the task to you; the **Unassign** button next to it takes the assignment away                                                                                            |
| **Comment**             | Opens an editor with a Markdown preview. Skribly turns the text into the tracker’s format (for example ADF in Jira Cloud). **Send the agent’s summary** fills it from `STATE.md` |
| **Log time**            | Hours (more than 0 and up to 24), the day (not in the future), an activity where the tracker has them and a comment. GitLab records time without a date                          |
| **Open in tracker**     | Opens the task in the browser                                                                                                                                                    |

## How to start a task with an agent

[Section titled “How to start a task with an agent”](#how-to-start-a-task-with-an-agent)

1. Select a task and press **Start with an agent**.

2. Choose the **Project** and the **Agent**. Installed agents are listed, and the default one is chosen.

3. Keep **Create the branch by the project’s pattern (clean repository only)** ticked, or tick **In a separate worktree**, which implies a branch.

4. Press **Start**. The app switches to the Agents view, on the new pane.

What the app does:

1. It creates `.skribly/tasks/<KEY>/` in the project and adds `.skribly/` to `.git/info/exclude`, a local ignore file that is not in the repository. Characters of the key outside letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-` become `-`, so `org/repo#5` is `org-repo-5`.

2. It writes `TASK.md` with the content and the comments, and with the rules of your enabled extensions. The file is overwritten on every start.

3. It creates `STATE.md` from a template only when it does not exist, so progress is never lost.

4. It writes `meta.json` with the key, the title, the address and the account.

5. It prepares the branch. The pattern is the project’s **Branch pattern**, `feature/{key}-{slug}` by default; `{slug}` is up to six words of the title, in lower case, without Polish accents, joined by hyphens. For `SKLEP-142` titled “Koszyk: zapis przy wylogowaniu” the branch is `feature/SKLEP-142-koszyk-zapis-przy-wylogowaniu`. An existing branch is switched to, a new one is created. If tracked files have changes, no branch is created and the agent starts on the current one.

6. With **In a separate worktree** it makes a worktree of that branch from the project’s **Base branch**, and starts the agent there. Your copy stays untouched. The task folder is linked into the worktree, so the agent finds `TASK.md` at its side. See [Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/).

7. It starts the agent in a terminal titled `<KEY> · <agent>`, with this prompt:

   * Claude Code, when the project has the `task` skill in `.claude/skills/task`: `/task <KEY>`;
   * Codex, with the skill in `.agents/skills/task`: `$task <KEY>`;
   * any other case: a short text that points to `TASK.md` and `STATE.md`, asks the agent to read both and propose a plan (a `SPEC.md` for a large task), to wait for your “ok” before changing code, to update `STATE.md` after each stage, and to commit only after your approval, in the style of the project history and without `Co-Authored-By` trailers.

`STATE.md` holds a stage line, the next step, and lists of what is done, decisions and open questions. The template is written in Polish. The app reads two lines of it: `Etap:` with one of `analiza`, `implementacja`, `weryfikacja` or `gotowe`, and `Następny krok:`. It shows them in **In progress**.

## How to create a task

[Section titled “How to create a task”](#how-to-create-a-task)

1. Press the plus in the head of the list (**New tracker task**).

2. Choose the **Tracker account** and the project (for GitHub the repository, for Linear the team). The place of the project settings is chosen, or one marked with a star.

3. Fill **Title** and the description in Markdown. Pick the type, the priority and the labels where the tracker has them.

4. Tick **Start with an agent right away** if you want to continue with the start dialog, then press **Create**.

## How to write a local task

[Section titled “How to write a local task”](#how-to-write-a-local-task)

Not every task lives in a tracker.

1. Press the second icon in the head of the list (**Custom task**).

2. Type a title and a description in Markdown: what to do, where to look, acceptance criteria.

3. Press **Next**. The same start dialog opens.

The task gets a key such as `W-10291412` (month, day, hour and minute) and then works like any other: `TASK.md`, `STATE.md`, a branch and an agent. A local task has no tracker buttons.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

Commit suggestions use your tasks: when the branch name contains the key of a started task, the title becomes the subject. See [Changes and commits](/agent/changes/).

* Ask the agent to keep `STATE.md` up to date. It is the same file that lets another agent take over the work, and the **Send the agent’s summary** button of the comment turns it into a tracker comment.
* If the list shows an error such as a 401 or 403 from the tracker, check the token and its permissions in **Settings → Task trackers** with **Test**.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Plan](/agent/plan/)The open items of the plan files of your project.

[Changes and commits](/agent/changes/)Commit suggestions that use the task key and title.

[Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/)The worktree that Start with an agent can create.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)All the sections of Settings.

# Terminals

> Shell panes of Skribly Agent, the terminal at the bottom of the Code view and SSH machines, with short pointers to resume, broadcast, hand-off and the agent panel.

A terminal in Skribly Agent is a pane that runs a shell or an agent. Terminals live in the app’s main process, so switching views or tabs, or reloading the window, does not interrupt them. A reopened pane replays its last output. This page covers the plain shell, the terminal of the Code view and SSH machines; agents and chat are on [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/).

## Shell panes

[Section titled “Shell panes”](#shell-panes)

Choose **Terminal** in **New session** for a plain shell. It opens a login shell in the folder of the project or worktree you chose. A split from a pane, `Ctrl+B v` or `Ctrl+B -`, also starts a shell in that pane’s folder. A shell pane does not notify you and is not in the [attention inbox](/agent/inbox/). If you start an agent by hand in it, for example `codex`, the app recognises it and gives the pane the agent’s avatar and state rules.

Splits, tabs and zoom are on [Workspaces](/agent/workspaces/). Shell panes are saved with the layout; after a restart they start as a fresh shell in the same folder.

## The terminal in the Code view

[Section titled “The terminal in the Code view”](#the-terminal-in-the-code-view)

The Code view has a shell in the project folder in a panel at the bottom. Press ``⌃` ``(Control and the backtick) to open it, or the terminal button in the view. There is one such shell per project, so opening the panel again starts no new one. Its panel header has **New shell** and **Hide panel** buttons, and you can drag its edge to change the height. The session is hidden from the Agents view and lives in memory only. See [Editor and files](/agent/code/).

## SSH machines

[Section titled “SSH machines”](#ssh-machines)

An agent can work on a server while its pane stays in Skribly.

1. Open **Settings → Sessions & control**, section **SSH machines**. Enter a name, such as `ci-server`, and an `ssh` target: `user@host` or an alias from `~/.ssh/config`. Press **Add**.

2. In **New session**, choose the machine in the **Machine** field.

The app opens `ssh -t <host>`, changes to the session’s folder, or to the home folder if it does not exist on the server, starts a login shell and runs the agent in it. The agent must be installed on the server. After a restart, an SSH session comes back as a new connection with a shell, without resuming the agent. OpenSSH handles the login, with keys in `ssh-agent` or `~/.ssh/config`; the app stores no passwords. A pane on a machine shows the machine in its header.

## Resume after restart

[Section titled “Resume after restart”](#resume-after-restart)

**Settings → Sessions & control → Restore sessions after restart** is on by default. Tabs, splits and panes return, and agents with a native session id continue their conversation. The details and the resume command of each agent are on [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/#resume-after-restart). Older sessions are in the [session history](/agent/session-history/).

## Broadcast

[Section titled “Broadcast”](#broadcast)

Tick the checkbox in the headers of several panes, type once in the field on the tab bar and send the same text to all of them. See [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/#broadcast).

## Handing off work

[Section titled “Handing off work”](#handing-off-work)

The hand-off button in a pane header passes the work to another agent through `STATE.md` or `handoff.md`. See [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/#handing-off-work).

## Agent panel

[Section titled “Agent panel”](#agent-panel)

The panel on the right, `⌘⇧A`, is a conversation with an agent over any view. See [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/#the-agent-panel).

Tip

Shortcuts on this site use `⌘`. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` instead. `Ctrl+B` never reaches the program in the terminal; if you use tmux in a pane, change its prefix.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)States, chat mode, resume, broadcast and hand-off.

[Workspaces](/agent/workspaces/)Tabs, splits, zoom and the sidebar.

[Editor and files](/agent/code/)The Code view with its terminal.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Sessions & control and the other sections.

# Appearance and themes

> Choose the theme mode, the day and night themes and the text size of Skribly Agent, and use themes from VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium or Open VSX.

The **Appearance** view sets how Skribly Agent looks: the theme mode (day, night, high contrast or follow the system), the text size and, if you want them, themes from your editor. One theme colours the interface, the code editor (syntax tokens) and the terminals. The built-in themes are the ones the Skribly sites use. A theme from VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium or Open VSX is an optional layer above them, off until you switch it on or pick one.

![The Appearance view: the day and night theme, text size, and theme cards from built-in, VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf themes](/_astro/agent-themes.C50hqJCr_Z2sedG8.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Appearance** at the bottom of the activity bar on the left (the palette icon), or
* open **Settings → Appearance and tour** and press **Choose themes**, or
* open the theme menu in the title bar (the sun, moon or monitor icon) and choose **More themes (VS Code, Cursor)…**.

## Theme mode

[Section titled “Theme mode”](#theme-mode)

The mode says which theme is on. You can change it in **Settings → Appearance and tour**, in the **Appearance** view, in the title bar menu **Theme mode** and by clicking the theme pill at the right of the status bar, which goes through the modes in this order: Day, Night, High contrast, Follow the system. In **Follow the system** the pill shows `Auto` and the theme it picked now.

* Day

  ![The same Settings page in the day theme](/_astro/agent-theme-light.DHf2Spzw_5jLdj.webp)

  **Day** is always the light theme.

* Night

  ![Settings, Appearance and tour at night: theme mode Day, Night, High contrast or Follow the system, text size, interface language, day and night themes, and the tour buttons](/_astro/agent-settings.D_OQtHEz_ZEt1WI.webp)

  **Night** is always the dark theme.

* High contrast

  ![The same Settings page in the high contrast theme: black background, white text and yellow accents](/_astro/agent-theme-contrast.Cqqc4oyW_Z2p1HXS.webp)

  **High contrast** is black, white and yellow.

* Follow the system

  ![The same Settings page with Follow the system chosen, here showing the day theme](/_astro/agent-theme-system.BxYn1zVE_VAUam.webp)

  **Follow the system** takes day, night or high contrast from the system, including its increased contrast setting.

The Appearance view names the same four modes **System**, **Day**, **Night** and **Contrast**.

## How to choose a theme

[Section titled “How to choose a theme”](#how-to-choose-a-theme)

1. Open **Appearance**. The cards **Day theme** and **Night theme** show what is set now, and mark the one in use.

2. In the **Themes** tab, filter with **Search themes** or with the source buttons (**All**, then one for each source that has themes, such as **Built-in**, **VS Code** or **Cursor**). Day themes are under **Day**, dark ones under **Night**.

3. Click a card. It becomes the day or the night theme by its type, and a theme from an editor or Open VSX also switches on **Themes from editors and Open VSX**. In **Follow the system** mode, picking a theme of the other kind shows a message that says when it will appear.

4. Choosing **Skribly · High contrast** switches the mode to High contrast.

Press **Reload** to read the themes from your editors again.

## How to use a theme from Open VSX

[Section titled “How to use a theme from Open VSX”](#how-to-use-a-theme-from-open-vsx)

1. Open **Appearance** and the **Open VSX** tab.

2. Type a name such as `dracula`, `nord` or `github` and press **Search**. With no query you see the most downloaded themes.

3. Press **Get theme** next to an extension. Skribly downloads the package only from `open-vsx.org` and takes from it only JSON and Markdown files of up to 5 MB each.

4. Click a theme name on the card to use it.

## How to install an editor extension

[Section titled “How to install an editor extension”](#how-to-install-an-editor-extension)

1. Open **Appearance** and the **Extensions in editors** tab.

2. Under **Install an extension in the editor**, write the identifier as `publisher.name`, for example `dracula-theme.theme-dracula`. Shortcuts offer Dracula, One Dark Pro, GitHub Theme, Catppuccin and Tokyo Night.
