3. Choose VS Code, Cursor or Windsurf and press **Install**. Skribly runs the editor’s command with `--install-extension`. The command (`code`, `cursor` or `windsurf`) must be in `PATH` or in the standard application folder.

The list below shows the extensions installed in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium with their version and editor. **Themes only** keeps those that have themes.

## Options

[Section titled “Options”](#options)

| Option                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                          | Default                 |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Theme mode                           | **Day**, **Night**, **High contrast** or **Follow the system**                                                                                                        | Follow the system       |
| **Themes from editors and Open VSX** | The chosen day and night theme replaces the Skribly colours. Off: the built-in Skribly themes                                                                         | Off                     |
| **Day theme**                        | Used in Day mode, and when the system is light                                                                                                                        | **Skribly · Parchment** |
| **Night theme**                      | Used in Night mode, and when the system is dark                                                                                                                       | **Skribly · Ink**       |
| **Text size**                        | A slider from 12 (compact) to 16 (large) pixels for the interface, editor and terminals. Settings → Appearance and tour has minus and plus buttons for the same value | 13                      |

The built-in themes are **Skribly · Parchment** (light), **Skribly · Ink** (dark) and **Skribly · High contrast**. [Accessibility](/agent/accessibility/) has a separate text size in percent and a switch that shows the high contrast or the light theme over the chosen theme.

## Where themes come from

[Section titled “Where themes come from”](#where-themes-come-from)

| Source     | Location                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Built-in   | The three Skribly themes                                                                    |
| VS Code    | `~/.vscode/extensions`, `~/.vscode-insiders/extensions` and the themes bundled with the app |
| Cursor     | `~/.cursor/extensions` and the app’s themes                                                 |
| Windsurf   | `~/.windsurf/extensions` and the app’s themes                                               |
| VSCodium   | `~/.vscode-oss/extensions` and the app’s themes                                             |
| Downloaded | From Open VSX, saved in `themes/` in the data directory                                     |

Skribly reads only the theme JSON files listed in `contributes.themes` of an extension’s `package.json`, with `include`, comments and `package.nls.json` translations. It never runs code from an extension.

## Contrast rules

[Section titled “Contrast rules”](#contrast-rules)

Many themes have a pale accent colour. Skribly picks the accent so that it has at least 3:1 contrast against the background, and text on accent buttons at least 4.5:1, otherwise it uses white, black or a colour of the theme. This way no theme gives unreadable buttons. With **High contrast** over an imported theme, each foreground moves towards black or white only as far as it needs to, so the theme stays recognisable.

The Skribly Agent mark in the title bar and the About box is the exception: it always keeps the product’s own orange, and at least 3:1 contrast against the built-in surfaces.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

Settings written by older versions move over on the first start: Day, Night and System stay as they were, high contrast becomes the High contrast mode, and a chosen editor theme turns the optional layer on.

* Themes are read only as JSON, so a theme can never run code on your computer.
* With **No network calls by the app** on, the Open VSX search and downloads report that the network is switched off; the themes you already have keep working.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Accessibility](/agent/accessibility/)Text size in percent, display modes, reading options and focus.

[Languages](/agent/languages/)The interface language and online translation.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Every section of Settings and its defaults.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What Open VSX and other downloads connect to.

# Token saving

> How agent-skills keeps the text that goes through the model small - loading on demand, scripts for mechanical work, asking before expensive actions, cheap restarts and working rules - with measured numbers.

Usage limits depend on how much text goes through the model. agent-skills keeps that small in five ways. The numbers below were measured on real projects by the agent-skills authors.

## Load on demand

[Section titled “Load on demand”](#load-on-demand)

An agent keeps only each skill’s name and description in context. The full `SKILL.md` loads when the skill runs, and reference files only when a step needs them. Every `SKILL.md` is at most 110 lines, and a check of the repository’s CI enforces it. Always-loaded files such as `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` stay short pointers to `.docs/`.

## Scripts do the mechanical work

[Section titled “Scripts do the mechanical work”](#scripts-do-the-mechanical-work)

Fetching, parsing, counting and filtering are done by scripts that print only what the model needs. Sizes are in bytes, and four bytes are roughly one token.

| Task                                          | Raw input | Script output | Saved |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------- | ----- |
| Lighthouse report                             | 455,534   | 754           | 99.8% |
| Test log of 86 passing tests                  | 27,098    | 86            | 99.7% |
| `npm audit --json` on a 300-package app       | 20,555    | 2,126         | 90%   |
| `git log -60` to learn the commit style       | 7,415     | 739           | 90%   |
| GitHub issue and comments                     | 8,178     | 1,018         | 88%   |
| SQL log of one request with an N+1            | 4,204     | 490           | 88%   |
| `package.json` to find test and lint commands | 2,122     | 275           | 87%   |

Fetching a task again prints only new comments and changed fields. Failing test runs print the failing blocks with `file:line` and a summary, never the full log.

## Ask before expensive actions

[Section titled “Ask before expensive actions”](#ask-before-expensive-actions)

A screenshot costs about 1,000 to 2,000 tokens, so `browser-check` asks first and captures only the changed element. Local Lighthouse, full test suites and load tests are proposed, not run silently.

## Sessions that restart cheaply

[Section titled “Sessions that restart cheaply”](#sessions-that-restart-cheaply)

`STATE.md`, about 30 lines long, holds the goal, what was done, changed files, check results, decisions and one concrete next step. It lives in `.tasks/<id>/`, outside git. After a stage, clear the session (`/clear` in Claude Code, `/new` in Codex, or a new chat) and resume from the file. It is cheaper and more precise than dragging a long transcript along or relying on automatic compaction. Change the model or the effort only between stages, so the prompt cache stays warm.

## Working rules

[Section titled “Working rules”](#working-rules)

The `token-saver` skill gives every agent the same habits:

* Search before reading, and read line ranges.
* Never open lockfiles or build output.
* Use short command forms, such as `git status --short`.
* Edit instead of rewriting.
* Put results first in answers.
* Use subagents with narrow briefs for wide searches.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Skills](/agent/skills/)Install the skills in a project from Skribly Agent.

[Token use](/agent/usage/)The board of tokens per agent and project, and what can be measured.

[Skills catalog](/skills/catalog/)All skills of agent-skills.

[Install agent-skills](/skills/install/)Set up the skills without the app.

# Troubleshooting

> Fixes for the most common Skribly Agent problems - agent detection, terminals, unsigned builds, Linux sandboxing, trackers, worktrees, hooks and audits.

Find the symptom, then follow the steps under it. If nothing here helps, the last section says what to collect before you report the problem.

## An agent is not detected

[Section titled “An agent is not detected”](#an-agent-is-not-detected)

**Symptom:** in **Settings → Agents** the agent shows “not installed”, even though it works in your terminal.

1. Click **Detect again**; the list is cached for five minutes.
2. Check where the agent is: `which claude` (Windows: `where claude`). Skribly searches the `PATH` of your login shell, plus `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`.
3. If you add the agent’s folder to `PATH` only inside a block for interactive shells, or in a file the login shell does not read, move it to `~/.zprofile` or `~/.bash_profile`.
4. A shell that takes more than five seconds to start cannot return its environment in time. Speed it up, or link the agent into `~/.local/bin`.
5. On Windows, Skribly does not read the shell; the agent must be in the system `PATH`. Restart Skribly after an npm install.
6. Restart Skribly after any change to `PATH`; the environment is read once at startup.

## Claude Code only in the VS Code extension

[Section titled “Claude Code only in the VS Code extension”](#claude-code-only-in-the-vs-code-extension)

Skribly finds the Claude Code binary from the VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium extensions, from `~/.claude/local`, from `~/.local/bin` and, on macOS, from the Claude app. If it does not, open the editor once after updating the extension so it unpacks the binary, or install the CLI with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Claude plugins need a working `claude`.

## A terminal does not open

[Section titled “A terminal does not open”](#a-terminal-does-not-open)

**Symptom:** **New session** fails with an error about `pty.node`, `node-pty` or `posix_spawnp failed`.

* Check that `$SHELL` points to an existing file. Skribly runs `$SHELL` (by default `/bin/zsh` on macOS, `/bin/bash` on Linux), and `pwsh` or `powershell.exe` on Windows.
* **First characters disappear:** the agent command is typed 400 ms after the shell starts, and a very slow prompt can lose it. Start the agent by hand in the pane, or speed up the shell.

## `Ctrl+B` does not reach the program in the terminal

[Section titled “Ctrl+B does not reach the program in the terminal”](#ctrlb-does-not-reach-the-program-in-the-terminal)

That is intentional: `Ctrl+B` is the pane prefix. Change the prefix in tmux or the shortcut in your program. See [Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/).

## An agent shows the wrong state

[Section titled “An agent shows the wrong state”](#an-agent-shows-the-wrong-state)

Click the state badge in the pane. **Why this state?** shows the source, the rule and the screen. A program that keeps redrawing, like a clock or a progress bar, shows as *working*.

## macOS: “can’t be opened” or “is damaged”

[Section titled “macOS: “can’t be opened” or “is damaged””](#macos-cant-be-opened-or-is-damaged)

The app is not signed or notarised. Use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, or:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Skribly Agent.app"
```

## Windows: SmartScreen

[Section titled “Windows: SmartScreen”](#windows-smartscreen)

“Windows protected your PC” → **More info → Run anyway**. Antivirus software can also slow down the first terminal launch.

## Linux: AppImage and sandbox

[Section titled “Linux: AppImage and sandbox”](#linux-appimage-and-sandbox)

* **Does not start:** `chmod +x Skribly-*.AppImage`.
* **`libfuse.so.2: cannot open`:** install FUSE 2 (`sudo apt install libfuse2`, or `libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04), or run `./Skribly-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run`.
* **“The SUID sandbox helper binary was found, but is not configured correctly”**, or a user namespaces error on Ubuntu 23.10+ with AppArmor: install the `.deb` package, or as a workaround run with `--no-sandbox`, which weakens isolation.
* **Tokens do not survive a restart:** there is no keyring (gnome-keyring or KWallet), so Skribly keeps tokens in memory only. Install and unlock a keyring.

## The browser port is in use

[Section titled “The browser port is in use”](#the-browser-port-is-in-use)

**Symptom:** after turning on **Share browser with agents** and restarting, the status bar does not show it, or the agent connects to another Chrome.

1. Find who uses the port: `lsof -i :9333` (macOS, Linux) or `netstat -ano | findstr 9333` (Windows).
2. Change the port in **Settings → Browser for agents → Port**.
3. Restart Skribly and update the address in the agent’s MCP configuration.

## A tracker returns 401 or 403

[Section titled “A tracker returns 401 or 403”](#a-tracker-returns-401-or-403)

| Tracker                   | Check                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Tracker           | The token has the `write` ability if you change issues, and it has not expired                       |
| Jira Cloud                | The account e-mail is filled in, and the token is an API token from id.atlassian.com, not a password |
| Jira Server / Data Center | The e-mail is empty, and the token is a Personal Access Token                                        |
| Redmine                   | The administrator enabled the REST API; the key is from **My account → API access key**              |
| GitHub                    | The fine-grained token has Issues access to the right repositories and the organisation approved it  |
| GitLab                    | The token has the `read_api` scope and has not expired                                               |
| Linear                    | It is a personal API key, not OAuth                                                                  |

“Not found (HTTP 404)” usually means a wrong address, such as Redmine with `/issues` at the end, or a GitHub or GitLab key without the repository (`owner/repo#123`).

## Git refuses to remove a worktree

[Section titled “Git refuses to remove a worktree”](#git-refuses-to-remove-a-worktree)

“contains modified or untracked files”: the worktree has uncommitted changes, and Skribly asks whether to force it. To keep them, commit or `git stash` first. The branch stays either way. “is locked”: run `git worktree unlock <path>`. “is not a working tree”: the folder was deleted by hand; `git worktree prune` cleans up.

## The task branch was not created

[Section titled “The task branch was not created”](#the-task-branch-was-not-created)

**Start with an agent** creates a branch only in a clean repository; untracked files do not matter. Commit or stash, then start again. `TASK.md` and `STATE.md` are created anyway.

## The hook without AI trailers does nothing

[Section titled “The hook without AI trailers does nothing”](#the-hook-without-ai-trailers-does-nothing)

* The repository uses `core.hooksPath` (husky, lefthook), so git does not read `.git/hooks`. Add the clean-up to your own `commit-msg` hook.
* A commit with `--no-verify` skips hooks.

## The Agent button for commits is disabled

[Section titled “The Agent button for commits is disabled”](#the-agent-button-for-commits-is-disabled)

It needs staged files and an agent with a headless mode: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, Copilot or Aider.

## A WCAG or SEO audit says the page did not load within 30 seconds

[Section titled “A WCAG or SEO audit says the page did not load within 30 seconds”](#a-wcag-or-seo-audit-says-the-page-did-not-load-within-30-seconds)

Start the project’s dev server and check the address, which defaults to **Settings → Projects → Dev-mode app URL**. A page behind a login shows the login screen, because the audit runs in a separate, empty session.

## Skills do not download

[Section titled “Skills do not download”](#skills-do-not-download)

Check that `git` is in `PATH`, the network, and the address in **Settings → Skills repository**. An SSH address needs a key in `ssh-agent`.

## The skribly command or the MCP server cannot connect

[Section titled “The skribly command or the MCP server cannot connect”](#the-skribly-command-or-the-mcp-server-cannot-connect)

**Symptom:** `skribly` exits with code `2`, or an agent says the Skribly MCP server has no connection.

1. Start Skribly Agent. The command and the server work only while the app runs.
2. Open **Settings → Sessions & control** and check that **Local control API** is on and shows a port.
3. If you moved the control file, check that the `SKRIBLY_CONTROL` variable points to it. By default it is `~/.skribly/control.json`.
4. A tool that changes something fails when you press **Deny** or close the question. That is intended. See [The Skribly MCP server](/agent/skribly-mcp/).

## The command guard writes nothing or an agent still asks

[Section titled “The command guard writes nothing or an agent still asks”](#the-command-guard-writes-nothing-or-an-agent-still-asks)

* The guard is off until you turn it on in **Settings → Command guard** and confirm the list of files.
* It supports Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode only.
* Without `node` in the `PATH`, Skribly writes the declarative rules of Claude Code and leaves out the hook; the section says so.
* Some commands always ask, whatever you tick: deleting files, discarding git changes, rewriting history and the other items of **Always ask**.
* A script run from a file, such as `python cleanup.py`, cannot be seen by the guard.

## A cost shows no price or an asterisk

[Section titled “A cost shows no price or an asterisk”](#a-cost-shows-no-price-or-an-asterisk)

* A model that is not in the price table has no price, and the interface says so instead of guessing. Add the model with the names it has in your session files in **Settings → Cost → Model prices**.
* An amount with an asterisk has some tokens without a price.
* An agent that leaves no token numbers in its session files has no cost.
* With a subscription switched on, the amount is an API equivalent, not what you pay.

## No notifications appear

[Section titled “No notifications appear”](#no-notifications-appear)

1. In **Settings → Editor & notifications**, check that **Notifications** is on.
2. A notification appears only when you are not looking at the session: the window is in the background or its pane is not on screen.
3. Check **Muted agents** and **Muted projects**. Muted sessions still reach the attention inbox.
4. Check that the system allows notifications from Skribly Agent.

## Updates are not checked

[Section titled “Updates are not checked”](#updates-are-not-checked)

When **Settings → Privacy and network → No network calls by the app** is on, no check is made and the update page says so. Turn it off, then use **Check for updates** in **Settings → Updates**.

## Still stuck

[Section titled “Still stuck”](#still-stuck)

* Find the data directory in **Settings → Updates → Data directory → Show**.
* Starting the app from a terminal shows errors from the main process. On macOS: `"/Applications/Skribly Agent.app/Contents/MacOS/Skribly Agent"`.
* Report the problem with the version from **Help → About** and your system, as described in [Security](/security/) for anything sensitive.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Frequently asked questions](/agent/faq/)Short answers about the Agent.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Every option and its default.

[Install](/agent/install/)Unsigned builds and the first start on each system.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What the app stores and which connections it makes.

# Updates

> How Skribly Agent updates itself on macOS, Windows and Linux, what Check for updates and Update automatically do, how versions are numbered and what changed from the former name.

Skribly Agent updates itself from a public release home that holds only installers and is read with no token. It checks at startup and every four hours, downloads a new version in the background and installs it when you restart or quit. To install it for the first time, use [the download page](https://agent.skribly.pl/download/).

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Open **Settings** and choose **Updates**, or
* click **Check for updates** in the tray or menu bar menu.

The page shows the version, the system and the architecture, **Check for updates**, the download progress, the **Update automatically** switch and the [data directory](/agent/settings/#data-directory).

## How to check for an update now

[Section titled “How to check for an update now”](#how-to-check-for-an-update-now)

1. Open **Settings → Updates**.

2. Press **Check for updates**. The line under it says what happened: checking, a new version is available, downloading with the percent, ready, or **You have the latest version.**

3. When the new version is ready, press **Restart and install** with its number, or click **Version … ready — restart** in the status bar. Without a click the update is installed when you quit the app.

## How auto-update works

[Section titled “How auto-update works”](#how-auto-update-works)

| When                                              | What happens                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 8 seconds after startup                           | The first check, in an installed app with **Update automatically** on                                                               |
| Every 4 hours                                     | Another check                                                                                                                       |
| New version available                             | Background download; the status bar shows **Downloading \<version> N%**                                                             |
| Downloaded                                        | The status bar shows **Version \<version> ready — restart**. Click it to install and restart, or the update installs when you quit. |
| Update refused for its signature (Windows, Linux) | The status bar offers **New version available** as a download link instead                                                          |
| Error                                             | A message in **Settings → Updates**                                                                                                 |

**Check for updates** works also when **Update automatically** is off. In a development build the check answers that updates work in the built app.

| System  | What is downloaded                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS   | The `-mac.zip` package of your architecture. The app is not signed, so Skribly checks the SHA-512 sum itself and swaps the app in after it quits. The downloaded package is removed afterwards. |
| Windows | The NSIS installer. The portable build does not update itself. An update keeps the `skribly` command, the link handlers and your data folder.                                                   |
| Linux   | The AppImage, or the `.deb` or `.rpm` package it was installed from. A package update asks for the administrator password once and keeps the `skribly-agent` command.                           |

## Options

[Section titled “Options”](#options)

| Option                   | What it does                                                                                       | Default                                                          |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Check for updates**    | Checks now and shows the result in the line below it                                               | Not checked in this session until you press it or the timer runs |
| **Update automatically** | Checks 8 seconds after startup and every 4 hours, downloads in the background and installs on quit | On                                                               |

When **No network calls by the app** is on in [Privacy and network](/agent/data-and-network/), no check is made and the page says that the network is switched off.

## Versions

[Section titled “Versions”](#versions)

A release is built only from a tag `v<version>` on `main` that equals the version in `package.json`. The first release made this way is 1.1.0; versions before it were numbered `1.0.<build number>`.

Caution

Skribly 1.0.x read a former private feed. Install 1.1.0 once by hand from [the download page](https://agent.skribly.pl/download/); later versions arrive by themselves. The **GitHub token (private repository)** field of **Settings → Updates** is gone, and a token saved there is deleted from the app’s secret store at the next start.

## Release files

[Section titled “Release files”](#release-files)

| System  | Files                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS   | `Skribly-mac-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon), `Skribly-mac-x64.dmg` (Intel)                                                     |
| Windows | `Skribly-Setup.exe` (x64 and ARM64 in one), `Skribly-Setup-x64.exe`, `Skribly-Setup-arm64.exe`, `Skribly-Portable-x64.exe` |
| Linux   | `Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage`, `Skribly-linux-amd64.deb`, `Skribly-linux-x86_64.rpm`                                     |

These fixed names always give the newest version. Every release also has a `SHA256SUMS.txt` and notes that say how to open the unsigned app on macOS and Windows and how to check the sums. Every packaged app is smoke-tested before it is published, and installed apps see a release only once it has the files of every system.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

* Turn off **Update automatically** if you want to choose when to update, and press **Check for updates** yourself.
* What an install, an update and an uninstall leave on each system is on [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/#what-an-uninstall-leaves).
* When an update fails, see [Troubleshooting](/agent/troubleshooting/).

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Install](/agent/install/)Install Skribly Agent on macOS, Windows or Linux.

[Settings](/agent/settings/)Every section of Settings and its defaults.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What the app stores, connects to and leaves behind.

[Troubleshooting](/agent/troubleshooting/)Fixes for the problems people meet most.

# Token use board

> The token use board of Skribly Agent shows tokens per day, agent and project for 7, 14 or 30 days, read from the session files your agents leave on this computer.

The token use board shows how many tokens your coding agents used, per day, agent and project, for the last 7, 14 or 30 days. It reads only the session files that the agents already leave on this computer. It needs no account and sends nothing anywhere.

![The Token use board for 14 days: tokens per agent and project in input, output, cache write and cache read, and what can be measured for each agent](/_astro/agent-usage-board.DoNdxhYp_Z1tdjQV.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

The board is a window that opens from the Dashboard.

1. Open the **Dashboard** (the first view of the activity bar, `⌘1`; on Windows and Linux `Ctrl+1`).

2. In the token chart press **Board**. The window **Token use** opens.

3. Choose the period. The first read of 30 days takes a few seconds; later reads read only what was appended.

The board reads files only while it is open, when you change the period and when you press **Refresh**. It has no timer, so a closed board or a hidden window never reads anything. The index the board builds is dropped from memory five minutes after the last request.

## How to read the table

[Section titled “How to read the table”](#how-to-read-the-table)

* **Period** is 7, 14 or 30 days. The default is 14. The line under the controls gives the dates and your time zone: days follow your local time.
* **Rows:** **Day**, **Agent** and **Project** switch the dimensions of the rows. Rows are added up over the dimensions that are off, and at least one stays on. By default the rows are by agent and project.
* **Input**, **Output**, **Cache write** and **Cache read** are always shown apart. Cache read is usually far larger than the rest.
* **Total** sums only the kinds ticked in the line **The Total column adds up**, and the line above the table names them. By default it sums input, output and cache write; cache read is off.
* **A dash** means the agent does not report that kind. It is not a zero, and in the CSV that cell is empty.
* **Project** is the folder the session ran in, as the agent’s own file records it. A folder inside a project you added to Skribly Agent is shown under that project’s name. Other folders, also worktrees outside the project, are shown by their folder name. A file with no folder shows **No folder in the session file**.

Your choices of period, rows and kinds are remembered.

## What each agent’s files allow

[Section titled “What each agent’s files allow”](#what-each-agents-files-allow)

The second table, **What can be measured for each agent**, says for every agent the app knows what its files hold. Nothing is guessed.

| State                         | Meaning                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Measured**                  | The files carry token numbers, and at least one record fell in the period. The table shows how many files and records |
| **No records in this period** | The files are read, but nothing was recorded in the period. There is no row and no zero                               |
| **No data**                   | The agent leaves no token numbers in its files, or has not been checked. No number is shown, not even a zero          |

| Agent                                                                              | Files read                                                                                        | Counted                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code                                                                        | `.jsonl` files under `~/.claude/projects` (or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), at any depth, with sub-agents | Input, output, cache write and cache read of each reply; each reply once                                                                                                          |
| Codex                                                                              | `.jsonl` files under `~/.codex/sessions` and `archived_sessions` (or `CODEX_HOME`)                | Running totals of input, output and cache read; a day gets the difference between totals. The cache write field was always 0 in the files that were checked, so it is not counted |
| Copilot CLI                                                                        | `events.jsonl` under `~/.copilot/session-state` (or `COPILOT_HOME`)                               | Input, output, cache write and cache read of each request. Its input contains the cache counts, so the board splits them out                                                      |
| Cursor Agent                                                                       | Checked: its files hold no token numbers                                                          | **No data**                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Aider, Amp, Factory Droid, Qwen Code, Goose, Crush, Kimi CLI | Not checked                                                                                       | **No data**, with the note **Not checked**                                                                                                                                        |

## How to save the table

[Section titled “How to save the table”](#how-to-save-the-table)

Press **Save CSV**. A save dialog opens, and the file holds the rows you see, in the order you see them. The columns are `date`, `agent` and `project` (only the dimensions that are on), then `input`, `output`, `cache_write`, `cache_read` and a total column whose name lists the kinds it sums, for example `total_input_plus_output_plus_cache_write`.

The file is UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so a spreadsheet reads Polish letters correctly. A text cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading `'`, so a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula. **Save CSV** is off when the table is empty.

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

Switch **Day** on to see which days were heavy, then switch **Agent** off to compare days across all agents.

* A row with no data has no number, because a zero would look like a measurement.
* Hover a project name to see the full folder path.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Token saving](/agent/token-saving/)How Skribly Agent keeps prompts short.

[Supported agents](/agent/agents/)The agents the app knows.

[Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/)What the app reads and sends.

# Workspaces and panes

> How the Agents view of Skribly Agent is organised: workspaces, tabs, splits and panes, the workspace sidebar, zoom, dragging, the Herdr tab and a worktree per agent.

The **Agents** view works like a terminal multiplexer built for agents: workspaces, then tabs, then splits, then panes. Each pane is a terminal or a chat with an agent. You use it to run several agents side by side and to see at a glance which one needs you.

![The Agents view: the workspace sidebar with three projects and their worktrees, and a Claude Code pane that reviews a diff and lists accessibility issues](/_astro/agent-agents.C2sSCdmD_ZOVEKt.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Agents** in the activity bar on the left, or press `⌘2`, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Agents**.

Shortcuts on this site use `⌘`. On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` instead. The pane shortcuts start with the prefix `Ctrl+B` on every system.

## The layout model

[Section titled “The layout model”](#the-layout-model)

| Level         | What it is                               | Where it comes from                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Workspace** | A project folder or one of its worktrees | A pane belongs to the workspace whose path matches its folder best. Sessions outside any project land in **Other directories**. |
| **Tab**       | A set of panes in one workspace          | **+** on the tab bar, `Ctrl+B c` or `⌘T`. Double-click a tab to rename it.                                                      |
| **Split**     | A tree of horizontal and vertical splits | **New session to the right** and **New session below** in a pane header, `Ctrl+B v` and `Ctrl+B -`, or `⌘D` and `⌘⇧D` on macOS. |
| **Pane**      | An agent terminal, a shell or a chat     | **New session**, the split buttons, the `skribly` command, pipelines or tasks.                                                  |

Terminals live in the app’s main process, so switching views or tabs, or reloading the window, does not interrupt them. A reopened pane replays its last output. The layout, with its tabs, splits, sizes and active workspace, is saved continuously.

When a new session has no place given, it goes to the active tab of its workspace. Once a tab has three panes, the next session opens in a new tab so the panes do not get too narrow. Sessions started from outside, by the `skribly` command, pipelines or tasks, also get a place, and the panes of closed sessions disappear by themselves.

## The workspace sidebar

[Section titled “The workspace sidebar”](#the-workspace-sidebar)

The **Workspaces** sidebar sits on the left of the view. Hide it with its button or `Ctrl+B b`; the button **Show areas** brings it back.

* One group per project, with its colour dot, collapsible with a click. In it, a **main** row and one row per worktree, named by its branch.
* Under each workspace, its sessions: the agent’s avatar, its name and its state. Click one to go to its pane; hover to peek at it.
* Next to a workspace, a dot with the most important state of its sessions and their number. The most important state is, in this order: waiting for a decision, done, working, starting, ready, finished.
* In the header, a button with the number of sessions waiting for you; it jumps to the next one (`Ctrl+B j`).
* **New worktree** (the **+** that appears on hover) next to a project, and the trash icon next to a worktree, which removes it and keeps its branch.

## How to work in tabs and splits

[Section titled “How to work in tabs and splits”](#how-to-work-in-tabs-and-splits)

1. Press **+** on the tab bar, or `Ctrl+B c`, for a new tab in the current workspace. Switch with a click, `Ctrl+B n` and `Ctrl+B p`, or `Ctrl+B` and the tab number.

2. Split a pane with the split buttons in its header or `Ctrl+B v` and `Ctrl+B -`. A new split starts a shell in the pane’s folder; **New session** next to it starts an agent.

3. Drag a divider between panes to resize them. A pane keeps at least 8 percent of its split.

4. Zoom the active pane with the maximize button or `Ctrl+B z`. The same shortcut restores it.

5. Move between panes with `Ctrl+B` and the arrow keys. Close the active pane with `Ctrl+B x`; for an agent that is working or waiting, the app asks first.

Closing a tab closes all of its sessions, after a confirmation that says how many still work. The full list of prefix keys is on [Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/).

## What is in a pane header

[Section titled “What is in a pane header”](#what-is-in-a-pane-header)

| Element                         | Action                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Checkbox                        | Selects the pane for [broadcast](/agent/terminals/#broadcast)                                  |
| Avatar and title                | Double-click to rename (`Enter` saves, `Esc` cancels)                                          |
| `@name`                         | The session’s name for the `skribly` command and MCP                                           |
| Branch                          | The session works in a separate worktree                                                       |
| Machine                         | The session runs on an SSH machine                                                             |
| **resumed**                     | The pane was restored after a restart                                                          |
| State badge                     | Opens **Why this state?**, described on [Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/#why-this-state) |
| Hand-off                        | [Hands the work to another agent](/agent/terminals/#handing-off-work)                          |
| New session to the right, below | Opens **New session** next to this pane                                                        |
| Maximize                        | The same as `Ctrl+B z`                                                                         |
| Close                           | Asks first when the agent is working or waiting                                                |

## The Herdr tab

[Section titled “The Herdr tab”](#the-herdr-tab)

If you also use [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), the **Herdr** button in the tab bar shows its workspaces and the agents in them, each with its state: working, waiting for a person, done or ready. A button on a workspace or an agent shows it in Herdr, and the field under an agent, **Send a prompt to the agent…**, sends it a prompt.

![The Herdr tab of the Agents view: two Herdr workspaces with their agents, states and a prompt field for each agent](/_astro/agent-herdr.CZ23-Rlw_Z1doXW5.webp)

The panel reads Herdr through its command line every few seconds, only while it is open and the window is visible. It never starts, stops or attaches a Herdr server. When the `herdr` command is missing, its server is not running, it has no workspaces or its answer cannot be read, the panel says so in a short empty state. Herdr refuses a prompt for an agent that waits for a decision, and the message is shown as it comes. Herdr sessions are not in the [attention inbox](/agent/inbox/).

## A worktree per agent

[Section titled “A worktree per agent”](#a-worktree-per-agent)

A worktree is a separate folder with the same git history, so two agents in two worktrees do not overwrite each other’s files. Choose **+ New worktree…** as the **Working copy** of **New session**, or press **New worktree** next to a project in the sidebar, then give a branch and a base. The worktree appears as its own workspace. Creating, listing and removing worktrees is on [Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/).

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Tip

`Ctrl+B` never reaches the program in the terminal. If you use tmux in a pane, or a `Ctrl+B` shortcut in your shell, change the prefix in that program.

* The prefix stays active for 2 seconds, and a **Ctrl+B…** badge pulses on the tab bar. Press `Ctrl+B` again to cancel it. Pane shortcuts do not work while a dialog or the palette is open.
* Press `Ctrl+B o` for the **Agent overview**, a grid of previews of all sessions with the ones that need you first.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Agents and sessions](/agent/sessions/)New session, states, the agent panel and chat mode.

[Terminals](/agent/terminals/)Shell panes, the Code view terminal and SSH machines.

[Worktrees](/agent/worktrees/)All worktrees of your projects and their state.

[Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/)The Ctrl+B prefix and every global shortcut.

# Worktrees

> The Worktrees view of Skribly Agent lists every git worktree of your projects with its state, shows which can go, and removes a worktree only when that is safe.

A worktree is a separate folder with its own checked-out branch and the same git history, so several agents can work in parallel without touching each other’s files. When you run many agents, worktrees pile up. The **Worktrees** view lists every worktree of every project of the app in one place: which are still in use, which hold work that is saved nowhere else, and which can go.

![The Worktrees view: worktrees of two projects with branch, state, distance to upstream and main, the pane working in each, and one opened with Show in the Code view, Start an agent here, Copy path and Remove worktree](/_astro/agent-worktrees.D1C3TMa1_ZnpVgq.webp)

## Open the view

[Section titled “Open the view”](#open-the-view)

* Click **Worktrees** (the folder with a branch) in the activity bar, or
* open the command palette (`⌘K`) and choose **Worktrees**.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` wherever this page says `⌘`. The view has no number shortcut. It reads the worktrees when it opens and when you press **Refresh**, never on a timer. It runs only local `git` commands in your project folders and makes no network call.

## What a row shows

[Section titled “What a row shows”](#what-a-row-shows)

Rows are grouped by project. Each row is one entry of `git worktree list`.

| Part                       | What it means                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Branch and folder          | The checked-out branch (or the commit, for a detached HEAD) and the folder, with your home folder shortened to `~`                              |
| **Main folder**            | The project’s own folder, its main working tree                                                                                                 |
| **Detached HEAD**          | The tree is on a commit, not on a branch                                                                                                        |
| **Clean** or **3 changes** | Changed, staged and untracked files, counted by git. **State unknown** when git could not read the tree                                         |
| **Merged into main**       | The tree’s HEAD is contained in the project’s main branch: the **Base branch** of the project, or `main` when none is set, local or on `origin` |
| `↑2 ↓0 origin/feature/x`   | Commits ahead of and behind the upstream. **No upstream** when the branch tracks nothing                                                        |
| `↑4 ↓1 main`               | Commits ahead of and behind the project’s main branch                                                                                           |
| **Locked**                 | The tree is locked with `git worktree lock`                                                                                                     |
| **Folder is gone**         | Git still lists the tree, but its folder does not exist                                                                                         |
| Agent badge                | A pane of the app whose folder is this tree or a folder inside it. Ended panes and panes on another machine are not counted                     |
| Last line                  | The subject of the last commit and how long ago it was made                                                                                     |

Above the list, a line counts the worktrees, those with changes and those that can be removed.

## How to find a worktree

[Section titled “How to find a worktree”](#how-to-find-a-worktree)

1. Pick a filter: **All**, **With changes**, **Merged** or **No agent**. **With changes** also lists trees whose state is unknown.

2. Type in **Search branch, folder, commit…**. The search looks in the branch, the folder, the project name, the subject of the last commit and the pane names.

## How to work in a worktree

[Section titled “How to work in a worktree”](#how-to-work-in-a-worktree)

1. Click a row, or press `Enter` or `Space` on it. It opens and shows its actions.

2. Press **Show in the Code view** to open the tree in [Code & git](/agent/code/). The main folder switches the open project. A linked worktree is added to your projects the first time and opened.

3. Or press **Start an agent here**. The usual new-session dialog of the Agents view opens on this tree, so you pick the agent, the name and the first message as always.

4. **Copy path** puts the full folder path in the clipboard.

## How to remove a worktree

[Section titled “How to remove a worktree”](#how-to-remove-a-worktree)

1. Open the row. If removal is possible, **Remove worktree…** is there. If not, the row says **Removal not available:** and lists what is in the way.

2. Press **Remove worktree…**. The dialog **Remove the worktree?** names the folder and the branch.

3. Press **Remove worktree**. The app reads the list and the tree again, checks every rule once more, and runs `git worktree remove` without `--force`.

Removal is offered only when all of these hold:

* the tree is not the project’s main folder, it is not locked, and its folder exists;
* it has no changed, staged or untracked file;
* its branch is merged into the main branch, or it is pushed with nothing left to push (a detached HEAD must be merged);
* no pane of the app works in it or in a folder inside it.

The branch and its commits always stay: **Worktree removed. The branch stays.** Nothing else is pruned.

## Where new worktrees go

[Section titled “Where new worktrees go”](#where-new-worktrees-go)

You create a worktree in the Agents view (**+ New worktree…**) or by starting a task with an agent in its own worktree. The app makes it under `~/.skribly/worktrees/<repository>/<branch>`. To use another folder, open **Settings**, go to **Sessions & control** and set **Worktree directory**. An empty field means the default. Worktrees made earlier stay where they are.

## Keyboard

[Section titled “Keyboard”](#keyboard)

| Key                   | Action                                              |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `↑` `↓`, `Home` `End` | Move between rows                                   |
| `Enter`, `Space`      | Open or close a row                                 |
| `Tab`                 | Move into the actions of the open row               |
| `Esc`                 | Close the open row and return to it; close a dialog |

## Tips

[Section titled “Tips”](#tips)

Caution

A worktree that is not merged and not pushed holds work that exists nowhere else. The view will not offer to remove it. Merge or push first.

* Use **No agent** together with **Merged** to find the trees that are safe to clean up.
* A project’s **Base branch** decides what counts as merged. Set it in the project settings if your main branch is not `main`.

## Related pages

[Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages)

[Tasks and trackers](/agent/tasks/)Start with an agent can create a worktree for a task.

[Changes and commits](/agent/changes/)Push the branch of a worktree before you remove it.

[Terminals and sessions](/agent/terminals/)Sessions and the new-session dialog.

## How we work

[Section titled “How we work”](#how-we-work)

Every Skribly tool is built the same way: documented, accessible, tested, and meant to keep running after the demo. Commits follow Conventional Commits in English, without AI co-author trailers. The coding agents that work on the Skribly repositories use the shared [agent-skills](/skills/) for the task workflow, commits and reviews.

# Changelog

> What changed in Skribly Agent, Skribly Tracker, agent-skills and this documentation, in plain words, newest first.

What changed in each tool, rewritten in plain words from the release notes. Releases with no visible change are left out. A release is published when a version tag is pushed, with notes grouped from its commits.

## November 2026

[Section titled “November 2026”](#november-2026)

### Documentation, 20 November: cleaner skill pages and seven agents

[Section titled “Documentation, 20 November: cleaner skill pages and seven agents”](#documentation-20-november-cleaner-skill-pages-and-seven-agents)

* The skill pages show what a skill is not for as its own sentence, so cases such as “a Playwright spec” no longer appear among the requests that call the skill. The new `framework-guide` and `upgrade` skills have their pages, marked for the next release.
* [All rules](/skills/all-rules/) shows each rule id as text; the source of each rule keeps its link.
* The home page, the FAQ and the install page say seven agents, the number the released agent-skills 0.3.0 supports.

### Documentation, 20 November: every rule on one page

[Section titled “Documentation, 20 November: every rule on one page”](#documentation-20-november-every-rule-on-one-page)

* [All rules](/skills/all-rules/) lists the 98 rules of the agent-skills rule dictionary by technology, with the severity, the versions, whether a line check exists and the public source of each. The page is generated from the rule files, so it says what they say.

### Documentation, 20 November: the new workflow skills in the catalogue

[Section titled “Documentation, 20 November: the new workflow skills in the catalogue”](#documentation-20-november-the-new-workflow-skills-in-the-catalogue)

* The [skills catalogue](/skills/catalog/) lists the eleven workflow skills that ship in the next release, from `plan` and `verify` to `writing` and `tracker-write`, each with a link to its own page.
* The skill pages and the [token cost](/skills/token-cost/) table follow the latest wording of the skills.

### Documentation, 20 November: the rule dictionary and more agent-skills commands

[Section titled “Documentation, 20 November: the rule dictionary and more agent-skills commands”](#documentation-20-november-the-rule-dictionary-and-more-agent-skills-commands)

* A new page, [Rule dictionary](/skills/rules/), describes `agent-skills rules` and `rules --check`: the rules of each technology with a severity and a public source, and the line checks that report `file:line`, the rule and its source.
* [Agent tooling](/skills/tooling/) describes `init --mcp` (the official MCP server of each framework), the nightly report, the Dependabot preset and the `/upgrade` skill for major versions. All of them ship in the next release.
* The home page and the skills catalogue keep the released 39 skills and seven agents, the facts of agent-skills 0.3.0.

### Documentation, 19 November: the compatibility page

[Section titled “Documentation, 19 November: the compatibility page”](#documentation-19-november-the-compatibility-page)
