# Supported agents

> Where agent-skills installs skills for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin, and how you call them in each. Also the per-agent files that `agent-skills agent-files` generates from `AGENTS.md`.

Every supported agent reads native **Agent Skills** folders: `<name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` front matter, and optional `reference/`, `scripts/` and `templates/`. Seven of them read the same shared folder, `.agents/skills`, so one copy serves Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin. Claude Code reads only `.claude/skills`. Locations were checked against each vendor’s documentation on 29 October 2026, and those for Devin and for the project instruction files on 11 November 2026.

## Default format: `--format skills`

[Section titled “Default format: --format skills”](#default-format---format-skills)

| Agent          | Target     | Project scope (copy)                                       | User scope (symlink)                                                                                               | Invoke                                     |
| -------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Claude Code    | `claude`   | `.claude/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.claude/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `/task 123`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `codex`    | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `$task 123`, or pick from `/skills`        |
| Cursor         | `cursor`   | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `/task 123` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `gemini`   | `.agents/skills/<name>/` + `.gemini/commands/<name>.toml`  | `~/.agents/skills/<name>` + `~/.gemini/commands/<name>.toml`                                                       | `/task 123`                                |
| OpenCode       | `opencode` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` + `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`  | `~/.agents/skills/<name>` + `~/.config/opencode/commands/<name>.md`                                                | `/task 123`                                |
| Windsurf       | `windsurf` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` + `.windsurf/workflows/<name>.md` | `~/.agents/skills/<name>` + `~/.codeium/windsurf/global_workflows/<name>.md`                                       | `/task 123` or `@task`                     |
| GitHub Copilot | `copilot`  | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `/task 123` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `devin`    | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`; the Devin CLI also reads `~/.config/devin/skills` (on Windows `%APPDATA%\devin\skills`) | `@skills:task` in a prompt                 |

Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Windsurf load skills through a tool or an `@mention` rather than a slash command, so the installer also writes a thin command of a few lines: “use the `<name>` skill with these arguments”. It never duplicates the skill text, so `git pull` and `agent-skills sync` are enough to update.

## Classic format: `--format rules`

[Section titled “Classic format: --format rules”](#classic-format---format-rules)

For older agent versions:

| Target                     | Written                                                                              | Notes                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cursor`                   | `.cursor/rules/<name>.mdc` (“Agent Requested”)                                       | Project scope only                                                                           |
| `windsurf`                 | `.windsurf/rules/<name>.md` (`trigger: model_decision`)                              | Project scope only; the 12,000-character limit per file is checked                           |
| `copilot`                  | `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md`; user scope `~/.copilot/instructions/` | No `applyTo`, so it is not attached to every request                                         |
| `gemini`                   | `.gemini/commands/<name>.toml` with the whole skill inlined                          | `@{` and `!{` are neutralised so Gemini never injects files or runs commands from skill text |
| `opencode`                 | `.opencode/commands/<name>.md` with the whole skill inlined                          |                                                                                              |
| `claude`, `codex`, `devin` | Same as `skills`                                                                     | They have no other format                                                                    |

## Known overlaps

[Section titled “Known overlaps”](#known-overlaps)

* Cursor, OpenCode and Copilot also read `.claude/skills` at project scope. With Claude and one of those in the same project, a skill may show twice. Install Claude at user scope and the others at project scope, or the reverse.
* Codex still loads the deprecated `~/.codex/skills`. agent-skills never writes there, and `agent-skills doctor` warns when old copies shadow the new ones.

## Not fully verified

[Section titled “Not fully verified”](#not-fully-verified)

* **Windsurf** now prefers `.devin/{rules,workflows,skills}` and reads `.windsurf/*` as a fallback. agent-skills writes `.windsurf/*`, which works in both the old and the renamed app, and the shared `.agents/skills`.
* **Gemini CLI** restricts file tools to workspace folders. Skills linked at user scope are activated through `activate_skill`, which grants access to the skill folder.

## Project instruction files

[Section titled “Project instruction files”](#project-instruction-files)

A repository keeps its instructions for coding agents in one file, `AGENTS.md`. Codex, OpenCode and Devin read it themselves. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Copilot need a small file of their own, and `agent-skills agent-files` generates those files from `AGENTS.md`, so you never write them by hand:

```bash
cd ~/code/shop                      # a repository with an AGENTS.md
agent-skills agent-files            # write what is missing or out of date
agent-skills agent-files --check    # write nothing, exit 1 when a generated file is missing or differs
agent-skills doctor                 # each agent: configured or not for this repository
```

Run it again after a `git pull` of agent-skills (new skill versions) or after a change to the structure of `AGENTS.md`. The pointer files contain no instructions, so editing `AGENTS.md` itself needs no re-run. The generator covers seven agents: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Devin. Windsurf reads `.agents/skills` and `AGENTS.md` too, so a generated repository works there without an extra file.

| File                              | For                                                                | Contents                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CLAUDE.md`                       | Claude Code                                                        | A marker comment, then the one line `@AGENTS.md`                    |
| `GEMINI.md`                       | Gemini CLI                                                         | A marker comment, then `@./AGENTS.md`                               |
| `.cursor/rules/agents.mdc`        | Cursor                                                             | An always-applied rule that references `@AGENTS.md`                 |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | GitHub Copilot                                                     | A marker comment and a link to `../AGENTS.md`                       |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/`          | Claude Code                                                        | The skills, copied                                                  |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/`          | Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot, Devin (and Windsurf) | The same skills, once for all                                       |
| `.mcp.json`                       | Claude Code                                                        | `{ "mcpServers": {} }`: read-only defaults and an empty server list |
| `.skribly/agent-files.json`       | The command                                                        | What was generated; commit it with the other files                  |

Every text file starts with a comment that says it was generated by `agent-skills agent-files`. Claude Code strips that comment before it reads `CLAUDE.md`, so the agent still sees the single import line. `.mcp.json` never contains a token or a URL with credentials; servers are added by a person.

The command is safe to run again and again:

* **Twice is the same.** A second run changes nothing and prints `0 change(s)`; line endings do not matter.
* **Hand-written files are kept.** A `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, rule, instruction file or skill folder without the marker is reported and left alone, and the command exits 1. Move its content into `AGENTS.md` and delete it, or pass `--force`: the old file is saved as `<path>.bak-agent-skills` first.
* **Your own `.mcp.json` servers are kept.** `--force` leaves such a file alone; only `--force-mcp` replaces it, saving the old one as `.mcp.json.bak-agent-skills`. That backup may hold an `env` block with tokens, so delete it or ignore it before `git add`.
* **Your own skills are never touched.** Only folders named like an agent-skills skill are managed.
* **Everything stays inside the repository.** A link that points outside it is refused, reported and skipped; the command exits 1.
* **`--check` and `--dry-run` write nothing.** `--check` exits 1 when a generated file is missing, differs or has no marker, and is the gate to use in CI. `--skills a,b` limits which skills are copied, and `--json` prints a machine-readable report.

`agent-skills doctor` lists each of the seven agents as `configured` or `not configured` for the current repository, with the reason, for example `CLAUDE.md missing`. It reports; it does not change anything.

The generated files do not yet include the guard hook of each agent or the subagent roles of `.claude/agents/`.

## Agents in Skribly Agent

[Section titled “Agents in Skribly Agent”](#agents-in-skribly-agent)

Skribly Agent runs 13 agents, more than agent-skills supports. Aider, Amp, Factory Droid, Qwen Code, Goose, Crush and Kimi CLI run in Skribly but have no skill target. See [Supported agents in Skribly Agent](/agent/agents/).

# All rules

> Every rule of the agent-skills rule dictionary, by technology, with its severity, versions, line check and public source.

This page is generated from `rules.json` of [agent-skills](/skills/), so it says what the rule files say. The rule dictionary is in development and ships in the next release: 98 rules in 29 technologies, 58 of them with a line check that `agent-skills rules --check` runs on the project’s files. The rest are read by the agent while it works. How to list and check the rules: [Rule dictionary](/skills/rules/).

| `node/handle-rejections`      | Every promise is awaited or has a `.catch()`, because an unhandled rejection ends the process. | high     | any      | no         | [Node.js, the –unhandled-rejections flag](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--unhandled-rejectionsmode)          |
| `node/no-sync-io-in-handlers` | A request handler never calls a `*Sync` file, crypto or zlib function.                         | high     | any      | no         | [Node.js, Don’t block the event loop](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/dont-block-the-event-loop) |

## PHP

[Section titled “PHP”](#php)

| Rule                      | What it says                                                                   | Severity | Versions | Line check | Source                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | -------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `php/prepared-statements` | SQL never concatenates request values; it binds them with prepared statements. | critical | any      | yes        | [PHP manual, prepared statements and stored procedures](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo.prepared-statements.php)            |
| `php/strict-types`        | Every PHP file starts with `declare(strict_types=1);`.                         | medium   | any      | no         | [PHP manual, strict typing](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.declarations.php#language.types.declarations.strict) |

| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pydantic/field-validator`  | Pydantic 2 validators use `@field_validator` and `@model_validator`.                               | high     | 2+       | yes        | [Pydantic, migration guide to v2](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/) |
| `pydantic/model-config`     | Pydantic 2 models configure with `model_config = ConfigDict(...)`.                                 | high     | 2+       | yes        | [Pydantic, migration guide to v2](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/) |
| `pydantic/model-dump`       | Pydantic 2 code calls `model_dump`, `model_dump_json`, `model_validate` and `model_validate_json`. | high     | 2+       | yes        | [Pydantic, migration guide to v2](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/) |

| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `python/mutable-default-argument` | A function never uses a list, dict or set literal as a default argument value.                | high     | any      | yes        | [Python reference, function definitions](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/compound_stmts.html#function-definitions)       |
| `python/subprocess-no-shell`      | `subprocess` runs commands as an argument list, never with `shell=True` around outside input. | critical | any      | yes        | [Python docs, subprocess security considerations](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#security-considerations) |

| `rails/no-string-sql`   | Never put request values into an SQL string; pass them as hash or placeholder conditions. | critical | 7.0+     | yes        | [Rails guides: Active Record query interface](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_querying.html) |

| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `react/act-import`       | Tests import `act` from `react`, not `react-dom/test-utils`.                                  | low      | 19+      | yes        | [React 19 upgrade guide](https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide) |

| `react/ref-prop`         | A new React 19 function component takes `ref` as a prop instead of using `forwardRef`.        | medium   | 19+      | no         | [React 19 upgrade guide](https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide) |
| `react/removed-legacy`   | Code uses `useRef` or callback refs and `createContext`, never string refs or `contextTypes`. | high     | 19+      | yes        | [React 19 upgrade guide](https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide) |
| `react/use-action-state` | Form action state uses `useActionState` from `react`, not `useFormState` from `react-dom`.    | high     | 19+      | yes        | [React 19](https://react.dev/blog/2024/12/05/react-19)                             |

| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `sqlalchemy/typed-mapping`     | New SQLAlchemy 2 models use `Mapped[...]` with `mapped_column()` in a `DeclarativeBase` subclass, one style per module. | low      | 2.0+     | no         | [SQLAlchemy, migrating to 2.0](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/changelog/migration_20.html) |

## Vue

[Section titled “Vue”](#vue)

| Rule                     | What it says                                                                           | Severity | Versions | Line check | Source                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vue/create-app`         | A Vue 3 app is created with `createApp(App).mount()`, not `new Vue()`.                 | high     | 3+       | yes        | [Vue 3 migration guide, breaking changes](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/) |
| `vue/if-before-for`      | `v-if` and `v-for` are never on the same element.                                      | medium   | 3+       | yes        | [Vue 3 migration guide, breaking changes](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/) |
| `vue/listeners-in-attrs` | Listeners are read from `$attrs` and emitted events are declared in `emits`.           | low      | 3+       | yes        | [Vue 3 migration guide, breaking changes](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/) |
| `vue/model-props`        | `v-model` on a component uses `modelValue` and `update:modelValue`.                    | high     | 3+       | no         | [Vue 3 migration guide, breaking changes](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/) |
| `vue/no-event-bus`       | Components talk through props, emits, provide and inject or a store, not an event bus. | medium   | 3+       | yes        | [Vue 3 migration guide, breaking changes](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/) |
| `vue/no-filters`         | Templates format values with methods or computed values, not filters.                  | medium   | 3+       | yes        | [Vue 3 migration guide, breaking changes](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/) |

# Skills catalog

> The skills of agent-skills, grouped by job, with what each one does, when to use it and how to call it; each of the 39 also has its own page.

Invoke a skill as `/name` in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf and Copilot, `$name` in Codex, or `@skills:name` in a Devin prompt. You can also just describe what you want: agents pick skills by their description.

The machine-readable list is `skills.json` in the repository, validated against a JSON schema in CI.

## Workflow

[Section titled “Workflow”](#workflow)

| Skill         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Example                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `task`        | Takes a ticket or a sentence to an approved commit: fetches the issue with a script, writes a small or large analysis (`SPEC.md` for approval), branches after approval, works in stages with `STATE.md` updated after each, runs the checks and commits after your OK. Extras: `estimate`, `plan`, `pr` (pull request description) and `comment` (tracker comment). | `/task 482` · `$task SHOP-42` · `/task fix the date sorting` · `/task` to resume the current branch’s task |
| `project`     | Detects the stack, the install, dev, build, test, lint, typecheck and format commands, the commit style and language, the base branch, CI and containers into `.skribly/project.json`, which every skill reads first. Values set by hand are never overwritten, and a value deleted by hand stays deleted.                                                           | `/project` · `$project` · “which commands does this repo use?”                                             |
| `commit`      | Proposes a message in the project’s convention, detected from your own recent commits, and commits the listed files after you approve. Never adds trailers, never pushes.                                                                                                                                                                                            | `/commit` · “commit this as two commits”                                                                   |
| `handoff`     | Writes or reads `.tasks/<id>/STATE.md` so another agent or a fresh session continues without the transcript.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `/handoff` · `$handoff resume 482`                                                                         |
| `orchestrate` | Splits big work into independent sub-tasks with self-contained briefs and file ownership, runs them in parallel subagents or worktrees, then merges and verifies.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `/orchestrate migrate all forms to the new validation helper`                                              |
| `estimate`    | A read-only estimate: deliverables, optimistic, likely and pessimistic hours, a PERT total and range, assumptions, risks and open questions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `/estimate 482`                                                                                            |
| `plan-step`   | Writes or expands a plan work package in the exact shape the plan defines: headings in order, tasks with their files, what to do and a check, owner actions, verification, done-when and risks. Task ids and section references stay stable. It writes a plan; it does not run a step.                                                                               | `/plan-step` · “write the work package for F9” · “add a task to F5”                                        |
| `run-step`    | Carries out one work package task by task by the plan’s step protocol: a short branch from `develop` for each task, its check, a Conventional Commit with explicit paths, a merge with `--no-ff`, a push, then the tick. Actions that belong to the owner are recorded as blocked, never attempted.                                                                  | `/run-step` · “run step F5” · “do the next task of F5”                                                     |
| `release`     | Walks the plan’s release checklist and runs read-only checks before a release: `develop` clean, `package.json` and `VERSION` in step, a `CHANGELOG.md` entry present, the tag still free. It never bumps a version, tags, merges into `main` or publishes.                                                                                                           | `/release` · “is this ready to release?” · “run the weekly routine”                                        |

## Quality and tests

[Section titled “Quality and tests”](#quality-and-tests)

| Skill           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Example                                            |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `test-loop`     | Runs only the checks affected by the change, fixes in a capped loop of three attempts, condenses logs, never weakens tests.                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/test-loop` · “make CI green”                     |
| `backend-tests` | Writes and runs backend tests for changed code: pytest with Django and DRF, Laravel PHPUnit or Pest, Node with supertest, Go, Spring. Test database, factories, isolation, mocked HTTP, coverage of changed lines.                                                                                                                        | `/backend-tests` · “cover the new orders endpoint” |
| `api-tests`     | Contract and integration tests for REST and GraphQL from OpenAPI (Schemathesis, Dredd, Hurl, newman), auth flows and error cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                         | “check the API against openapi.yaml”               |
| `e2e-tests`     | Playwright specs for changed user flows; runs only affected specs, keeps traces, fixes flaky tests at the root cause.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `/e2e-tests` · “this spec fails on CI only”        |
| `load-test`     | k6, autocannon or Locust from smoke to load, stress and spike, with thresholds and condensed results.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `/load-test GET /api/orders at 20 users`           |
| `review`        | Self-review of the diff before a commit: findings first, with severity, `file:line` and a fix.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `/review` · `/review src/billing`                  |
| `debug`         | Reproduce, narrow down, prove the cause, make the smallest fix, and use the same reproduction as proof.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `/debug totals are wrong after applying a coupon`  |
| `refactor`      | Behaviour-preserving refactoring: characterisation tests first, then small verified steps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `/refactor split OrderService`                     |
| `db-migrations` | Zero-downtime migrations for Django, Laravel, Prisma, Alembic, Flyway and Rails, with a linter for locks and risks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | “is this migration safe?”                          |
| `i18n`          | Missing, empty and unused translation keys, placeholder mismatches, keys used in code but missing, and string extraction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `/i18n` · “check the locale files”                 |
| `browser-check` | Headless Chromium screenshots of only the changed element, desktop and mobile, plus console errors. Only with your consent.                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/browser-check the cart badge on /cart`           |
| `design-review` | Reviews a page or component against the plan’s list of what fails a design review and its cross-site checklist. A script scans for emoji icons, gradients, glass effects, missing alt text, landmarks and heading, title, meta and hreflang rules; the rest is judged on screenshots at phone and desktop width in each theme. Read-only. | `/design-review` · “does this page fail review?”   |

## Performance

[Section titled “Performance”](#performance)

| Skill          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Example                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `pagespeed`    | Core Web Vitals with PageSpeed Insights for public URLs or local Lighthouse for localhost, mobile and desktop, condensed to the top opportunities, with a fix-and-measure loop for Next.js, Vite, Django and Laravel. | `/pagespeed http://localhost:3000/products` |
| `perf-backend` | N+1 detection from query logs, indexes from `EXPLAIN`, caching and profiling, proven with before and after numbers.                                                                                                   | `/perf-backend /api/orders is slow`         |

## Security and accessibility

[Section titled “Security and accessibility”](#security-and-accessibility)

| Skill            | What it does                                                                                                                                                   | Example                                      |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `security-audit` | A masked secret scan, vulnerable dependencies (npm, pnpm, Composer, pip or OSV.dev) and dangerous code patterns, with severity, evidence and fixes. Read-only. | `/security-audit` · `/security-audit full`   |
| `wcag-audit`     | WCAG 2.2 AA for the changed UI: axe-core through Playwright when available, plus a targeted checklist and concrete fixes.                                      | `/wcag-audit http://localhost:3000/checkout` |

## DevOps

[Section titled “DevOps”](#devops)

| Skill         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                    | Example                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `docker`      | Dockerfile and compose review and fixes: multi-stage builds, pinned images, non-root users, caching, healthchecks, secrets and exposed databases. Uses hadolint when installed. | `/docker` · “make the image smaller”       |
| `ci-setup`    | Creates or fixes GitHub Actions or GitLab CI for the detected stack, and reviews workflows for injection and unpinned actions. Uses actionlint when installed.                  | `/ci-setup` · “is our workflow safe?”      |
| `deps-update` | Outdated packages grouped by risk, changelogs read for majors, one group at a time with tests and a commit each.                                                                | `/deps-update` · “bump all patch versions” |

## Docs and meta

[Section titled “Docs and meta”](#docs-and-meta)

| Skill           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Example                                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `project-docs`  | A `.docs/` knowledge folder (overview, architecture, modules, data flow, development, decisions) and a short `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` that points to it.                                                                                                                                           | `/project-docs` · “slim down our CLAUDE.md”                      |
| `seo-audit`     | Technical SEO: meta tags, headings, canonical, robots and sitemap, hreflang, Open Graph, JSON-LD and performance basics.                                                                                                                                                                             | `/seo-audit https://example.com/product/1`                       |
| `release-notes` | Release notes and `CHANGELOG.md` entries from git history in the project’s style, without AI trailers.                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/release-notes since v1.4.0`                                    |
| `adr`           | Writes an architecture decision record in MADR 4.0.0 with the four fields Skribly requires (confidence, reopen when, exit plan and a confirmation that names its check), numbers it and keeps the index of `.docs/adr`. It refuses to edit an accepted record and supersedes it with a link instead. | `/adr` · “record this decision” · “supersede ADR 0007”           |
| `docs-sync`     | Checks that a change a user can see updated, in the same change, the Polish and English language files with the same keys, the repository’s `.docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the matching page on this site. Read-only: it reports what is missing and the agent adds it.                                | `/docs-sync` · “did I update the docs?”                          |
| `learn`         | Keeps confirmed project lessons (a command that works, a convention, a pitfall) in `.skribly/lessons.md`, one dated line each with the skill it came from, written only after you agree. Every skill reads the file first. Refuses anything that looks like a secret.                                | `/learn` · “remember that the e2e suite needs a seeded database” |
| `token-saver`   | Working rules for a small context: search before reading, line ranges, condensed logs, scripts instead of the model, `/clear` plus `STATE.md`.                                                                                                                                                       | `/token-saver` · “I’m close to the limit”                        |

## In development: eleven workflow skills

[Section titled “In development: eleven workflow skills”](#in-development-eleven-workflow-skills)

These skills are on the `develop` branch of agent-skills and ship in the next release; until then they are marked “next” on their own pages.

| Skill                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                         | Example                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| [`plan`](/skills/skill/plan/)                   | Turns a large or vague initiative into `.tasks/plans/<slug>.md`: the goal, what is out of scope, the risks and an ordered list of small tasks, each with what it delivers and how it is checked.     | `/plan` · “break this epic down”              |
| [`verify`](/skills/skill/verify/)               | Proves a change works in the running application: starts it with the project’s own command, exercises the changed path with a request or a headless browser, runs lint, types and the related tests. | `/verify` · “does it actually work?”          |
| [`improve`](/skills/skill/improve/)             | A short session of small fixes after a feature works: you name one thing, the agent fixes it with the smallest change, shows it and waits for the next.                                              | `/improve` · “small fixes”                    |
| [`merge`](/skills/skill/merge/)                 | Finishes a done branch into `develop` the way the project merges, pushes, and removes the branch and its worktree only after you agree. Never touches the release branch and never force pushes.     | `/merge` · “finish the branch”                |
| [`blast-radius`](/skills/skill/blast-radius/)   | Finds what a change can break outside its diff (callers, routes, jobs, migrations, configuration) and proves its one key assumption by running code.                                                 | `/blast-radius` · “what could this break?”    |
| [`deslop`](/skills/skill/deslop/)               | Cleans machine-written leftovers from the lines an agent added: comments that repeat the code, impossible checks, swallowed errors, unused helpers, inflated prose. Only on request.                 | `/deslop` · “make this look like our code”    |
| [`correct`](/skills/skill/correct/)             | Turns a mistake agents keep making into a guard that stops it: a type, a lint rule, a test or a check script, added after you agree. Only on request.                                                | `/correct` · “agents keep doing X”            |
| [`report`](/skills/skill/report/)               | A delivery report for the person who asked: each requirement mapped to the code and to the check that proves it, what is not done and the risks left.                                                | `/report` · “what did we deliver?”            |
| [`record-docs`](/skills/skill/record-docs/)     | Writes the as-built page of an important feature or decision: what it does, how it is built, the decisions, how to run and test it, and its limits.                                                  | `/record-docs` · “document this feature”      |
| [`writing`](/skills/skill/writing/)             | One plain style, in Polish or English, for every text an agent writes for people, and a rewrite of a given text on request.                                                                          | `/writing` · “rewrite this plainly”           |
| [`tracker-write`](/skills/skill/tracker-write/) | Drafts an issue, a tracker comment, a pull request description or a review reply for your approval; nothing is posted until you say so.                                                              | `/tracker-write` · “write the PR description” |

## Files the skills leave behind

[Section titled “Files the skills leave behind”](#files-the-skills-leave-behind)

| File                             | Written by                             | What it holds                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.skribly/project.json`          | `project`, project-scope installs, you | The project profile: stack, commands, commit style and language, base branch and, optionally, the Skribly Tracker project. Its schema comes from [`@skribly/core`](/core/) |
| `.skribly/project.detected.json` | `project`                              | The last detection, so the next run can tell detected values from values you set by hand                                                                                   |
| `.skribly/lessons.md`            | `learn`, after your OK                 | Dated one-line lessons, each with the skill it came from                                                                                                                   |
| `.tasks/<id>/TASK.md`            | `task`                                 | The issue as fetched, refreshed with only the changes on later fetches                                                                                                     |
| `.tasks/<id>/SPEC.md`            | `task`                                 | The analysis of a larger task, for your approval                                                                                                                           |
| `.tasks/<id>/STATE.md`           | `task`, `handoff`                      | About 30 lines: goal, what is done, changed files, check results, decisions, one next step                                                                                 |
| `.tasks/<id>/COMMENT.md`         | `task`                                 | A draft tracker comment, posted only after your explicit OK                                                                                                                |
| `.tasks/workflow.md`             | `task`                                 | Project conventions: tracker, base branch, branch and commit patterns, check commands, dev URL                                                                             |

`.tasks/` is added to `.git/info/exclude`, so fetched tickets never land in a commit and the team’s `.gitignore` stays untouched. The `.skribly/` files are meant to be committed with the project, so the whole team and every agent read the same profile and lessons.

# Commits without AI trailers

> The three independent layers agent-skills uses so commits look like yours - the skills themselves, the Claude Code attribution setting and a commit-msg hook for any tool.

Commits should look like yours. agent-skills uses three independent layers, so one failing does not matter.

## 1. The skills

[Section titled “1. The skills”](#1-the-skills)

`commit` and `task` write messages in the project’s convention, from `.tasks/workflow.md` or detected from your own recent commits, and never add trailers: no `Co-Authored-By`, no “Generated with”, no agent links or emoji signatures. They commit only after you say OK, stage only the listed files, and never push, merge, rebase or force unless you ask in that conversation.

## 2. The Claude Code setting

[Section titled “2. The Claude Code setting”](#2-the-claude-code-setting)

```bash
agent-skills config attribution off                # ~/.claude/settings.json
agent-skills config attribution off --project .    # this project's .claude/settings.json
agent-skills config attribution status
agent-skills config attribution on                 # undo
```

It sets `"attribution": { "commit": "", "pr": "" }`, which hides the commit trailer and the pull request footer, and the older `"includeCoAuthoredBy": false` for earlier Claude Code versions. Other keys are kept, a backup is written before the first change, and invalid JSON is never overwritten.

## 3. The git hook, for any tool

[Section titled “3. The git hook, for any tool”](#3-the-git-hook-for-any-tool)

```bash
cd ~/code/shop
agent-skills hooks install
agent-skills hooks status
agent-skills hooks uninstall
```

The `commit-msg` hook removes:

* `Co-authored-by:` trailers. All of them by default; to keep human co-authors, run `git config agent-skills.keepHumanCoauthors true`, and only AI ones are removed.
* Footers such as “Generated with Claude Code”, “Generated by GitHub Copilot” or “Made with Cursor”. A “generated, made or created with” line is removed only when it names an AI tool, so “Generated with protoc” stays.

It never touches anything else: the subject, the body, `Signed-off-by`, comment lines and everything below the scissors line of `git commit -v` stay byte for byte, line endings included.

* Your existing `commit-msg` hook is kept and still runs after this one; uninstalling restores it.
* In repositories that use husky, lefthook or another `core.hooksPath`, the installer does not take over that folder. It prints one line to add to your own hook: `node .git/hooks/agent-skills-commit-msg.cjs "$1"`.
* The hook needs `node` on `PATH`; without it, the hook skips itself instead of blocking commits.
* Hooks are per repository and are not committed. Install it in each clone.

Skribly Agent has the same hook built in: **Code & git → Hook without AI trailers**.

## Checking old commits

[Section titled “Checking old commits”](#checking-old-commits)

```bash
git log --format='%h %s%n%b' | grep -inE 'co-authored-by|generated with' | head
```

Rewriting published history is a team decision; agent-skills never does it.

# How it works

> How the agent-skills skills work together - one pipeline from a plan to a merged branch, read-only guardrails along it, the project profile every skill reads first, and lessons with a scope.

In development

This page describes the version in development, which ships in the next release. The released agent-skills 0.3.0 has the profile, lessons without scopes and most of the steps; the steps marked “next” on [All skills](/skills/skill/) come with the next release.

Every step of the work is a skill. Each one reads the project profile (`.skribly/project.json`) and the lessons (`.skribly/lessons.md`) first, keeps its working files under `.tasks/` (out of git), and waits for you at the points marked **OK**.

## The pipeline

[Section titled “The pipeline”](#the-pipeline)

One path from an idea to a merged branch:

```text
plan -> spec -> task -> verify -> e2e-check -> improve -> commit -> merge
         \___ review · gate-convention · blast-radius · security-audit · design-review · deslop ___/
```

Small work skips the early steps: a one-file fix starts at `task`, a task that fits in one sitting needs no `plan`, and a task `task` can describe in five lines needs no `spec`.

| Step | Skill                                   | Writes                                           | Waits for                              |
| ---- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 1    | [`plan`](/skills/skill/plan/)           | `.tasks/plans/<slug>.md`                         | **OK** on the plan                     |
| 2    | [`spec`](/skills/skill/spec/)           | `.tasks/specs/SPEC-<slug>.md`                    | **OK**, then `Status: approved`        |
| 3    | [`task`](/skills/skill/task/)           | a branch, code in phases, `.tasks/<id>/STATE.md` | **OK** before the branch               |
| 4    | [`verify`](/skills/skill/verify/)       | nothing: a pass or fail per step                 | -                                      |
| 5    | [`e2e-check`](/skills/skill/e2e-check/) | screenshots under the test output folder         | **OK** to spend tokens on screenshots  |
| 6    | [`improve`](/skills/skill/improve/)     | one small fix per note                           | your next note                         |
| 7    | [`commit`](/skills/skill/commit/)       | a local commit, no trailers                      | **OK** on the message and files        |
| 8    | [`merge`](/skills/skill/merge/)         | the merge into `develop`, a push                 | **OK** before the push and the cleanup |

The `project` skill writes the conventions of the two planning folders into the project: `.tasks/plans/README.md` and `.tasks/specs/README.md`, with the naming, what each file holds and the life cycle `draft -> approved -> done -> archived`.

## The guardrails

[Section titled “The guardrails”](#the-guardrails)

The guardrails are read-only reviews. Each reports its findings first, with `file:line` and a fix, and changes code only when you accept a finding.

| Guardrail                                           | Asks                                                                  | Called from                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`review`](/skills/skill/review/)                   | does the change do what it claims, for every input?                   | `task` before each commit; `review pr` before `merge`                  |
| [`gate-convention`](/skills/skill/gate-convention/) | does it follow what the project wrote in `AGENTS.md` and the profile? | after each phase of a spec; `task` before a commit                     |
| [`blast-radius`](/skills/skill/blast-radius/)       | what outside the diff relies on what changed?                         | `task` when an export, route, schema, config or shared module changes  |
| [`security-audit`](/skills/skill/security-audit/)   | secrets, injection, authorization, vulnerable dependencies?           | `task` when auth, input handling or dependencies change; `deps-update` |
| [`design-review`](/skills/skill/design-review/)     | does a page pass the design checklist?                                | `task` for a visible UI change                                         |
| [`deslop`](/skills/skill/deslop/)                   | machine-written noise in the added lines?                             | `task` before a commit                                                 |

`review pr` is the one place where every guardrail runs on the same diff: the whole branch against `develop`, written as a draft review that is posted only after you approve it.

## The project profile

[Section titled “The project profile”](#the-project-profile)

`.skribly/project.json` holds the stack, the commands (install, dev, build, test, lint, typecheck, format), the commit style and language, the base branch, CI and containers. The [`project`](/skills/skill/project/) skill or `agent-skills init` detects it from `package.json` and lock files, `pyproject.toml`, `composer.json`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, Dockerfiles, CI files, the README and your commit history.

* **Read first, everywhere.** Every skill starts from the profile and falls back to its own detection only when the profile is missing.
* **Your edits win.** A value you set by hand is never overwritten by a later detection, and a value you delete stays deleted.
* **Safe commands.** A package folder goes into a command such as `cd web && npm test` only when its path is made of plain segments; any other folder is left out and reported as `skipped`. In a repository you did not write, every skill shows you the profile’s commands before running them.
* **Only the skills that fit.** The profile becomes stack tags (`node`, `php`, `python` and the other runtimes, plus `web`, `backend`, `database`, `docker`, `data`, `skribly-app`). A skill without stacks fits every project; a skill with stacks is installed only where they match. See [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

## Lessons with scopes

[Section titled “Lessons with scopes”](#lessons-with-scopes)

At the end of `task`, `test-loop`, `review` and `debug` the agent proposes one lesson it confirmed: a command that works, a convention the code does not show, a pitfall that cost time. With your OK, [`learn`](/skills/skill/learn/) writes it to `.skribly/lessons.md` with the date and the skill it came from. Anything that looks like a secret is refused.

Each lesson sits under a scope heading, so a skill reads only the lessons for the files it changes:

| Scope           | Covers                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `## [All]`      | any change; lines above the first heading count as `All`                                   |
| `## [CI]`       | the pipeline files (`.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile` and their like)  |
| `## [<module>]` | a folder name (`cart` matches any `cart/` folder), a path (`src/cart`) or a glob (`*.sql`) |

`lessons.mjs for-diff --base <branch>` prints only the lessons whose scope matches the changed files. A lesson that proves itself can be promoted into the profile.

## What feeds every step

[Section titled “What feeds every step”](#what-feeds-every-step)

* [`project`](/skills/skill/project/): the profile and the work folders.
* [`learn`](/skills/skill/learn/): the lessons, each with its scope.
* [`guide-tests`](/skills/skill/guide-tests/): what deserves a test and at which level, used by `task`, `spec` and `test-loop`.
* [`writing`](/skills/skill/writing/): the style of every text for people, from commit bodies to reports.
* [`handoff`](/skills/skill/handoff/): `STATE.md`, so any agent can resume at any step after `/clear` or a usage limit.

## Cheap on tokens

[Section titled “Cheap on tokens”](#cheap-on-tokens)

An agent keeps only each skill’s name and description in context. `SKILL.md` loads when the skill runs, its other references only when a step needs them, and small scripts hand the model a few lines instead of raw output. Every skill has a measured size and a budget the repository’s check enforces: [Token cost](/skills/token-cost/).

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/): `init`, `train-skills`, switches, lessons and project skills, step by step.
* [Agent tooling](/skills/tooling/): the delete guard, the status line, permissions, the MCP smoke test and the CI job.
* [All skills](/skills/skill/): every skill on its own page.

# Install agent-skills

> Install agent-skills for one or all seven agents, at user or project scope, keep it updated and remove it cleanly.

## Requirements

[Section titled “Requirements”](#requirements)

* `git` and **Node.js 20 or newer** (`node --version`). No npm packages are installed: the CLI and every skill script use only Node’s standard library.
* At least one supported agent: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot or Devin.

Access

The repository is private for now, so cloning needs access to the Skribly organisation on GitHub.

## Install in a minute

[Section titled “Install in a minute”](#install-in-a-minute)

1. Clone the repository and put the command on your `PATH`:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills.git ~/agent-skills
   cd ~/agent-skills
   npm link
   ```

2. Install every skill for every agent, at user scope:

   ```bash
   agent-skills install --target all
   ```

3. Turn off Claude Code’s own attribution and check the result:

   ```bash
   agent-skills config attribution off
   agent-skills doctor
   ```

4. Restart your agent, or open a new chat, so it reads its skills folder again. Then try `/task 123` in Claude Code or `$task 123` in Codex.

On Windows use the same commands in PowerShell with `$HOME\agent-skills`. Folder links are created as junctions, which need no administrator rights. Without `npm link`, run `node cli/agent-skills.mjs …` or `bin\agent-skills.cmd …`.

## User scope or project scope

[Section titled “User scope or project scope”](#user-scope-or-project-scope)

|          | User scope (default)                      | Project scope                                             |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command  | `agent-skills install --target all`       | `agent-skills install --target all --project ~/code/shop` |
| Where    | `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, … | `<project>/.claude/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, … |
| How      | Symlinks to the repository                | Copies                                                    |
| Updates  | `git pull`, then `agent-skills sync`      | `agent-skills sync` after `git pull`                      |
| Good for | Your own machine, all projects            | Sharing with a team through the project’s repository      |

A project-scope install also detects the project profile, `.skribly/project.json`; pass `--no-detect` to skip it.

You can mix them: install everything at user scope and commit `task` and `commit` into a team project so colleagues get them too. Choose explicitly with `--scope user|project`, `--link` or `--copy`.

## Choose skills and agents

[Section titled “Choose skills and agents”](#choose-skills-and-agents)

```bash
agent-skills install --target claude,codex --skills task,commit,handoff,review,test-loop,token-saver
agent-skills list
```

`--target` takes `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `windsurf`, `copilot`, `devin` or `all`. `--format rules` writes the classic formats for older agent versions; see [Supported agents](/skills/agents/).

## Recommended setup

[Section titled “Recommended setup”](#recommended-setup)

```bash
agent-skills config attribution off             # Claude Code: no Co-Authored-By trailer or PR footer
cd ~/code/shop && agent-skills hooks install    # per repository: strip AI trailers from any tool
```

Then configure your tracker as in [Trackers](/skills/trackers/).

## Connect a tracker

[Section titled “Connect a tracker”](#connect-a-tracker)

```bash
agent-skills tasks check
agent-skills tasks list
agent-skills tasks fetch 482
```

Credentials come from environment variables or `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env`, never from the repository. The first fetch writes `.tasks/<id>/TASK.md`, later fetches print only what changed, and `.tasks/` is excluded locally, so fetched tickets stay out of commits.

## Update and remove

[Section titled “Update and remove”](#update-and-remove)

```bash
cd ~/agent-skills && git pull && agent-skills sync      # refresh everything that was installed
agent-skills uninstall --target all                     # user scope
agent-skills uninstall --target all --project ~/code/shop
```

Installs are recorded in `~/.config/agent-skills/installs.json` with a hash of each file. `uninstall` removes only what agent-skills installed, keeps files you edited unless you pass `--force`, and deletes folders it leaves empty. A file agent-skills did not write is never overwritten; with `--force` it is moved to `<path>.bak-agent-skills` first.

## CLI reference

[Section titled “CLI reference”](#cli-reference)

| Command                                                                                                                                                                | Purpose                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent-skills list [--json]`                                                                                                                                           | The catalogue                                                                                                                                 |
| `agent-skills install --target <agents\|all> [--scope user\|project] [--project <dir>] [--skills a,b] [--link\|--copy] [--format skills\|rules] [--dry-run] [--force]` | Install                                                                                                                                       |
| `agent-skills uninstall --target … [--scope] [--project] [--skills]`                                                                                                   | Remove only what was installed                                                                                                                |
| `agent-skills sync`                                                                                                                                                    | Re-apply every recorded install after `git pull`                                                                                              |
| `agent-skills project [--project <dir>] [--dry-run] [--json]`                                                                                                          | Detect the project into `.skribly/project.json`, keeping values set by hand                                                                   |
| `agent-skills agent-files [--project <dir>] [--check] [--force] [--force-mcp] [--skills a,b\|all] [--dry-run] [--json]`                                                | Generate the per-agent files of a repository from its `AGENTS.md`; see [Project instruction files](/skills/agents/#project-instruction-files) |
| `agent-skills doctor [--project <dir>] [--json]`                                                                                                                       | Agents, installs, trackers, hook, attribution and whether each agent is configured for the repository                                         |
| `agent-skills hooks install\|uninstall\|status [--project <dir>]`                                                                                                      | The `commit-msg` hook                                                                                                                         |
| `agent-skills config attribution off\|on\|status [--project <dir>]`                                                                                                    | Claude Code attribution                                                                                                                       |
| `agent-skills tasks fetch\|attachments\|list\|comment-draft\|event\|detect\|check`                                                                                     | The tracker client; `event` prints the `skills.task.completed` event of a task                                                                |
| `agent-skills manifest [--check\|--write]`                                                                                                                             | Validate skills, sync shared files, regenerate `skills.json`                                                                                  |

## With Skribly Agent

[Section titled “With Skribly Agent”](#with-skribly-agent)

[Skribly Agent](/agent/skills/) clones agent-skills, shows the catalogue from `skills.json` (a stable v1 contract with a JSON schema), installs the chosen skills per project and per agent through this CLI, and can ask an agent to adapt them to the project. It runs the CLI with its own runtime, so no separate Node.js is needed there.

# Rule dictionary

> The rules of agent-skills as data - one sentence, a severity and a public source per rule - listed for the files in hand and checked line by line with agent-skills rules --check.

In development

The rule dictionary and the commands on this page ship in the next release; the released agent-skills 0.3.0 does not have them yet.

The rule dictionary holds the common mistakes of each technology as data, one file per rule: Node, PHP, Python, Go, Java, databases and migrations, mobile, Docker, CI, infrastructure, data and ML, security, testing and docs, and the frameworks Next.js, React, Vue, Angular, Express, Tailwind CSS, Laravel, Django, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Ruby on Rails, Spring Boot, .NET, Kubernetes and Flutter. The `framework-guide` skill reads the rules of the framework at hand; the commands below read them without a skill.

Every rule has:

| Field              | What it holds                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Id                 | a stable name such as `nextjs/async-request-apis`                                   |
| Rule               | one sentence                                                                        |
| Severity           | `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`                                               |
| Versions           | the framework versions it is for, such as `15+` (optional)                          |
| Applies to         | the files it is for, written like `.gitignore` patterns                             |
| Source             | the title and address of a public page that says so                                 |
| Why, fix, examples | a short reason, the fix, and a bad and a good example                               |
| Check              | a one-line pattern that finds the bad case, or the reason why a line cannot show it |

## List the rules

[Section titled “List the rules”](#list-the-rules)

```bash
agent-skills rules --tech docker
agent-skills rules --files src/app/page.tsx,Dockerfile --severity high
agent-skills rules --tech go --json
```

One line per rule: the id, the severity, the rule and its source. `--tech` keeps the given technologies, `--files` the rules that apply to those files, and `--severity` that level and above, most severe first.

## Check a project

[Section titled “Check a project”](#check-a-project)

```bash
agent-skills rules --check
agent-skills rules --check --project ../shop --tech nextjs,react
agent-skills rules --check --files src/app/page.tsx --json
```

`--check` runs the rules that carry a line pattern over the project, or over the given files, and prints one line per finding: `file:line rule-id (severity, versions): rule source-address`. The exit code is 1 when there is a finding, so the command fits a CI step. A pattern is at most 200 characters and must match the bad example of its rule and not the good one; some patterns run only in files that import the framework, so code of another library is not reported.

The command reads only text: it skips files over 1 MB, binary files, lines past 1,000 characters, dependency and build folders such as `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist` and `.venv`, and paths outside the project, and it stops at 20,000 files and 1,000 findings. Nothing in the project is changed.

A rule whose bad case is something missing, spans several lines or depends on history (a missing `USER` in a Dockerfile, an `await` before a use of `context`, a migration that already ran) has no pattern. It says why in its data, and the last line of the report counts these review-only rules: read them with `agent-skills rules`.

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [All rules](/skills/all-rules/): every rule by technology, with its severity and source.
* [Agent tooling](/skills/tooling/): the other commands of the CLI.
* [`framework-guide`](/skills/skill/framework-guide/): the skill that reads these rules, also in the next release.

# All skills

> Every one of the 57 skills of agent-skills on its own page, generated from its SKILL.md: what it does, when to use it, how to call it, its scripts, the stacks it fits and its token cost.

57 skills are in development: 39 of them are in the released agent-skills 0.3.0, the other 18 ship in the next release. Each page is generated from the skill’s `SKILL.md`, so it says what the skill says.

# Architecture decision record

> The adr skill of agent-skills: writes an architecture decision record in MADR 4.0.0 with the four fields Skribly requires (Confidence, Reopen when, Exit plan, Confirmation naming its fitness function), numbers it, keeps the index of the repository's .docs/adr folder, refuses to edit an accepted ADR and supersedes it with a link instead.

`adr` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                              |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/adr`, `$adr` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Docs                                                                                         |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                      |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                           |
| Source  | [skills/adr/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/adr/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Writes an architecture decision record in MADR 4.0.0 with the four fields Skribly requires (Confidence, Reopen when, Exit plan, Confirmation naming its fitness function), numbers it, keeps the index of the repository’s `.docs/adr` folder, refuses to edit an accepted ADR and supersedes it with a link instead.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “write an ADR”
* “record this decision”
* “we chose X over Y”
* “supersede ADR 0007”
* Also: before code that is costly to reverse lands.

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/adr`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$adr`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/adr` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/adr`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/adr`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/adr` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/adr`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

The skill hands the mechanical work to these Node scripts with no dependencies, which print a few lines instead of raw output:

* `adr.mjs`: `node scripts/adr.mjs new "<title>" | supersede <number> "<title>" | guard <file> | check [file...] | index`

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable adr` removes it from a project, `project enable adr` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# What a change breaks outside the diff

> The blast-radius skill of agent-skills: finds what a change can break outside its own diff before it is committed or merged - every caller, importer, route, job, migration and configuration that depends on what changed, the one assumption the change relies on, and a quick proof of that assumption by running code (a test, a script, a query) instead of reading.

`blast-radius` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                                |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/blast-radius`, `$blast-radius` in Codex                                                                      |

| Stacks  | general                                                                                                        |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                                      |
| Source  | [skills/blast-radius/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/blast-radius/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Finds what a change can break outside its own diff before it is committed or merged - every caller, importer, route, job, migration and configuration that depends on what changed, the one assumption the change relies on, and a quick proof of that assumption by running code (a test, a script, a query) instead of reading. Reports the risk in a few lines.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “what could this break”
* “is this change safe”

# Commit in project style

> The commit skill of agent-skills: proposes a commit message in the project's own convention (read from .tasks/workflow.md or inferred from git log), shows it with the exact file list and commits only after explicit approval.

`commit` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                    |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/commit`, `$commit` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Workflow                                                                                           |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                            |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                 |
| Source  | [skills/commit/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/commit/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Proposes a commit message in the project’s own convention (read from `.tasks/workflow.md` or inferred from git log), shows it with the exact file list and commits only after explicit approval. Never adds Co-Authored-By, “Generated with” or any other trailer, and never pushes, merges or amends unless asked.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “commit this”
* “commit the changes”
* “write a Conventional Commit”
* “commit message”
* “what should the commit say”
* Also: splitting changes into clean commits.

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Cursor         | `/commit` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/commit`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/commit`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/commit` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/commit`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

# Safe database migrations

> The db-migrations skill of agent-skills: reviews and writes safe database migrations for Django, Laravel, Prisma, Alembic, Flyway and Rails, catching table locks, NOT NULL without defaults, destructive drops and renames, type changes, unvalidated foreign keys, unbatched backfills and missing rollbacks, and rewrites them into zero-downtime expand and contract steps.

`db-migrations` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Reviews and writes safe database migrations for Django, Laravel, Prisma, Alembic, Flyway and Rails, catching table locks, NOT NULL without defaults, destructive drops and renames, type changes, unvalidated foreign keys, unbatched backfills and missing rollbacks, and rewrites them into zero-downtime expand and contract steps.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “review this migration”
* “is this migration safe”
* “add a column to a big table”
* “zero-downtime migration”
* “rename a column safely”
