# Design review of a page

> The design-review skill of agent-skills: reviews a site page or component against the plan's fails-review list (design.md section 10.5) and the cross-site checklist (section 12), both read live.

`design-review` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/design-review`, `$design-review` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Quality and tests                                                                                                |
| Stacks  | `web`                                                                                                            |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                               |
| Source  | [skills/design-review/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/design-review/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Reviews a site page or component against the plan’s fails-review list (`design.md` section 10.5) and the cross-site checklist (section 12), both read live. A script scans the files for emoji icons, purple and blue gradients, glass effects, stock illustrations, missing alt, landmarks and the single h1, title, meta and hreflang rules, third-party scripts and wording bans; the rest is judged by eye on screenshots at 360 and 1440 px in each theme. Read-only.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “review this page’s design”
* “does this page fail review”

# Clean machine leftovers from a diff

> The deslop skill of agent-skills: cleans the lines a coding agent added in the current diff of the usual machine-written leftovers - comments that repeat the code, defensive checks for things that cannot happen, needless type escapes, try/catch that swallows errors, wordy log messages, unused helpers, a style different from the rest of the file, and inflated prose in docs.

`deslop` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Cleans the lines a coding agent added in the current diff of the usual machine-written leftovers - comments that repeat the code, defensive checks for things that cannot happen, needless type escapes, try/catch that swallows errors, wordy log messages, unused helpers, a style different from the rest of the file, and inflated prose in docs. Fixes them in place, only in added lines, and lists what it changed. Run only on request.

# Task estimation

> The estimate skill of agent-skills: estimates a task or feature without changing code, breaking it into deliverables with optimistic, likely and pessimistic hours, a PERT total and range, plus assumptions, risks and questions ready to send to whoever asked for the work.

`estimate` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command | `/estimate`, `$estimate` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Workflow                                                                                               |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                     |
| Source  | [skills/estimate/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/estimate/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Estimates a task or feature without changing code, breaking it into deliverables with optimistic, likely and pessimistic hours, a PERT total and range, plus assumptions, risks and questions ready to send to whoever asked for the work.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “how long will this take”
* “estimate this ticket”
* “ile to zajmie”
* “oszacuj”
* “size this work”
* “how many days”
* Also: sizing work before planning.

Not for making a test suite or a build faster.

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Claude Code    | `/estimate`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$estimate`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/estimate` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/estimate`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/estimate`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/estimate` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/estimate`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

None: the skill is instructions only, and the agent runs the project’s own commands.

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable estimate` removes it from a project, `project enable estimate` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Framework code for the installed version

> The framework-guide skill of agent-skills: writes framework code against the version the project has installed, not the one in the model's memory - reads the installed version and its docs (the AGENTS.md docs index, node_modules or vendor), confirms each API in the installed package before using it, and checks the common errors of that major version (Next.js, React, Vue, Angular, Express, Tailwind, Laravel, Django, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Rails, Spring Boot, .NET, Flutter, Kubernetes manifests).

`framework-guide` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/framework-guide`, `$framework-guide` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Quality and tests                                                                                                    |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                              |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                                            |
| Source  | [skills/framework-guide/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/framework-guide/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Writes framework code against the version the project has installed, not the one in the model’s memory - reads the installed version and its docs (the `AGENTS.md` docs index, node_modules or vendor), confirms each API in the installed package before using it, and checks the common errors of that major version (Next.js, React, Vue, Angular, Express, Tailwind, Laravel, Django, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Rails, Spring Boot, .NET, Flutter, Kubernetes manifests).

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “which API does our version have”
* “is this the right API for our Next.js”
* “you used an old API”
* “check against the installed version”

Not for moving to a new version (upgrade).

| OpenCode       | `/framework-guide`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/framework-guide` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/framework-guide`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

None: the skill is instructions only, and the agent runs the project’s own commands.

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable framework-guide` removes it from a project, `project enable framework-guide` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Convention gate

> The gate-convention skill of agent-skills: a review gate for the project's own conventions - collects the rules of AGENTS.md (and nested ones above the changed files), CLAUDE.md and the conventions of .skribly/project.json into a numbered checklist, checks the diff against each rule and reports findings first, each with file line, the rule it breaks and its source, and a concrete fix.

`gate-convention` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/gate-convention`, `$gate-convention` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Quality and tests                                                                                                    |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                              |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                                            |
| Source  | [skills/gate-convention/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/gate-convention/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

A review gate for the project’s own conventions - collects the rules of `AGENTS.md` (and nested ones above the changed files), `CLAUDE.md` and the conventions of `.skribly/project.json` into a numbered checklist, checks the diff against each rule and reports findings first, each with file line, the rule it breaks and its source, and a concrete fix. Not a bug hunt (review) or a security pass (security-audit). Read-only unless asked to fix.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “check the conventions”
* “does this follow AGENTS.md”
* “convention gate”
* Also: after each phase of a spec and before a commit.

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/gate-convention`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$gate-convention`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/gate-convention` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/gate-convention`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/gate-convention`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/gate-convention` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/gate-convention`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

The skill hands the mechanical work to these Node scripts with no dependencies, which print a few lines instead of raw output:

* `lessons.mjs`: `node scripts/lessons.mjs list [--scope <scope>] [--project <dir>]`
* `rules.mjs`: `node scripts/rules.mjs [changed path...] [--project <dir>] [--json]`

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable gate-convention` removes it from a project, `project enable gate-convention` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Test guide

> The guide-tests skill of agent-skills: decides what deserves a test and where it goes - the three levels (unit with mocks at the boundary, integration with the real framework and database, end to end against the running app), one folder per domain under tests/, and the switch that turns each level on - read from the tests the project already has by a script that maps them by level and domain.

`guide-tests` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command | `/guide-tests`, `$guide-tests` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Quality and tests                                                                                            |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                      |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                                    |
| Source  | [skills/guide-tests/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/guide-tests/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Decides what deserves a test and where it goes - the three levels (unit with mocks at the boundary, integration with the real framework and database, end to end against the running app), one folder per domain under tests/, and the switch that turns each level on - read from the tests the project already has by a script that maps them by level and domain.

## When to use it

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “what should I test”
* “where does this test go”
* “unit or integration”
* “how are tests organised here”
* Also: before writing tests in the task, spec and test-loop skills.

# Handoff and resume

> The handoff skill of agent-skills: saves or restores working state in a .tasks/ STATE.md file so another agent, or a fresh session after /clear, compaction or a usage limit, can continue without the transcript.

`handoff` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/handoff`, `$handoff` in Codex                                                                      |

| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                   |
| Source  | [skills/handoff/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/handoff/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Saves or restores working state in a `.tasks/` `STATE.md` file so another agent, or a fresh session after /clear, compaction or a usage limit, can continue without the transcript.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “save state”
* “hand this over to Codex/Claude”
* “I’m about to hit the limit”
* “resume”
* “continue from STATE.md”
* “where were we”

Not for “saving settings to a config file”.

# Translations and i18n

> The i18n skill of agent-skills: keeps translations complete and correct by finding missing, empty and extra keys per locale, placeholder mismatches and keys used in code but absent from the catalog (JSON, YAML, gettext PO and Laravel lang files), then adds translations in the project's format and extracts hard-coded UI strings.

`i18n` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

| Source  | [skills/i18n/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/i18n/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Keeps translations complete and correct by finding missing, empty and extra keys per locale, placeholder mismatches and keys used in code but absent from the catalog (JSON, YAML, gettext PO and Laravel lang files), then adds translations in the project’s format and extracts hard-coded UI strings.

* “missing translations”

# Small improvements, live

> The improve skill of agent-skills: runs a short, interactive session of small improvements after a feature works - the user names what bothers them (spacing, a label, a slow step, an edge case), the agent fixes one item at a time with the smallest change, shows the result and waits for the next note.

`improve` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/improve`, `$improve` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Workflow                                                                                             |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                              |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                            |
| Source  | [skills/improve/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/improve/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Runs a short, interactive session of small improvements after a feature works - the user names what bothers them (spacing, a label, a slow step, an edge case), the agent fixes one item at a time with the smallest change, shows the result and waits for the next note. Nothing outside the named item changes, and every item is checked before the next.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “let us polish this”
* “small fixes”
* “tweak it live”

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                      |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/improve`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$improve`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/improve` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/improve`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/improve`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/improve` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/improve`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

None: the skill is instructions only, and the agent runs the project’s own commands.

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable improve` removes it from a project, `project enable improve` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Project lessons

> The learn skill of agent-skills: records a confirmed lesson about the current project (a command that works, a convention the team follows, a pitfall that cost time) in .skribly/lessons.md under a scope (All, CI or one module) with the date and the skill it came from, only after the user agrees, so every skill starts smarter next time.

`learn` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command | `/learn`, `$learn` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Meta                                                                                             |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                          |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                               |
| Source  | [skills/learn/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/learn/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Records a confirmed lesson about the current project (a command that works, a convention the team follows, a pitfall that cost time) in `.skribly/lessons.md` under a scope (All, CI or one module) with the date and the skill it came from, only after the user agrees, so every skill starts smarter next time. Also lists, prunes and promotes lessons into `.skribly/project.json`, and prints only the lessons for the files a diff changes. Never stores secrets.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “remember this”
* “note that for next time”
* “what have we learned about this project”
* Also: at the end of task, test-loop, review and debug.

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/learn`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$learn`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/learn` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/learn`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/learn`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/learn` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/learn`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

The skill hands the mechanical work to these Node scripts with no dependencies, which print a few lines instead of raw output:

* `lessons.mjs`: `node scripts/lessons.mjs list [--scope <scope>] [--project <dir>]`

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable learn` removes it from a project, `project enable learn` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Load testing

> The load-test skill of agent-skills: plans, writes and runs load tests with k6 (or autocannon or Locust) from a short smoke run up to load, stress and spike profiles, with explicit thresholds for latency percentiles and error rate, then reads the results through a condensed summary and points to the bottleneck.

`load-test` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/load-test`, `$load-test` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Quality and tests                                                                                        |
| Stacks  | `backend`                                                                                                |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                       |
| Source  | [skills/load-test/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/load-test/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Plans, writes and runs load tests with k6 (or autocannon or Locust) from a short smoke run up to load, stress and spike profiles, with explicit thresholds for latency percentiles and error rate, then reads the results through a condensed summary and points to the bottleneck.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “load test this endpoint”
* “how many users can it handle”
* “stress test”
* “k6 script”
* “check performance under load”
* Also: before a launch or after a performance fix.

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- |

| Codex CLI      | `$load-test`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/load-test` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/load-test`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/load-test`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/load-test` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/load-test`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

The skill hands the mechanical work to these Node scripts with no dependencies, which print a few lines instead of raw output:

* `load-summary.mjs`: `node scripts/load-summary.mjs <summary.json> [--json]`

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

# Finish a branch into develop

> The merge skill of agent-skills: finishes a branch whose work is done - checks it is clean and green, brings in the latest integration branch, merges it into the integration branch (develop by default) the way the project does it (a merge commit, or a squash where the project squashes), pushes, and removes the branch and its worktree, local and remote, only after the user agrees.

`merge` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command | `/merge`, `$merge` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Workflow                                                                                         |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                          |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                        |
| Source  | [skills/merge/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/merge/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Finishes a branch whose work is done - checks it is clean and green, brings in the latest integration branch, merges it into the integration branch (develop by default) the way the project does it (a merge commit, or a squash where the project squashes), pushes, and removes the branch and its worktree, local and remote, only after the user agrees. Never touches the release branch and never force pushes.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “merge this into develop”
* “finish the branch”
* “clean up the worktree”

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/merge`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$merge`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/merge` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/merge`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/merge`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/merge` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/merge`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

None: the skill is instructions only, and the agent runs the project’s own commands.

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable merge` removes it from a project, `project enable merge` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Newsletter issue

> The newsletter skill of agent-skills: drafts one issue of the Skribly Newsletter (AI news for developers plus what is new in Skribly) in Polish and English.

`newsletter` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                            |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/newsletter`, `$newsletter` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Docs                                                                                                       |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                    |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                         |
| Source  | [skills/newsletter/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/newsletter/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Drafts one issue of the Skribly Newsletter (AI news for developers plus what is new in Skribly) in Polish and English. Collects candidate items from a curated list of public feeds, picks the best, opens and checks every item at its primary source, writes `pl.md` and `en.md` in the issue format with a source under every item, adds “From Skribly” from the live public sites and changelogs, validates the folder and saves it as a draft. Never sends and never approves.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “napisz numer newslettera”
* “przygotuj newsletter”
* “write the next newsletter issue”
* “draft newsletter issue 3”
* “collect AI news for the newsletter”

Not for “a sign-up form”, “a subscription checkbox” or “sending to subscribers”.

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                         |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/newsletter`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$newsletter`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/newsletter` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/newsletter`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/newsletter`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/newsletter` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/newsletter`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

The skill hands the mechanical work to these Node scripts with no dependencies, which print a few lines instead of raw output:

* `check-issue.mjs`: `node scripts/check-issue.mjs <issue folder> [--deny <file>] [--json]`
* `collect.mjs`: `node scripts/collect.mjs [--days 14] [--issues <content/issues>] [--sources <file>] [--topic a,b] [--only id,id]`
* `save-draft.mjs`: `node scripts/save-draft.mjs <issue folder> [--dry-run] [--timeout 20000]`

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable newsletter` removes it from a project, `project enable newsletter` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Parallel subagents

> The orchestrate skill of agent-skills: splits a large job into independent sub-tasks and runs them in parallel with subagents (Claude Code Agent/Task tool, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode agents, or separate sessions) using self-contained briefs and explicit file ownership so they never edit the same files, then merges and verifies the results.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Splits a large job into independent sub-tasks and runs them in parallel with subagents (Claude Code Agent/Task tool, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode agents, or separate sessions) using self-contained briefs and explicit file ownership so they never edit the same files, then merges and verifies the results.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Writes or expands a plan work package (`steps/F5.md` style) in the exact shape of the plan’s `agents.md` section 23.6 - the headings in order, tasks with Files, Do and Check, Owner actions, Verification, Done when, Risks and fallbacks - and keeps task ids and section-number references stable so later waves are expanded in one consistent shape. It writes a plan; it does not run a step.

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Detects how the current project is built and worked on (stack, languages, frameworks, package manager, install, dev, build, test, lint, typecheck and format commands, commit style and language, base branch, CI and containers) and keeps it in `.skribly/project.json`, the Skribly project profile every other skill reads first. # Record how a feature is built

> The record-docs skill of agent-skills: writes or updates the as-built documentation of an important feature or decision after it works - what it does, how it is built (the modules, the data, the flow), the decisions and their reasons, how to run and test it, and its limits, in the project documentation folder, so the next person or agent reads one page instead of the code.

`record-docs` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

| Stacks  | general                                                                                                      |
| Release | In development, ships in the next release                                                                    |
| Source  | [skills/record-docs/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/record-docs/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Writes or updates the as-built documentation of an important feature or decision after it works - what it does, how it is built (the modules, the data, the flow), the decisions and their reasons, how to run and test it, and its limits, in the project documentation folder, so the next person or agent reads one page instead of the code. Short, factual, from the code as it is.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “document this feature”
* “write down how this works”
* “record the decisions and how to test it”

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                          |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/record-docs`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$record-docs`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/record-docs` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/record-docs`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/record-docs`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/record-docs` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/record-docs`                                |

Refactors code without changing behaviour, starting with characterization tests that pin down what the code does today, then moving in small verified steps (extract, rename, move, inline, replace conditionals), with tests, types and a diff review after each step and nothing mixed in from feature work.

# Release checklist

> The release skill of agent-skills: walks the project's release checklist (changelogs, dependency updates, contract versioning, registry, vendor sync, tags and releases, the weekly routine) and runs read-only repository checks before a release - develop clean, package.json and VERSION in step, CHANGELOG entry present, tag free.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Walks the project’s release checklist (changelogs, dependency updates, contract versioning, registry, vendor sync, tags and releases, the weekly routine) and runs read-only repository checks before a release - develop clean, `package.json` and VERSION in step, CHANGELOG entry present, tag free. It never tags or publishes; the person who cuts the release does.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “prepare the release”
* “release train 0.3”
* “is this ready to release”
* “run the weekly routine”

Not for bumping a version, merging into main or publishing a package.

# Self-review before commit

> The review skill of agent-skills: reviews your own uncommitted changes or branch diff before committing, looking for bugs, missed edge cases, security slips, dead or debug code, convention breaks and missing tests, and reports findings first, ordered by severity, each with file:line and a concrete fix.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Reviews your own uncommitted changes or branch diff before committing, looking for bugs, missed edge cases, security slips, dead or debug code, convention breaks and missing tests, and reports findings first, ordered by severity, each with file:line and a concrete fix. A pull request mode reviews a whole branch against develop through every gate and writes a draft review that waits for approval. Read-only unless asked to fix.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

* “review my changes”
* “check the diff before I commit”
* “self-review”
* “look over what I changed”
* “anything wrong with this?”
* “review the whole branch”
* “review this pull request”

# Run a work package

> The run-step skill of agent-skills: carries out one plan work package (steps/F5.md style) task by task by the step protocol of the plan's agents.md section 23.3 - read the step, one task at a time in order, a short branch from develop per task, run its check, a Conventional Commit with explicit paths, merge into develop with --no-ff, push, tick the box; main only after the audit.

`run-step` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                        |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Carries out one plan work package (`steps/F5.md` style) task by task by the step protocol of the plan’s `agents.md` section 23.3 - read the step, one task at a time in order, a short branch from develop per task, run its check, a Conventional Commit with explicit paths, merge into develop with –no-ff, push, tick the box; main only after the audit. Owner-only actions are recorded as blocked, never attempted.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

# Vertical slice

> The slice skill of agent-skills: scaffolds a command or query slice, or a whole new module, in an app made from the Skribly app template by deriving it from the app's own reference module at run time (no copied conventions) - plain (input, deps) functions, the input.ts, handler.ts or query.ts, route.ts split, the handler that authorises first and opens one tenant transaction for the organisation it checked, no slice importing another, the outbox for a command, the MCP tool.ts when asked, the seed, and the swap-a-dependency recipe.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Scaffolds a command or query slice, or a whole new module, in an app made from the Skribly app template by deriving it from the app’s own reference module at run time (no copied conventions) - plain (input, deps) functions, the `input.ts`, `handler.ts` or `query.ts`, `route.ts` split, the handler that authorises first and opens one tenant transaction for the organisation it checked, no slice importing another, the outbox for a command, the MCP `tool.ts` when asked, the seed, and the swap-a-dependency recipe.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Writes an implement-ready spec for one task as `.tasks/specs/SPEC-slug.md` - goal, scope in and out, the files and contracts it touches, and phases that each leave the project working and end with an exact check - from a plan task, a tracker issue or a request, then waits for approval. The plan skill hands its tasks here and the task skill works an approved spec phase by phase.

## When to use it

* “how exactly do we build this”

Not for “implementing an approved spec” (the task skill does) or “a Playwright spec”.

# Repository standard

> The standard skill of agent-skills: checks a repository against the Skribly standard and guides the repair.

`standard` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command | `/standard`, `$standard` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Workflow                                                                                               |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                     |
| Source  | [skills/standard/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/standard/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Checks a repository against the Skribly standard and guides the repair. One read-only script runs the checks the repository ships in its own `.tools/` (standard, headers, licences, build output, wording, TODO sync, the source commit of the tools), the per-agent files through the agent-skills CLI, and checks of its own for the uniform npm script names and the git hooks path, then prints one line per check.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “check the standard”
* “is this repository on the standard”
* “bring this repository to the standard”
* “sprawdź standard repozytorium”
* “doprowadź repozytorium do standardu”

# Task workflow

> The task skill of agent-skills: runs a development task end to end, from a tracker issue (Redmine, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Skribly Tracker) or a plain-text request, through analysis, approval, branch, staged implementation and checks to a local commit made only after the user says OK.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Runs a development task end to end, from a tracker issue (Redmine, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Skribly Tracker) or a plain-text request, through analysis, approval, branch, staged implementation and checks to a local commit made only after the user says OK. Keeps a `STATE.md` file under `.tasks/` current so any agent can resume.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

* “start task”
* “take task”
* “resume task”
* “pick up ticket”
* “continue where we left off”
* Also: task extras such as estimate, plan, PR/MR description or tracker comment draft.

# Focused test loop

> The test-loop skill of agent-skills: runs only the checks affected by the current change (lint, types, related tests), fixes failures in a capped loop of at most 3 attempts, and reports compact failure summaries instead of full logs.

`test-loop` is a skill of [agent-skills](/skills/). This page is generated from its `SKILL.md`.

|         |                                                                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command | `/test-loop`, `$test-loop` in Codex                                                                      |
| Group   | Quality and tests                                                                                        |
| Stacks  | general                                                                                                  |
| Release | agent-skills 0.3.0                                                                                       |
| Source  | [skills/test-loop/SKILL.md](https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/test-loop/SKILL.md) |

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Runs only the checks affected by the current change (lint, types, related tests), fixes failures in a capped loop of at most 3 attempts, and reports compact failure summaries instead of full logs. Stops and asks when the same failure repeats, and never edits, skips or weakens tests just to make them pass.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “run the tests”
* “make the checks pass”
* “fix the failing tests”
* “is it green?”

| Gemini CLI     | `/test-loop`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/test-loop`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/test-loop` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/test-loop`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

* `stack.mjs`: `node scripts/stack.mjs [dir] [--json]`

# Draft tracker and review texts

> The tracker-write skill of agent-skills: drafts the texts a developer posts to others, for their approval before anything is sent - a new issue, a comment on an issue (progress, a question, an estimate, a hand-off), a pull or merge request description, a review reply.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Drafts the texts a developer posts to others, for their approval before anything is sent - a new issue, a comment on an issue (progress, a question, an estimate, a hand-off), a pull or merge request description, a review reply. Built from the task files, the diff and the checks, short and in the reader’s language, with nothing posted until the user says so.

# Train the skills for a project

> The train-skills skill of agent-skills: fits the skills to a new project in one loop - runs agent-skills init (stack, commands and conventions into .skribly/project.json, only the skills that fit, for every agent), reads the profile, runs the project's checks once, records the lessons it confirmed with a scope and a file-line or commit citation through the learn skill after the person's OK, and proposes small project-specific skills under .agents/skills with the person's OK.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Moves a project to a new major version of its framework or runtime (Next.js, React, Angular, Laravel, Django, Rails, Spring Boot, Node, PHP, Python) with the target version’s own migration guide, one area at a time, each with a failing test first and a check with the person before the next area.

## When to use it

[Section titled “When to use it”](#when-to-use-it)

Ask for it in your own words, for example:

* “upgrade to Next.js 16”
* “migrate to Laravel 12”
* “move us to Django 5”
* “major version upgrade”
* “follow the migration guide”

Not for routine patch and minor bumps (deps-update).

## How to call it

[Section titled “How to call it”](#how-to-call-it)

| Agent          | Call                                      |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code    | `/upgrade`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `$upgrade`, or pick it from `/skills`     |
| Cursor         | `/upgrade` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `/upgrade`                                |
| OpenCode       | `/upgrade`                                |
| GitHub Copilot | `/upgrade` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `/upgrade`                                |

Every agent also picks the skill by itself when your request matches its description.

## Scripts

[Section titled “Scripts”](#scripts)

None: the skill is instructions only, and the agent runs the project’s own commands.

## Where it fits

[Section titled “Where it fits”](#where-it-fits)

A general skill: it fits every project, so `agent-skills init` always installs it. `agent-skills project disable upgrade` removes it from a project, `project enable upgrade` brings it back. More: [Train the skills for your project](/skills/train/).

# Verify a change in the running app

> The verify skill of agent-skills: proves a change works in the running application, not only in unit tests - starts the project the way it really runs (its own dev or Docker command from the profile), waits until it answers, exercises the changed path with a smoke request or a headless browser, runs lint, types and the related tests, and reports pass or fail per step in a few lines.

## What it does

[Section titled “What it does”](#what-it-does)

Proves a change works in the running application, not only in unit tests - starts the project the way it really runs (its own dev or Docker command from the profile), waits until it answers, exercises the changed path with a smoke request or a headless browser, runs lint, types and the related tests, and reports pass or fail per step in a few lines. Never opens a visible browser and never starts a second copy of an app that already runs.

# Token cost

> How many tokens each agent-skills skill costs an agent: the listing kept in every session, a run, the budget the check enforces and the references read on demand.

Every skill is measured, and every skill has a budget. The numbers are an estimate, characters / 4, the rule of thumb of the [`token-saver`](/skills/skill/token-saver/) skill. They come from the version in development, which ships in the next release; `agent-skills tokens` prints them for the version you have installed.

## The columns

[Section titled “The columns”](#the-columns)

* **Listing**: the name and description. An agent keeps them in context in every session, for every installed skill. `agent-skills init` installs only the skills that fit the project, so a project pays for fewer listings.
* **Run**: `SKILL.md` plus the references it loads by default, read each time the skill runs. What a run writes depends on the task and is not counted; scripts keep their output to a few lines.
* **Budget**: the ceiling of a run. The repository’s check fails when a skill grows past it, so a skill cannot get heavier by accident.
* **On demand**: the other reference files, read only when a step needs them.

All 57 skills together: listings 7480 tokens, runs 52598 tokens, on demand 22771 tokens.
